quote: should be authorised only if the relevant law enforcement authority has completed a fundamental rights impact assessment and, unless provided otherwise in this Regulation, has registered the system in the database
obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital, 'should be authorised only if'); precondition of authorisation
note: Registration in the EU database 'as set out in this Regulation' as a condition of authorised use. Cross-ref Delivery/Design (FRIA, same quote). See Recital (131) on the non-public section for law enforcement.

quote: the law enforcement authority should in such situations request such authorisation while providing the reasons for not having been able to request it earlier, without undue delay and at the latest within 24 hours
if_not_met: If authorisation is rejected, the use 'should cease with immediate effect and all the data related to such use should be discarded and deleted'
note: Urgent use: the authority answers to the judicial or independent administrative authority, giving reasons. Urgent use is restricted to 'the absolute minimum necessary' with safeguards 'as determined in national law'. Cross-ref Decision-making/Design (authorisation gate).

quote: unless provided otherwise in this Regulation, has registered the system in the database as set out in this Regulation
if_not_met: use 'should be authorised only if' registered, unless provided otherwise
note: Registration in the EU database (see recital (131): law enforcement registrations go in a secure non-public section). Also coded Delivery (FRIA).

quote: By 2 August 2025, and once every two years thereafter, Member States shall report to the Commission on the status of the financial and human resources of the national competent authorities, with an assessment of their adequacy.
note: Answer to: the Commission; the Commission transmits the information 'to the Board for discussion and possible recommendations'. No consequence stated.

quote: Where Union institutions, bodies, offices or agencies fall within the scope of this Regulation, the European Data Protection Supervisor shall act as the competent authority for their supervision.
note: EU public bodies answer to the EDPS as supervisor. Consequence: EDPS fines under Art. 100. See also Art. 74(9), coded Decision-making/Design.
basis: AI pass B; different cell in pass A

quote: The data listed in Sections A and B of Annex VIII shall be entered into the EU database by the provider or, where applicable, by the authorised representative.
holder: Provider or, where applicable, the authorised representative
if_not_met: Art. 83(1)(e)-(2): the market surveillance authority requires the provider to end the non-compliance; if it persists, 'appropriate and proportionate measures to restrict or prohibit the high-risk AI system being made available on the market or to ensure that it is recalled or withdrawn'
note: Registration. Contents coded under Annex VIII Sections A and B.

quote: The data listed in Section C of Annex VIII shall be entered into the EU database by the deployer who is, or who acts on behalf of, a public authority, agency or body
holder: Deployer who is, or who acts on behalf of, a public authority, agency or body
if_not_met: not stated in this Article; [inference] deployer obligations under Art. 26 attract fines under Art. 99(4)(e), but Art. 99(8) leaves fines on public authorities to each Member State
note: Registration by public-sector deployers, 'in accordance with Article 49(3) and (4)'. Section C includes a summary of the fundamental rights impact assessment findings (coded under Annex VIII). Answer to: the public (Art. 71(4)), except the non-public section under Art. 49(4).

quote: the information contained in the EU database registered in accordance with Article 49 shall be accessible and publicly available in a user-friendly manner.
note: Publication. Exceptions: the section under Art. 49(4) [inference: secure non-public section for law enforcement, migration, asylum and border control] and Art. 60(4)(c). Testing registrations under Art. 60 are 'accessible only to market surveillance authorities and the Commission' unless the provider consents. 'The information should be easily navigable and machine-readable' (should). Passive; nearest named actor: Commission.

quote: That information shall include the names and contact details of natural persons who are responsible for registering the system and have the legal authority to represent the provider or the deployer, as applicable.
holder: Natural persons responsible for registering the system (for the provider or deployer)
note: Named accountable person in the register. Personal data limited to what is necessary.

quote: Providers of high-risk AI systems placed on the Union market shall report any serious incident to the market surveillance authorities of the Member States where that incident occurred.
holder: Providers of high-risk AI systems placed on the Union market
note: Answer to: market surveillance authority. Deadlines: immediately after a causal link is established or reasonably likely, 'not later than 15 days after the provider or, where applicable, the deployer, becomes aware'; two days for widespread infringement or Art. 3(49)(b) incidents; ten days in case of death (provider 'or the deployer' establishes or suspects the link); an incomplete initial report is allowed. Art. 73(9)-(10): limited to Art. 3(49)(c) incidents for providers under equivalent Union reporting rules and for medical devices.

quote: shall not perform any investigation which involves altering the AI system concerned in a way which may affect any subsequent evaluation of the causes of the incident, prior to informing the competent authorities of such action
note: Answer to: competent authorities and, where relevant, the notified body; the provider 'shall cooperate' during investigations.

quote: They shall also annually report to the Commission about the use of prohibited practices that occurred during that year and about the measures taken.
note: Answer to: the Commission. They also report annually to the Commission and national competition authorities information of potential interest for competition law. Art. 74(1) applies Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 (market surveillance) to AI systems.

quote: market surveillance authorities may exercise the powers referred to in Article 14(4), points (d) and (j), of that Regulation remotely, as appropriate.
note: Remote exercise of powers from another instrument; the powers themselves are not set out here.

quote: Market surveillance activities shall in no way affect the independence of judicial authorities, or otherwise interfere with their activities when acting in their judicial capacity.
note: Limits how far judicial authorities using AI (e.g. Annex III point 8(a)) answer to market surveillance when acting judicially.

quote: the European Data Protection Supervisor shall act as their market surveillance authority, except in relation to the Court of Justice of the European Union acting in its judicial capacity.
note: EU institutions, bodies, offices and agencies within scope answer to the EDPS as market surveillance authority. Also see Decision-making/Design (Art. 70(9)).
basis: AI pass A; different cell in pass B

quote: the market surveillance authorities shall be granted full access by providers to the documentation as well as the training, validation and testing data sets used for the development of high-risk AI systems
holder: Providers of high-risk AI systems (grant access); market surveillance authorities (receive it)
note: Answer to: market surveillance authority. 'where relevant and limited to what is necessary'. Also coded Accountability/Resources (remote access means).

quote: Market surveillance authorities shall be granted access to the source code of the high-risk AI system upon a reasoned request
obligation: statutory duty (access on reasoned request, conditional)
note: Conditions: access 'is necessary to assess the conformity' with Chapter III, Section 2, and 'testing or auditing procedures and verifications based on the data and documentation provided by the provider have been exhausted or proved insufficient'. Confidentiality per Art. 78 (Art. 74(14)).

quote: Where an AI system is based on a general-purpose AI model, and the model and the system are developed by the same provider, the AI Office shall have powers to monitor and supervise compliance of that AI system
note: Providers answer to the AI Office, which has 'all the powers of a market surveillance authority'. [inference] Relevant where a public body deploys an assistant built by the model provider itself.

quote: the AI Office shall have powers to monitor and supervise compliance of that AI system with obligations under this Regulation
note: Trigger: an AI system based on a general-purpose AI model where model and system come from the same provider. The provider answers to the AI Office, which has 'all the powers of a market surveillance authority'.

quote: Market surveillance authorities shall have competences and powers to ensure that testing in real world conditions is in accordance with this Regulation.
note: Within sandboxes, the authorities 'shall verify the compliance with Article 60 as part of their supervisory role' (Art. 76(2)). The authority carries out the check [could also be read as Delivery].

quote: the decision or the objection shall indicate the grounds therefor and how the provider or prospective provider can challenge the decision or objection.
note: Reasons and a challenge route, for providers (not for test subjects).

quote: shall have the power to request and access any documentation created or maintained under this Regulation in accessible language and format
holder: National public authorities or bodies which supervise or enforce Union law protecting fundamental rights
note: Applies 'in relation to the use of high-risk AI systems referred to in Annex III', including the right to non-discrimination, when necessary for their mandates. [inference] Covers documentation held by public-sector deployers. Also coded Coordination/Design (inform market surveillance authority).

quote: respect the confidentiality of information and data obtained in carrying out their tasks and activities
holder: The Commission, market surveillance authorities, notified bodies and any other natural or legal person involved in the application of this Regulation
note: Limits disclosure. Protects intellectual property and trade secrets 'including source code', effective implementation (inspections, investigations, audits), public and national security, criminal or administrative proceedings, classified information. Art. 78(2): authorities request only data 'strictly necessary', protect it and delete it when no longer needed. [inference] Constrains what supervisors can publish about public-sector tools.

quote: Those authorities shall ensure that the market surveillance authorities referred to in Article 74(8) and (9), as applicable, can, upon request, immediately access the documentation or obtain a copy thereof.
holder: Law enforcement, immigration or asylum authorities that are providers of high-risk AI systems in Annex III points 1, 6 or 7
note: Public authorities as providers answer to their market surveillance authority. The technical documentation 'shall remain within the premises of those authorities'; 'Only staff of the market surveillance authority holding the appropriate level of security clearance shall be allowed to access'.

quote: it shall carry out an evaluation of the AI system concerned in respect of its compliance with all the requirements and obligations laid down in this Regulation.
holder: Market surveillance authority of a Member State
if_not_met: corrective action, withdrawal or recall required by the market surveillance authority (Art. 79(2)); provisional measures to prohibit or restrict (Art. 79(5))
note: Operators answer to the market surveillance authority. Trigger: 'sufficient reason to consider an AI system to present a risk' to health, safety or fundamental rights (Art. 79(1)). Compared against: all requirements and obligations of the Regulation. 'Particular attention shall be given to AI systems presenting a risk to vulnerable groups'. 'The relevant operators shall cooperate'. The authority carries out the check [could also be read as Delivery].
basis: AI pass A; different cell in pass B

quote: Where a market surveillance authority has sufficient reason to consider that an AI system classified by the provider as non-high-risk pursuant to Article 6(3) is indeed high-risk, the market surveillance authority shall carry out an evaluation
if_not_met: requirement to bring into compliance (Art. 80(2)); fines (Art. 80(4), (7))
note: Check on the provider's self-classification. Compared against: Art. 6(3) conditions and the Commission guidelines. Metric: not stated. The authority carries out the check [could also be read as Delivery].

quote: does not bring the AI system into compliance with those requirements and obligations within the period referred to in paragraph 2 of this Article, the provider shall be subject to fines in accordance with Article 99.
if_not_met: 'the provider shall be subject to fines in accordance with Article 99'
note: Sanction for failing to correct a misclassified system. Answer to: MSA.

quote: the AI system was misclassified by the provider as non-high-risk in order to circumvent the application of requirements in Chapter III, Section 2, the provider shall be subject to fines in accordance with Article 99
note: Sanction for deliberate misclassification, established by the market surveillance authority during evaluation.

quote: market surveillance authorities may perform appropriate checks, taking into account in particular information stored in the EU database referred to in Article 71 of this Regulation.
note: The register (including Annex VIII Section B non-high-risk claims) is a basis for checks; per Art. 11 Regulation (EU) 2019/1020.
basis: AI pass A; different cell in pass B

quote: Where the market surveillance authority of a Member State makes one of the following findings, it shall require the relevant provider to put an end to the non-compliance concerned, within a period it may prescribe
holder: Market surveillance authority (requires); relevant provider (must end the non-compliance)
if_not_met: 'appropriate and proportionate measures to restrict or prohibit the high-risk AI system being made available on the market or to ensure that it is recalled or withdrawn from the market without delay' (Art. 83(2))
note: Formal findings: CE marking misused or missing; EU declaration of conformity not drawn up or incorrect; '(e) the registration in the EU database referred to in Article 71 has not been carried out'; no authorised representative; technical documentation not available.
basis: AI pass A; different cell in pass B

quote: the relevant market surveillance authority and the national data protection authority should be notified of each use of the real-time biometric identification system.
note: Reporting each use to regulators. Passive; nearest named actor: the law enforcement authority using the system. Trigger: each use.

quote: Market surveillance authorities and the national data protection authorities that have been notified should submit to the Commission an annual report on the use of real-time biometric identification systems.
holder: Market surveillance authorities and the national data protection authorities that have been notified
note: Answer to: the Commission; consequence: not stated. Trigger: annual.

quote: any natural or legal person having grounds to consider that there has been an infringement of the provisions of this Regulation may submit complaints to the relevant market surveillance authority.
holder: Any natural or legal person (complainant); market surveillance authority (receives)
note: Complaint route, 'Without prejudice to other administrative or judicial remedies'. Complaints 'shall be taken into account for the purpose of conducting market surveillance activities' and handled under the authorities' own procedures. [inference] No right to a decision on the complaint is stated.

quote: shall have the right to obtain from the deployer clear and meaningful explanations of the role of the AI system in the decision-making procedure and the main elements of the decision taken.
if_not_met: not stated in this Article; [inference] complaint to the market surveillance authority (Art. 85). Art. 86 is not among the provisions listed for fines in Art. 99(4).
note: Right to explanation. Applies to decisions 'taken by the deployer on the basis of the output from a high-risk AI system listed in Annex III, with the exception of systems listed under point 2', with legal or similarly significant adverse effects on health, safety or fundamental rights. Exceptions from Union or national law (Art. 86(2)); applies only where not otherwise provided under Union law (Art. 86(3)).

quote: Directive (EU) 2019/1937 shall apply to the reporting of infringements of this Regulation and the protection of persons reporting such infringements.
note: Whistleblowing route; points to another instrument. Nearest named actors: persons reporting infringements.

quote: the AI Office may take the necessary actions to monitor the effective implementation and compliance with this Regulation by providers of general-purpose AI models, including their adherence to approved codes of practice.
note: General-purpose model providers answer to the AI Office.

quote: Downstream providers shall have the right to lodge a complaint alleging an infringement of this Regulation.
note: Complaint route against model providers. Must be 'duly reasoned' and state the model provider's contact point, the facts, provisions concerned and reasons. The body receiving it is not named in Art. 89(2) [inference: the AI Office].

quote: The Commission may request the provider of the general-purpose AI model concerned to provide the documentation drawn up by the provider in accordance with Articles 53 and 55, or any additional information
holder: Commission (requests); provider of the general-purpose AI model (supplies)
obligation: statutory power (Commission); statutory duty (provider must supply)
if_not_met: fines under Art. 101 'for supplying incorrect, incomplete or misleading information' (Art. 91(4); Art. 101(1)(b))
note: A structured dialogue may precede (Art. 91(2)); may be triggered by the scientific panel (Art. 91(3)). Request states legal basis, purpose and deadline. Clients 'remain fully responsible if the information supplied is incomplete, incorrect or misleading' (Art. 91(5)).

quote: The provider of the general-purpose AI model concerned, or its representative shall supply the information requested.
holder: Provider of the general-purpose AI model or its representative
note: Answer to: the Commission. 'The clients shall nevertheless remain fully responsible if the information supplied is incomplete, incorrect or misleading.'

quote: The AI Office, after consulting the Board, may conduct evaluations of the general-purpose AI model concerned
note: Purposes: (a) assess compliance where Art. 91 information is insufficient; (b) investigate systemic risks at Union level, especially after a qualified alert. The AI Office carries out the evaluation [could also be read as Delivery]. Metric: not stated (detail by implementing act, Art. 92(6)).
basis: AI pass A; different cell in pass B

quote: the Commission may request access to the general-purpose AI model concerned through APIs or further appropriate technical means and tools, including source code.
holder: Commission (requests access); providers of the general-purpose AI model (provide it)
obligation: statutory power (Commission); statutory duty (provider must give access)
if_not_met: 'the fines provided for in Article 101 for failure to provide access' (Art. 92(4); Art. 101(1)(d))
note: Before requesting access, the AI Office may hold a structured dialogue on 'the internal testing of the model, internal safeguards for preventing systemic risks, and other internal procedures' (Art. 92(7)).

quote: Article 18 of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 shall apply mutatis mutandis to the providers of the general-purpose AI model
note: Challenge route for model providers; points to another instrument whose content is not set out here.

quote: may be revoked at any time by the European Parliament or by the Council. A decision of revocation shall put an end to the delegation of power specified in that decision.
holder: The European Parliament or the Council
if_not_met: revocation of the delegation; objection blocks entry into force (Art. 97(6))
note: The Commission answers to the co-legislators for delegated acts. Report on the delegation nine months before the period ends (97(2)); notify acts to both (97(5)); acts enter into force only without objection within three months (97(6)).

quote: shall enter into force only if no objection has been expressed by either the European Parliament or the Council within a period of three months of notification
holder: Commission (answers to the European Parliament and the Council)
if_not_met: delegated act does not enter into force; delegation may be revoked
note: Answer to: European Parliament and Council. Commission reports on the delegation nine months before the period ends; Parliament or Council may oppose extension or revoke 'at any time' (Art. 97(3)); Commission notifies each act (Art. 97(5)); consults Member State experts before adopting (Art. 97(4)).

quote: Member States shall lay down the rules on penalties and other enforcement measures, which may also include warnings and non-monetary measures, applicable to infringements of this Regulation by operators
note: Sanctions regime. Penalties 'shall be effective, proportionate and dissuasive' and take SMEs into account; Commission guidelines (Art. 96) to be considered. Member States notify the rules to the Commission by the date of application (Art. 99(2)). Fines may be imposed by courts or other bodies depending on the legal system (Art. 99(9)).

quote: Non-compliance with the prohibition of the AI practices referred to in Article 5 shall be subject to administrative fines
if_not_met: administrative fines up to EUR 35 000 000 or, for an undertaking, up to 7% of total worldwide annual turnover, whichever is higher
note: Answer to: the authority imposing fines under national rules. SMEs: the lower of the amount or percentage (Art. 99(6)). Factors (Art. 99(7)) include gravity, number of affected persons, cooperation, whether the operator notified the infringement, intent or negligence, mitigation. Quote stops before the amounts to avoid spacing errors in the figures.

quote: Non-compliance with any of the following provisions related to operators or notified bodies, other than those laid down in Articles 5, shall be subject to administrative fines
holder: Providers, authorised representatives, importers, distributors, deployers, notified bodies
if_not_met: administrative fines up to EUR 15 000 000 or, for an undertaking, up to 3% of total worldwide annual turnover, whichever is higher
note: Listed: (a) providers, Art. 16; (b) authorised representatives, Art. 22; (c) importers, Art. 23; (d) distributors, Art. 24; '(e) obligations of deployers pursuant to Article 26'; (f) notified bodies, Arts. 31, 33(1), (3), (4), 34; (g) transparency for providers and deployers, Art. 50. Art. 27 and Art. 86 are not among the listed provisions.

quote: obligations of deployers pursuant to Article 26
if_not_met: administrative fines up to EUR 15 million or 3% of worldwide annual turnover; for public authorities, subject to member-state rules (Art. 99(8))
note: Deployers' duties are sanctionable. Whether a public-authority deployer can actually be fined depends on Art. 99(8) (Member States) or Art. 100 (Union bodies).

quote: The European Data Protection Supervisor may impose administrative fines on Union institutions, bodies, offices and agencies falling within the scope of this Regulation.
holder: European Data Protection Supervisor (imposes); Union institutions, bodies, offices and agencies (subject)
if_not_met: fines up to EUR 1 500 000 for Art. 5 breaches (Art. 100(2)); up to EUR 750 000 for other requirements or obligations (Art. 100(3))
note: Sanctions for EU public bodies. Factors include gravity, responsibility, mitigation, cooperation, previous infringements, how the infringement became known, 'the annual budget'. Fines go to the Union budget and 'shall not affect the effective operation of the Union institution, body, office or agency fined' (Art. 100(6)).

quote: The exercise of powers under this Article shall be subject to appropriate procedural safeguards in accordance with Union and national law, including effective judicial remedies and due process.
note: Challenge route for fined operators. Nearest named actors: Member States and the bodies imposing fines.

quote: Member States shall, on an annual basis, report to the Commission about the administrative fines they have issued during that year, in accordance with this Article, and about any related litigation or judicial proceedings.
note: Answer to: the Commission; consequence not stated.

quote: The supply of incorrect, incomplete or misleading information to notified bodies or national competent authorities in reply to a request shall be subject to administrative fines
if_not_met: administrative fines up to EUR 7 500 000 or, for an undertaking, up to 1% of total worldwide annual turnover, whichever is higher
note: Answerability for information given to supervisors. Nearest named actors: operators replying to requests.

quote: When deciding whether to impose an administrative fine and when deciding on the amount of the administrative fine in each individual case, all relevant circumstances of the specific situation shall be taken into account
note: Nearest actors: authorities or courts imposing fines (99(9)). Factors include gravity and number affected, prior fines, size, cooperation, degree of responsibility given technical and organisational measures, '(h) ... whether ... the operator notified the infringement', intent or negligence, mitigation.

quote: Each Member State shall lay down rules on to what extent administrative fines may be imposed on public authorities and bodies established in that Member State.
note: Whether public authorities face fines is left to each Member State. Directly governs the consequence for public-sector providers and deployers. Also coded Decision-making/Design.

quote: the European Data Protection Supervisor shall give the Union institution, body, office or agency which is the subject of the proceedings conducted by the European Data Protection Supervisor the opportunity of being heard
note: Due process for EU bodies; decisions based only on elements the parties could comment on; 'Complainants, if any, shall be associated closely with the proceedings'; rights of defence and access to file (Art. 100(5)).

quote: The fines shall not affect the effective operation of the Union institution, body, office or agency fined.
note: Limits the consequence for public bodies. Fines go to the general budget of the Union. Nearest actor: EDPS.

quote: The European Data Protection Supervisor shall, on an annual basis, notify the Commission of the administrative fines it has imposed pursuant to this Article and of any litigation or judicial proceedings it has initiated.
note: Answer to: the Commission; consequence not stated.

quote: The Commission may impose on providers of general-purpose AI models fines
holder: Commission (imposes); providers of general-purpose AI models (subject)
if_not_met: fines not exceeding 3% of annual total worldwide turnover or EUR 15 000 000, whichever is higher
note: Grounds (intentional or negligent): infringing the Regulation; failing an information request or giving incorrect information; failing a requested measure (Art. 93); failing to give access for evaluation (Art. 92). Preliminary findings and right to be heard (Art. 101(2)); information to the Board (Art. 101(4)); procedural implementing acts (Art. 101(6)). Art. 101 applies later than the rest of Chapter XII (Art. 113(b)).

quote: The Court of Justice of the European Union shall have unlimited jurisdiction to review decisions of the Commission fixing a fine under this Article. It may cancel, reduce or increase the fine imposed.
holder: Court of Justice of the European Union
note: Challenge route for model providers; the Commission answers to the Court.

quote: In Annex I to Directive (EU) 2020/1828 of the European Parliament and of the Council (58), the following point is added:
note: Adds the AI Act to the list covered by the Directive on representative actions for the collective interests of consumers (footnote 58). [inference] Opens collective redress by qualified entities for AI Act infringements harming consumers; whether this reaches public-sector use is not stated. Points to another instrument.

quote: The Commission shall assess the need for amendment of the list set out in Annex III and of the list of prohibited AI practices laid down in Article 5, once a year
note: Answer to: European Parliament and Council ('shall submit the findings'). Runs until the end of the delegation period (Art. 97).
basis: AI pass A; different cell in pass B

quote: By 2 August 2028 and every four years thereafter, the Commission shall evaluate and report to the European Parliament and to the Council on the following:
note: Topics: extending or adding Annex III area headings; the Art. 50 transparency list; 'amendments enhancing the effectiveness of the supervision and governance system'. Reports must pay attention to national authorities' resources, penalties applied, standards, and SME market entry (Art. 112(4)). Also: energy-efficiency standardisation report (112(6)); voluntary codes evaluation every three years (112(7)); Commission takes account of Board, Parliament, Council positions (112(9)) and may propose amendments (112(10)).

quote: The report shall include an assessment with regard to the structure of enforcement and the possible need for a Union agency to resolve any identified shortcomings.
note: By 2 August 2029 and every four years; possibly with an amendment proposal; 'The reports shall be made public'. By 2 August 2031, an assessment of enforcement to Parliament, Council and the European Economic and Social Committee (Art. 112(13)).

quote: By 2 August 2028, the Commission shall evaluate the functioning of the AI Office, whether the AI Office has been given sufficient powers and competences to fulfil its tasks
note: Also whether to upgrade the AI Office and its enforcement competences and increase its resources; report to Parliament and Council.

quote: test logs and all test reports dated and signed by the responsible persons
note: Sign-off on testing; to whom the signers answer: not stated.

quote: A statement that the EU declaration of conformity referred to in Article 47 is issued under the sole responsibility of the provider;
if_not_met: formal non-compliance if not drawn up or not drawn up correctly (Art. 83(1)(c)-(d))
note: Sign-off placing responsibility on the provider. The declaration also states conformity with the Regulation and, where personal data is processed, with Regulations (EU) 2016/679 and 2018/1725 and Directive (EU) 2016/680 (point 5).

quote: the name and function of the person who signed it, as well as an indication for, or on behalf of whom, that person signed, a signature.
holder: Person who signs the declaration (for or on behalf of the provider)
note: Named signatory.

quote: The notified body shall carry out periodic audits to make sure that the provider maintains and applies the quality management system and shall provide the provider with an audit report.
note: Ongoing audit. The provider 'shall allow the notified body to access the premises' and share all necessary information (point 5.2). The notified body may carry out additional tests of certified systems.

quote: The following information shall be provided and thereafter kept up to date with regard to high-risk AI systems to be registered in accordance with Article 49(1):
if_not_met: formal non-compliance if registration not carried out (Art. 83(1)(e))
note: Registration. Items include provider details; trade name; intended purpose; 'A basic and concise description of the information used by the system (data, inputs) and its operating logic'; status; certificate; Member States; declaration of conformity; electronic instructions for use, which 'shall not be provided' for Annex III points 1, 6 and 7 systems in law enforcement or migration.

quote: A short summary of the grounds on which the AI system is considered to be not-high-risk in application of the procedure under Article 6(3);
location: p. 136, Annex VIII, Section B, point 7
holder: Providers registering AI systems considered not high-risk under Art. 6(3)
note: Registration of a self-classification, with grounds and the Art. 6(3) condition relied on. Used for checks (Art. 80(8)). Public per Art. 71(4) [inference].

quote: Section C — Information to be submitted by deployers of high-risk AI systems in accordance with Article 49(3)
holder: Deployers of high-risk AI systems registering under Art. 49(3)
note: Registration by public-sector deployers, 'provided and thereafter kept up to date': deployer name and contact details; person submitting; URL of the provider's database entry; FRIA summary (coded separately); 'A summary of the data protection impact assessment' where applicable (Art. 26(8)). Answer to: the public (Art. 71(4)), except the non-public section (Art. 49(4)).

quote: A summary of the findings of the fundamental rights impact assessment conducted in accordance with Article 27;
location: p. 137, Annex VIII, Section C, point 4
holder: Deployers of high-risk AI systems registering under Art. 49(3)
note: Publication of FRIA findings in summary through the EU database. Answer to: the public; consequence not stated.

quote: A summary of the main characteristics of the plan for testing in real world conditions;
holder: Providers or prospective providers conducting testing in real world conditions
note: Registration of testing, kept up to date: identification number; provider and deployers involved; system description and purpose; plan summary; suspension or termination. Visible only to market surveillance authorities and the Commission unless the provider consents (Art. 71(4)).

quote: should provide that documentation to national competent authorities upon request. Such a provider should be obliged to register the AI system in the EU database established under this Regulation.
holder: a provider who considers that an AI system is not high-risk
note: Answers to: national competent authorities (on request); registration in the EU database (see Recital 131). Consequence: not stated here. Cross-ref Delivery/Design (Recital 53).

quote: the difficulty in obtaining meaningful information on the functioning of those systems and the resulting difficulty in challenging their results in court
note: States that the impact of AI tools on suspects' defence rights 'should not be ignored', especially the difficulty of challenging results in court; no mechanism is set out here. Also: AI use by law enforcement 'should not become a factor of inequality, or exclusion'. Nearest named actors: law enforcement and other relevant authorities. To whom: courts (implied [inference]); consequence: not stated.

quote: The impact of the use of AI tools on the defence rights of suspects should not be ignored
note: Names 'the difficulty in challenging their results in court'; gives no mechanism, holder or consequence. Same recital: 'The use of AI tools by law enforcement and other relevant authorities should not become a factor of inequality, or exclusion.' Coded for the challenge question; thin.

quote: It is appropriate that a specific natural or legal person, defined as the provider, takes responsibility for the placing on the market or the putting into service of a high-risk AI system
note: Named responsible role, 'regardless of whether that natural or legal person is the person who designed or developed the system'. To whom: not stated here; consequence: not stated here.

quote: providers established in third countries should, by written mandate, appoint an authorised representative established in the Union.
note: Trigger: 'prior to making their AI systems available in the Union'. The representative plays 'a pivotal role in ensuring the compliance' and serves as contact person. Answers to: authorities (implied); consequence: not stated. Cross-ref Coordination/Design (Recital 82).

quote: any distributor, importer, deployer or other third-party should be considered to be a provider of a high-risk AI system and therefore assume all the relevant obligations.
holder: any distributor, importer, deployer or other third-party
note: Shift of responsibility where the party puts its name or trademark on the system, makes a substantial modification, or changes the intended purpose of a system (including a general-purpose AI system) so that it becomes high-risk. Relevant to public deployers that modify or repurpose systems [inference]. To whom: as for providers.

quote: those operators could act in more than one role at the same time and should therefore fulfil cumulatively all relevant obligations associated with those roles
holder: operators along the value chain (e.g. importers and distributors)
note: Allocation of responsibility by role; would cover a public body acting as both provider and deployer [inference].

quote: It remains necessary to ensure information of workers and their representatives on the planned deployment of high-risk AI systems at the workplace
obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital); describes an information requirement
note: Applies where information or consultation duties under other instruments are not met; 'an information requirement to that effect should be laid down in this Regulation'. Nearest named actors: employers (deployers), including public employers [inference]. Trigger: planned deployment. Consequence: not stated.

quote: should, when they make decisions or assist in making decisions related to natural persons, where applicable, inform the natural persons that they are subject to the use of the high-risk AI system.
holder: Deployers of high-risk AI systems listed in an annex to this Regulation
note: Disclosure to affected persons, including 'the intended purpose and the type of decisions it makes'. For law enforcement, done under Article 13 of Directive (EU) 2016/680. Cross-ref Accountability/Design (right to explanation, Recital 93).

quote: The deployer should also inform the natural persons about their right to an explanation provided under this Regulation.
note: Points affected persons to a challenge or redress route (right to explanation; operative provision appears to be Art. 86 [inference; not in this part]).

quote: After performing that impact assessment, the deployer should notify the relevant market surveillance authority.
note: Answers to: the market surveillance authority; consequence: not stated. Trigger: after completing the FRIA. Cross-ref Delivery/Design (FRIA, Recital 96).

quote: complaint handling and redress procedures, as they could be instrumental in mitigating risks to fundamental rights in concrete use-cases
obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital); example of measures ('could be instrumental')
note: Complaint and redress named as an example of measures the deployer should determine; not a free-standing duty in the recital.

quote: Technical documentation should be prepared and kept up to date by the general-purpose AI model provider for the purpose of making it available, upon request, to the AI Office and the national competent authorities.
obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital, 'should be prepared and kept up to date')
note: Answers to: AI Office and national competent authorities (on request); consequence: not stated. Minimal elements set in annexes.

quote: it is adequate that providers of such models draw up and make publicly available a sufficiently detailed summary of the content used for training the general-purpose AI model.
holder: providers of such models (general-purpose AI models)
note: Publication. The summary should be 'generally comprehensive in its scope instead of technically detailed', e.g. listing main data collections. Recital (104): the open-source exception does not cover this duty. Cross-ref Accountability/Resources (template, Recital 107).

quote: the AI Office should monitor whether the provider has fulfilled those obligations without verifying or proceeding to a work-by-work assessment of the training data in terms of copyright compliance.
note: Oversight of GPAI providers' copyright policy and training summary: providers answer to the AI Office; consequence: not stated here. The scope of the check is limited (no work-by-work assessment).

quote: Upon a reasoned request of a provider whose model has been designated as a general-purpose AI model with systemic risk, the Commission should take the request into account and may decide to reassess
holder: the Commission (on a reasoned request of a provider)
obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital, 'should take the request into account and may decide')
note: Challenge route for designated providers: the Commission answers the request; reassessment is discretionary ('may').

quote: The provider should notify the AI Office at the latest two weeks after the requirements are met or it becomes known that a general-purpose AI model will meet the requirements that lead to the presumption.
holder: The provider (of a general-purpose AI model meeting the threshold)
if_not_met: not stated here (Recital 113: the Commission may designate the model where the provider failed to notify)
note: Reports to: the AI Office. In the notification the provider 'should be able to demonstrate' that the model exceptionally does not present systemic risks. Trigger: threshold met or foreseeably met (can be before training is complete).

quote: the general-purpose AI model provider should without undue delay keep track of the incident and report any relevant information and possible corrective measures to the Commission and national competent authorities.
holder: the general-purpose AI model provider (with systemic risk)
note: Serious-incident reporting. Answers to: the Commission and national competent authorities; consequence: not stated. Trigger: a serious incident caused by development or use of the model.

quote: High-risk AI systems should bear the CE marking to indicate their conformity with this Regulation so that they can move freely within the internal market.
note: Visible sign-off of conformity; a digital CE marking for systems provided only digitally. Member States 'should not create unjustified obstacles' to compliant, CE-marked systems. Nearest named actor: provider.

quote: law enforcement authorities or civil protection authorities may put a specific high-risk AI system into service without the authorisation of the market surveillance authority, provided that such authorisation is requested during or after the use without undue delay.
holder: law enforcement authorities or civil protection authorities
note: Answers to: the market surveillance authority, after the fact. Consequence if authorisation refused: not stated here. Cross-ref Decision-making/Design (same quote).

quote: should be required to register themselves and information about their AI system in an EU database, to be established and managed by the Commission.
holder: providers of high-risk AI systems other than those related to products falling within the scope of relevant existing Union harmonisation legislation, as well as providers who consider that an AI system listed in the high-risk use cases in an annex to this Regulation is not high-risk on the basis of a derogation
note: Registration. 'Any substantial modification of high-risk AI systems should also be registered'. Purpose: to 'increase the transparency towards the public'. Cross-ref Coordination/Design (database, Recital 131).

quote: deployers of high-risk AI systems that are public authorities, agencies or bodies, should register themselves in such database and select the system that they envisage to use.
holder: deployers of high-risk AI systems that are public authorities, agencies or bodies
obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital, 'should register'); mandatory for public-authority deployers, voluntary for other deployers ('entitled to do so voluntarily')
note: Public-sector-specific registration. Trigger: 'Before using an AI system listed in the high-risk use cases in an annex'. To whom: the public, via the database (Commission controller); consequence: not stated. Law enforcement, migration, asylum and border uses go to a non-public section (next entries).

quote: This section of the EU database should be publicly accessible, free of charge, the information should be easily navigable, understandable and machine-readable.
note: Publication of registered information; should be 'user-friendly', with keyword search, and accessible under Directive (EU) 2019/882. Nearest named actor: the Commission (controller of the EU database).

quote: For high-risk AI systems in the area of law enforcement, migration, asylum and border control management, the registration obligations should be fulfilled in a secure non-public section of the EU database.
obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital, 'should be fulfilled'); exception to publication
note: Reduced publicity for public-sector uses in these areas: access 'strictly limited to the Commission as well as to market surveillance authorities with regard to their national section'. Critical infrastructure systems 'should only be registered at national level'. Nearest named actors: providers and public-authority deployers in those areas.

quote: natural persons should be notified that they are interacting with an AI system, unless this is obvious from the point of view of a natural person who is reasonably well-informed, observant and circumspect
note: Disclosure to persons interacting with AI (e.g. public-facing chatbots [inference]), applying whether or not the system is high-risk, 'subject to targeted exceptions to take into account the special need of law enforcement'. Account for vulnerable groups; accessible formats. Nearest named actor: provider [inference; Art. 50 not in this part].

quote: natural persons should be notified when they are exposed to AI systems that, by processing their biometric data, can identify or infer the emotions or intentions of those persons or assign them to specific categories.
note: Disclosure for emotion recognition and biometric categorisation; accessible formats for persons with disabilities. Nearest named actor: deployer [inference].

quote: require providers of those systems to embed technical solutions that enable marking in a machine readable format and detection that the output has been generated or manipulated by an AI system
holder: providers of those systems (systems generating synthetic content)
obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital, 'it is appropriate to require')
note: Machine-readable marking of AI origin (disclosure; also a technical Delivery task). Techniques should be 'sufficiently reliable, interoperable, effective and robust as far as this is technically feasible' (e.g. watermarks, metadata, cryptographic provenance). Excludes systems with 'primarily an assistive function for standard editing'. EDGE CASE: detection lets others, including public bodies, check whether incoming content is AI-generated.
basis: AI pass A; different cell in pass B

quote: should also clearly and distinguishably disclose that the content has been artificially created or manipulated by labelling the AI output accordingly and disclosing its artificial origin.
holder: deployers who use an AI system to generate or manipulate image, audio or video content that appreciably resembles existing persons, objects, places, entities or events and would falsely appear to a person to be authentic or truthful (deep fakes)
note: Labelling of deep fakes. For evidently creative, satirical, artistic or fictional works, disclosure is limited to not hampering the work.

quote: AI-generated or manipulated text to the extent it is published with the purpose of informing the public on matters of public interest unless the AI-generated content has undergone a process of human review or editorial control
obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital); describes a disclosure obligation
note: Disclosure of AI-generated text published to inform the public, unless it has had human review or editorial control 'and a natural or legal person holds editorial responsibility for the publication'. Bears directly on public bodies publishing AI-drafted public information and on human review of AI outputs [inference]. Nearest named actor: deployers.

quote: The supervision of the AI systems in the AI regulatory sandbox should therefore cover their development, training, testing and validation before the systems are placed on the market or put into service
note: Regulatory oversight of sandbox participants, including 'the notion and occurrence of substantial modification that may require a new conformity assessment procedure'. Nearest named actors: national competent authorities. Cross-ref Decision-making/Design (suspension, Recital 139).

quote: Providers and prospective providers in the AI regulatory sandbox should ensure appropriate safeguards and cooperate with the competent authorities, including by following their guidance and acting expeditiously and in good faith to adequately mitigate any identified significant risks
holder: Providers and prospective providers in the AI regulatory sandbox
note: Answers to: competent authorities (follow their guidance); consequence: see Recital (139) (suspension). Mitigation is also a Delivery task.
basis: AI pass A; different cell in pass B

quote: require prospective providers to have a real-world testing plan submitted to competent market surveillance authority, register the testing in dedicated sections in the EU database subject to some limited exceptions
note: Answers to: the market surveillance authority, plus registration. Also time limits on testing and extra safeguards for vulnerable groups.

quote: The national competent authorities should exercise their powers independently, impartially and without bias
note: Conditions on the supervisors; members 'should refrain from any action incompatible with their duties' and are subject to confidentiality rules.
basis: AI pass B; different cell in pass A

quote: providers should also be required to have a system in place to report to the relevant authorities any serious incidents resulting from the use of their AI systems
note: Reports to: relevant authorities; consequence: not stated. Serious incident covers death or serious harm to health, serious and irreversible disruption of critical infrastructure, 'infringements of obligations under Union law intended to protect fundamental rights', or serious damage to property or the environment.

quote: Market surveillance authorities designated pursuant to this Regulation should have all enforcement powers laid down in this Regulation and in Regulation (EU) 2019/1020
holder: Market surveillance authorities designated pursuant to this Regulation
obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital, 'should have'); describes enforcement powers
note: Enforcement over providers and deployers, exercised 'independently, impartially and without bias'; the Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 system applies 'in its entirety'. Market surveillance should not affect supervised entities' independence where Union law requires it.

quote: Due to the specific nature of Union institutions, agencies and bodies falling within the scope of this Regulation, it is appropriate to designate the European Data Protection Supervisor as a competent market surveillance authority for them.
note: EU institutions, agencies and bodies (as providers or deployers) answer to the EDPS as market surveillance authority; consequence: not stated here. Also a Decision-making appointment. 'without prejudice to the designation of national competent authorities by the Member States'.

quote: A specific safeguard procedure should be set for ensuring adequate and timely enforcement against AI systems presenting a risk to health, safety and fundamental rights.
note: Applies to high-risk systems presenting a risk, prohibited systems placed on the market or used in violation, and systems made available in breach of the transparency requirements that present a risk. Nearest named actors: market surveillance authorities.

quote: should be designated, within their respective competences, as competent authorities for the purpose of supervising the implementation of this Regulation
holder: the competent authorities for the supervision and enforcement of Union financial services legal acts
note: Concerns AI provided or used by regulated private financial institutions, so only marginally within the object; 'unless Member States decide to designate another authority'. Recital starts at line 2092 (in part 1 range) and ends at line 2129; coded here. Also limited derogations for credit institutions from QMS and deployer monitoring duties.
basis: AI pass B; different cell in pass A

quote: should have effective investigative and corrective powers, including at least the power to obtain access to all personal data that are being processed and to all information necessary for the performance of its tasks
holder: Each market surveillance authority for high-risk AI systems in the area of biometrics
note: Verb 'should'. Applies where biometric systems are used for law enforcement, migration, asylum and border control management, or the administration of justice and democratic processes, i.e. public-sector uses. Recital adds MSAs 'should be able to exercise their powers by acting with complete independence'. Coded Accountability: users/providers answer to an independent supervisor with investigative and corrective powers; consequence = corrective powers (not specified here). [inference] Operative provision is in the articles on market surveillance (Art. 74, outside this part). The access-to-data element is also a resource for the supervisor.
basis: AI pass B; different cell in pass A

quote: it should provide for the possibility that downstream providers lodge complaints about possible infringements of the rules on providers of general-purpose AI models and systems
note: Complaint route against GPAI model providers, who answer to the AI Office; consequence not stated here. [inference] A public body integrating a GPAI model into its own system would be a downstream provider. Operative Art. 89(2) (outside this part).

quote: through requests to take appropriate measures, including risk mitigation measures in the case of identified systemic risks as well as restricting the making available on the market, withdrawing or recalling the model
holder: AI Office (enforcer); providers of general-purpose AI models (answerable)
note: Providers of GPAI models answer to the AI Office, which 'should be able to investigate possible infringements ... including by requesting documentation and information, by conducting evaluations, as well as by requesting measures'. Consequences: restriction, withdrawal, recall. Providers keep procedural rights under Art. 18 of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020. Also coded Delivery/Resources (independent experts).
basis: AI pass B; different cell in pass A

quote: including by requesting documentation and information, by conducting evaluations, as well as by requesting measures from providers of general-purpose AI models
note: Recital: 'The AI Office should be able to investigate possible infringements in accordance with the powers provided for in this Regulation'. GPAI model providers answer to the AI Office. Safeguard: providers 'should have the procedural rights provided for in Article 18 of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020'. Also coded Decision-making/Design and Accountability/Resources.

quote: Member States should take all necessary measures to ensure that the provisions of this Regulation are implemented, including by laying down effective, proportionate and dissuasive penalties for their infringement
note: Sanctions regime; upper limits on fines to be laid down; fines to weigh nature, gravity, duration and provider size. Operative Art. 99 (outside this part).

quote: The European Data Protection Supervisor should have the power to impose fines on Union institutions, agencies and bodies falling within the scope of this Regulation.
note: Union institutions answer to the EDPS, with fines as consequence. Operative Art. 100 (outside this part).

quote: Compliance with the obligations on providers of general-purpose AI models imposed under this Regulation should be enforceable, inter alia, by means of fines.
holder: providers of general-purpose AI models (liable); the Commission (enforces)
if_not_met: fines (amounts not given in this recital)
note: Includes failure to comply with measures requested by the Commission; subject to limitation periods. Also coded Accountability/Design (CJEU review).

quote: All decisions taken by the Commission under this Regulation are subject to review by the Court of Justice of the European Union in accordance with the TFEU
holder: the Commission (answers to the Court of Justice of the European Union)
note: Challenge route against Commission decisions, incl. unlimited jurisdiction on penalties under Art. 261 TFEU.

quote: any natural or legal person that has grounds to consider that there has been an infringement of this Regulation should be entitled to lodge a complaint to the relevant market surveillance authority
holder: any natural or legal person (complainant); the relevant market surveillance authority (receives)
note: Complaint route, without prejudice to existing Union and national remedies. Consequence of complaint not stated here. Operative Art. 85 (outside this part).

quote: Persons acting as whistleblowers on the infringements of this Regulation should be protected under the Union law.
note: Points to Directive (EU) 2019/1937 for reporting infringements and protecting reporters. Operative Art. 87 (outside this part).

quote: the Commission should evaluate and review this Regulation by 2 August 2029 and every four years thereafter and report to the European Parliament and the Council
holder: the Commission (reports to the European Parliament and the Council)
note: Also by 2 August 2028 and every four years: high-risk area headings, transparency scope, effectiveness of supervision and governance, energy-efficiency standardisation; by 2 August 2028 and every three years: voluntary codes of conduct. Operative provision outside this part.

quote: Member States should lay down and notify to the Commission the rules on penalties, including administrative fines
note: Sanctions to be in place and 'properly and effectively implemented by the date of application'. Notification to the Commission is also a Coordination link. Operative provision Art. 99(1)-(2) (outside this part).

quote: as regards AI systems put into service or used by Union institutions, agencies, offices and bodies, references to national competent authorities or market surveillance authorities in this Regulation shall be construed as references to the European Data Protection Supervisor
holder: Union institutions, agencies, offices and bodies (answerable); the European Data Protection Supervisor (forum)
if_not_met: not stated here; EDPS may fine Union bodies (Art. 100, outside this part; see recital 168)
note: EU institutions using or putting AI into service answer to the EDPS in its capacity as market surveillance/competent authority. Also coded Decision-making/Design (same passage).

quote: has registered the system in the EU database according to Article 49. However, in duly justified cases of urgency, the use of such systems may be commenced without the registration in the EU database
if_not_met: use is not to be authorised ('shall be authorised only if')
note: In urgency, registration must be 'completed without undue delay'. Registration for law enforcement is in a non-public section (Art. 49(4)).

quote: each use of a ‘real-time’ remote biometric identification system in publicly accessible spaces for law enforcement purposes shall be notified to the relevant market surveillance authority and the national data protection authority
note: Passive; nearest actor: law enforcement authority using the system. Answers to MSA and national DPA; consequence not stated. Per national rules (Art. 5(5)); minimum content as in Art. 5(6); excludes sensitive operational data.

quote: shall submit to the Commission annual reports on such use
holder: National market surveillance authorities and the national data protection authorities of Member States that have been notified
note: Annual reporting to the Commission on real-time RBI use for law enforcement. Consequence not stated. Also coded Accountability/Resources (template).

quote: The Commission shall publish annual reports on the use of real-time remote biometric identification systems in publicly accessible spaces for law enforcement purposes, based on aggregated data in Member States
note: Publication; reports exclude sensitive operational data.

quote: Upon request of national competent authorities, the provider shall provide the documentation of the assessment.
if_not_met: Not stated here; incorrect, incomplete or misleading information in reply to a request: fines up to EUR 7 500 000 or 1% (Art. 99(5), outside this part).
note: Provider answers to national competent authorities for its non-high-risk classification.

quote: to provide national competent authorities and notified bodies with the necessary information in a clear and comprehensive form to assess the compliance of the AI system with those requirements
if_not_met: Not stated here; 'technical documentation is not available' is a formal non-compliance: MSA requires the provider to end it, and if it persists restricts, prohibits, recalls or withdraws the system (Art. 83, outside this part).
note: The documentation lets the provider answer to NCAs and notified bodies. Also coded Delivery/Design.

quote: Recipient national authorities and Union institutions, bodies, offices and agencies making use of such outputs in the Union remain accountable to ensure their use complies with Union law.
holder: Recipient national authorities and Union institutions, bodies, offices and agencies making use of such outputs in the Union
note: Applies to public bodies in the Union that use outputs of AI systems run by excluded third-country authorities or international organisations. To whom they answer: not stated; consequence: not stated.

quote: their name, registered trade name or registered trade mark, the address at which they can be contacted
if_not_met: Not stated here. Art. 99(4)(a) (outside this part): fines up to EUR 15 000 000 or 3%.
note: Identifies the responsible provider on the system, packaging or documentation; also a contact point (Coordination).

quote: upon a reasoned request of a national competent authority, demonstrate the conformity of the high-risk AI system with the requirements set out in Section 2
if_not_met: Not stated here. Art. 99(4)(a) (outside this part): fines up to EUR 15 000 000 or 3%; incorrect information in reply: up to EUR 7 500 000 or 1% (Art. 99(5)).
note: Provider answers to NCAs. See Art. 21.

quote: an accountability framework setting out the responsibilities of the management and other staff with regard to all the aspects listed in this paragraph.
if_not_met: Not stated here. Art. 16(c) breach: Art. 99(4)(a) (outside this part).
note: Internal named responsibilities within the provider; to whom they answer and with what consequence: not stated.

quote: The provider shall, for a period ending 10 years after the high-risk AI system has been placed on the market or put into service, keep at the disposal of the national competent authorities:
if_not_met: Not stated here. Art. 16(d) breach: fines up to EUR 15 000 000 or 3% (Art. 99(4)(a)); unavailable technical documentation is formal non-compliance (Art. 83(1)(g)) (both outside this part).
note: Items: technical documentation, QMS documentation, changes approved by notified bodies, notified body decisions, EU declaration. Financial institutions keep it within sectoral documentation (18(3)).

quote: Each Member State shall determine conditions under which the documentation referred to in paragraph 1 remains at the disposal of the national competent authorities
note: Covers a provider or authorised representative that goes bankrupt or ceases activity before the 10-year period ends.
basis: AI pass A; different cell in pass B

quote: inform the market surveillance authorities competent for the high-risk AI system concerned and, where applicable, the notified body that issued a certificate for that high-risk AI system
if_not_met: Not stated here. Art. 16(j) breach: Art. 99(4)(a) (outside this part).
note: Report covers 'the nature of the non-compliance and of any relevant corrective action taken'. Answers to MSAs and notified body; consequence not stated here.

quote: it shall immediately investigate the causes, in collaboration with the reporting deployer, where applicable, and inform the market surveillance authorities competent for the high-risk AI system concerned
if_not_met: not stated here; Art. 99(4)(a) (outside this part) via Art. 16(j)
note: Reports to the competent MSA and, where applicable, the notified body that issued the certificate, 'in particular, of the nature of the non-compliance and of any relevant corrective action taken'. Consequence not stated here. Also coded Delivery/Design.

quote: Providers of high-risk AI systems shall, upon a reasoned request by a competent authority, provide that authority all the information and documentation necessary to demonstrate the conformity of the high-risk AI system
if_not_met: Not stated here. Incorrect, incomplete or misleading information in reply to a request: fines up to EUR 7 500 000 or 1% (Art. 99(5), outside this part); 16(k) breach under Art. 99(4)(a).
note: In an official EU language indicated by the Member State. 21(2): give access to automatically generated logs under their control. Information treated confidentially (Art. 78, 21(3)).

quote: Prior to making their high-risk AI systems available on the Union market, providers established in third countries shall, by written mandate, appoint an authorised representative which is established in the Union.
if_not_met: Not stated here; 'no authorised representative has been appointed' is formal non-compliance under Art. 83(1)(f) (outside this part): MSA requires remedy, then restricts, prohibits, recalls or withdraws.
note: Creates a named accountable party in the EU; provider must enable it to perform the mandate (22(2)).
basis: AI pass A; different cell in pass B

quote: The mandate shall empower the authorised representative to be addressed, in addition to or instead of the provider, by the competent authorities, on all issues related to ensuring compliance with this Regulation.
if_not_met: Not stated here. Art. 99(4)(b) (outside this part).
note: Answerable party in the Union to competent authorities. Must provide a copy of the mandate to MSAs on request; keep contact details, declaration, technical documentation and certificate for 10 years (22(3)(b)); provide information and logs on reasoned request (c); cooperate to reduce and mitigate risks (d); registration under Art. 49(1) or check its correctness (e).
basis: AI pass B; different cell in pass A

quote: provide a competent authority, upon a reasoned request, with all the information and documentation, including that referred to in point (b) of this subparagraph, necessary to demonstrate the conformity of a high-risk AI system
if_not_met: Not stated here. Art. 99(4)(b) (outside this part): fines up to EUR 15 000 000 or 3%.
note: (b) keep provider contact details, EU declaration, technical documentation and certificate for 10 years; (c) incl. log access; (d) cooperate to reduce and mitigate risks; (e) registration under Art. 49(1) or check registration data. Provides copy of mandate to MSAs on request.

quote: it shall immediately inform the relevant market surveillance authority, as well as, where applicable, the relevant notified body, about the termination of the mandate and the reasons therefor
if_not_met: Not stated here. Art. 99(4)(b) (outside this part).
note: Trigger: representative 'shall terminate the mandate if it considers or has reason to consider the provider to be acting contrary to its obligations'. Reports the provider to the MSA.

quote: The authorised representative shall terminate the mandate if it considers or has reason to consider the provider to be acting contrary to its obligations pursuant to this Regulation.
if_not_met: not stated here; Art. 99(4)(b) (outside this part)
note: Must then 'immediately inform the relevant market surveillance authority, as well as, where applicable, the relevant notified body, about the termination of the mandate and the reasons therefor'. A check on the provider with reporting to the regulator.

quote: Importers shall provide the relevant competent authorities, upon a reasoned request, with all the necessary information and documentation, including that referred to in paragraph 5, to demonstrate the conformity of a high-risk AI system
if_not_met: Not stated here. Art. 99(4)(c) (outside this part); incorrect information: Art. 99(5).
note: 23(3): name and contact on system/packaging; 23(4): storage/transport not to jeopardise compliance; 23(5): keep certificate, instructions, EU declaration 10 years; 23(7): cooperate to reduce and mitigate risks.

quote: Upon a reasoned request from a relevant competent authority, distributors of a high-risk AI system shall provide that authority with all the information and documentation regarding their actions pursuant to paragraphs 1 to 4
holder: distributors of a high-risk AI system
if_not_met: Not stated here. Art. 99(4)(d) (outside this part); incorrect information: Art. 99(5).
note: 24(6): cooperate with competent authorities to reduce or mitigate risk.

quote: Any distributor, importer, deployer or other third-party shall be considered to be a provider of a high-risk AI system for the purposes of this Regulation and shall be subject to the obligations of the provider under Article 16
holder: Any distributor, importer, deployer or other third-party
if_not_met: Not stated here. As provider, breach of Art. 16: fines up to EUR 15 000 000 or 3% (Art. 99(4)(a), outside this part); national public authorities as each Member State lays down (Art. 99(8)).
note: When they (a) put their name or trademark on a high-risk system; (b) make a substantial modification; (c) modify the intended purpose of a non-high-risk AI system, incl. a general-purpose AI system, so it becomes high-risk. [inference] A public body that repurposes a general-purpose AI system for an Annex III use becomes its provider. Initial provider then ceases to be provider (25(2)). 25(3): product manufacturers as providers for Annex I safety components.

quote: Where deployers have identified a serious incident, they shall also immediately inform first the provider, and then the importer or distributor and the relevant market surveillance authorities of that incident.
if_not_met: Not stated here. Art. 99(4)(e) (outside this part).
note: If provider unreachable, Art. 73 applies mutatis mutandis. Excludes sensitive operational data of law enforcement deployers. Serious incident defined in Art. 3(49), incl. infringement of obligations protecting fundamental rights.

quote: Before putting into service or using a high-risk AI system at the workplace, deployers who are employers shall inform workers’ representatives and the affected workers that they will be subject to the use of the high-risk AI system.
if_not_met: Not stated here. Art. 99(4)(e) (outside this part).
note: Disclosure to affected workers before use, per Union and national rules on informing workers. [inference] Covers public bodies as employers.

quote: Deployers of high-risk AI systems that are public authorities, or Union institutions, bodies, offices or agencies shall comply with the registration obligations referred to in Article 49.
holder: Deployers of high-risk AI systems that are public authorities, or Union institutions, bodies, offices or agencies
if_not_met: Not stated here. Art. 99(4)(e) (outside this part): fines up to EUR 15 000 000 or 3%; national public authorities only as each Member State lays down (Art. 99(8)); Union bodies up to EUR 750 000 (Art. 100(3)).
note: Registration of public-sector use (Art. 49(3)) in the EU database; non-public section for law enforcement, migration, asylum, border (Art. 49(4)). Also coded Decision-making/Design.

quote: each use of such high-risk AI systems shall be documented in the relevant police file and shall be made available to the relevant market surveillance authority and the national data protection authority upon request
if_not_met: Not stated here. Art. 99(4)(e) (outside this part).
note: 'Regardless of the purpose or deployer'; nearest actor: the deployer. Answers to MSA and DPA on request; excludes sensitive operational data.

quote: Deployers shall submit annual reports to the relevant market surveillance and national data protection authorities on their use of post-remote biometric identification systems
if_not_met: Not stated here. Art. 99(4)(e) (outside this part).
note: Excludes sensitive operational data; reports may be aggregated across deployments. Consequence not stated.

quote: deployers of high-risk AI systems referred to in Annex III that make decisions or assist in making decisions related to natural persons shall inform the natural persons that they are subject to the use of the high-risk AI system
holder: deployers of high-risk AI systems referred to in Annex III that make decisions or assist in making decisions related to natural persons
if_not_met: Not stated here. Art. 99(4)(e) (outside this part).
note: Disclosure to affected persons, e.g. users of public services [inference]. For law enforcement, Art. 13 Directive (EU) 2016/680 applies. Without prejudice to Art. 50.

quote: Deployers shall cooperate with the relevant competent authorities in any action those authorities take in relation to the high-risk AI system in order to implement this Regulation.
if_not_met: Not stated here. Art. 99(4)(e) (outside this part).
note: Deployers answer to competent authorities.

quote: the measures to be taken in the case of the materialisation of those risks, including the arrangements for internal governance and complaint mechanisms.
holder: deployers that are bodies governed by public law, or are private entities providing public services, and deployers of high-risk AI systems referred to in points 5 (b) and (c) of Annex III
if_not_met: Not stated here; Art. 27 is not listed in Art. 99(4) (outside this part).
note: The FRIA must set out internal governance and complaint arrangements; their content is left to the deployer.

quote: the deployer shall notify the market surveillance authority of its results, submitting the filled-out template referred to in paragraph 5 of this Article as part of the notification
if_not_met: Not stated here; Art. 27 is not listed in Art. 99(4) (outside this part); Union bodies up to EUR 750 000 (Art. 100(3)).
note: Answers to the MSA; consequence not stated. [inference] Notification to the regulator, not publication. Deployers may be exempt in the Art. 46(1) derogation case.

quote: Notified bodies shall take out appropriate liability insurance for their conformity assessment activities
if_not_met: Not stated here. Art. 99(4)(f) (outside this part).
note: Consequence-bearing mechanism for the checker's errors, unless liability is assumed by the Member State or the Member State is itself directly responsible.

quote: Notified bodies shall take full responsibility for the tasks performed by any subcontractors or subsidiaries.
if_not_met: Not stated here. Art. 99(4)(f) (outside this part) covers Art. 33(1), (3), (4).
note: 33(1): ensure subcontractor/subsidiary meets Art. 31 and inform notifying authority; 33(4): keep qualification and work documents for the notifying authority for five years.

quote: Notified bodies shall make a list of their subsidiaries publicly available.
if_not_met: Not stated here. Art. 99(4)(f) (outside this part).
note: Publication.

quote: Notified bodies shall make available and submit upon request all relevant documentation, including the providers’ documentation, to the notifying authority referred to in Article 28
if_not_met: Not stated here. Art. 99(4)(f) (outside this part).
note: Lets the notifying authority conduct assessment, designation, notification and monitoring.

quote: it shall restrict, suspend or withdraw the designation as appropriate, depending on the seriousness of the failure to meet those requirements or fulfil those obligations
note: Trigger: sufficient reason to consider the notified body no longer meets Art. 31 or fails its obligations; investigate 'with the utmost diligence', hear the body, inform Commission and Member States. Notified bodies answer to the notifying authority; consequence: loss of designation. 36(5): notified body informs providers within 10 days; 36(6): files kept and made available to other authorities.

quote: If the notifying authority comes to the conclusion that the notified body no longer meets the requirements laid down in Article 31 or that it is failing to fulfil its obligations, it shall restrict, suspend or withdraw the designation
holder: the notifying authority (holds the notified body to account)
if_not_met: restriction, suspension or withdrawal of the designation (as quoted)
note: Notified bodies answer to the notifying authority. Trigger: 'sufficient reason to consider' non-compliance; authority 'shall without delay investigate the matter with the utmost diligence', inform the body of objections and 'give it the possibility to make its views known'; sanction depends on seriousness; Commission and other Member States informed immediately. Also bears on Decision-making (stopping a checker).

quote: submit a report on its findings to the Commission and the other Member States within three months of having notified the changes to the designation
note: Notifying authority reports to Commission and Member States; consequence not stated.

quote: The Commission shall, where necessary, investigate all cases where there are reasons to doubt the competence of a notified body or the continued fulfilment by a notified body of the requirements laid down in Article 31
note: Commission oversight of notified bodies; notifying authority provides information on request (37(2)); confidentiality (37(3)). Consequence: Art. 37(4).

quote: they shall duly justify that they have adopted technical solutions that meet the requirements referred to in Section 2 of this Chapter
holder: providers of high-risk AI systems or general-purpose AI models
note: Applies where they do not comply with common specifications; solutions must reach 'a level at least equivalent'. To whom the justification is given: not stated.
