quote: Where providers of high-risk AI systems or general-purpose AI models do not comply with the common specifications referred to in paragraph 1, they shall duly justify that they have adopted technical solutions that meet the requirements
holder: providers of high-risk AI systems or general-purpose AI models
note: Comply-or-justify: equivalent level of protection required. To whom the justification is given is not stated.

quote: An appeal procedure against decisions of the notified bodies, including on conformity certificates issued, shall be available.
note: Challenge route against notified-body decisions; who runs it, who may appeal, and consequence: not stated.

quote: Notified bodies shall inform the notifying authority of the following:
if_not_met: Not stated here. Notified-body obligations under Art. 31, 33, 34 are fined under Art. 99(4)(f); Art. 45 not listed there (outside this part).
note: Items: certificates and QMS approvals issued; refusals, restrictions, suspensions, withdrawals; circumstances affecting notification; MSA requests for information; on request, activities incl. cross-border and subcontracting.

quote: any refusal, restriction, suspension or withdrawal of a Union technical documentation assessment certificate or a quality management system approval issued in accordance with the requirements of Annex VII
note: Reporting to the notifying authority: certificates and approvals issued (a); refusals, restrictions, suspensions, withdrawals (b); circumstances affecting notification (c); information requests from MSAs (d); on request, activities performed incl. cross-border and subcontracting (e).

quote: By drawing up the EU declaration of conformity, the provider shall assume responsibility for compliance with the requirements set out in Section 2.
if_not_met: Not stated here. Missing or incorrect EU declaration is formal non-compliance (Art. 83(1)(c)-(d)): MSA requires remedy, then restricts, prohibits, recalls or withdraws; Art. 16(g) breach fined under Art. 99(4)(a) (both outside this part).
note: Provider sign-off. 47(1): written, machine-readable, physical or e-signed declaration per system, kept 10 years for NCAs, copy on request; 47(2): content per Annex V, translated; 47(3): single declaration across Union law; kept up to date.

quote: The CE marking shall be affixed visibly, legibly and indelibly for high-risk AI systems.
if_not_met: Not stated here. CE marking not affixed or affixed in violation is formal non-compliance (Art. 83(1)(a)-(b), outside this part); Art. 16(h) breach fined under Art. 99(4)(a).
note: Public sign of conformity. Digital CE marking for digital systems (48(2)); followed by notified body identification number where applicable, incl. in promotional material (48(4)).

quote: the provider or, where applicable, the authorised representative shall register themselves and their system in the EU database referred to in Article 71.
holder: the provider or, where applicable, the authorised representative
if_not_met: Not stated here. Failure to register is formal non-compliance (Art. 83(1)(e), outside this part); Art. 16(i) breach fined under Art. 99(4)(a). Public-sector deployers may not use an unregistered system (Art. 26(8)).
note: Trigger: before placing on market or putting into service an Annex III high-risk system (except point 2).

quote: an AI system for which the provider has concluded that it is not high-risk according to Article 6(3), that provider or, where applicable, the authorised representative shall register themselves and that system in the EU database
holder: that provider or, where applicable, the authorised representative
if_not_met: Not stated here. Failure to register: Art. 83(1)(e) (outside this part).
note: Makes the provider's self-classification as not high-risk (Art. 6(3)-(4)) visible.

quote: deployers that are public authorities, Union institutions, bodies, offices or agencies or persons acting on their behalf shall register themselves, select the system and register its use in the EU database referred to in Article 71.
holder: deployers that are public authorities, Union institutions, bodies, offices or agencies or persons acting on their behalf
if_not_met: Not stated here. Required by Art. 26(8); breach of Art. 26 fined up to EUR 15 000 000 or 3% (Art. 99(4)(e), outside this part); national public authorities only as each Member State lays down (Art. 99(8)); Union bodies up to EUR 750 000 (Art. 100(3)).
note: Trigger: before putting into service or using an Annex III high-risk system (except point 2). Registration of public-sector use; see 49(4) for non-public section.

quote: the registration referred to in paragraphs 1, 2 and 3 of this Article shall be in a secure non-public section of the EU database referred to in Article 71
note: For Annex III points 1, 6 and 7 in law enforcement, migration, asylum and border control management; limited information; 'Only the Commission and national authorities referred to in Article 74(8) shall have access'. Limits publication for these public-sector uses.

quote: High-risk AI systems referred to in point 2 of Annex III shall be registered at national level.
note: Point 2 of Annex III (content outside this part) is excluded from EU-database registration in 49(1) and 49(3); who registers and where nationally: not stated.

quote: Providers shall ensure that AI systems intended to interact directly with natural persons are designed and developed in such a way that the natural persons concerned are informed that they are interacting with an AI system
if_not_met: Not stated here. Art. 99(4)(g) (outside this part): fines up to EUR 15 000 000 or 3%; national public authorities as each Member State lays down (Art. 99(8)); Union bodies up to EUR 750 000 (Art. 100(3)).
note: Disclosure to people interacting with AI (e.g. public-service chatbots [inference]). Unless obvious to a reasonably well-informed person. Not for systems authorised by law for criminal offences, unless available for the public to report a criminal offence. Information given at first interaction, accessibly (50(5)). Applies to all such systems, not only high-risk.

quote: shall ensure that the outputs of the AI system are marked in a machine-readable format and detectable as artificially generated or manipulated
holder: Providers of AI systems, including general-purpose AI systems, generating synthetic audio, image, video or text content
obligation: statutory duty ('as far as this is technically feasible')
if_not_met: Not stated here. Art. 99(4)(g) (outside this part): fines up to EUR 15 000 000 or 3%.
note: Edge case: marking also lets public bodies detect AI-generated content submitted to them by others. Technical solutions effective, interoperable, robust, reliable. Not for assistive standard editing, where input not substantially altered, or law-enforcement authorised uses. Could also be read as Delivery (technical marking).

quote: Deployers of an emotion recognition system or a biometric categorisation system shall inform the natural persons exposed thereto of the operation of the system
holder: Deployers of an emotion recognition system or a biometric categorisation system
if_not_met: Not stated here. Art. 99(4)(g) (outside this part).
note: Also process personal data per GDPR, EUDPR, LED. Not for systems permitted by law to detect, prevent or investigate criminal offences, with safeguards.

quote: Deployers of an AI system that generates or manipulates image, audio or video content constituting a deep fake, shall disclose that the content has been artificially generated or manipulated.
holder: Deployers of an AI system that generates or manipulates image, audio or video content constituting a deep fake
if_not_met: Not stated here. Art. 99(4)(g) (outside this part).
note: Not where authorised by law for criminal offences; for evidently artistic, creative, satirical or fictional works, limited to disclosure that does not hamper the work.

quote: Deployers of an AI system that generates or manipulates text which is published with the purpose of informing the public on matters of public interest shall disclose that the text has been artificially generated or manipulated.
holder: Deployers of an AI system that generates or manipulates text which is published with the purpose of informing the public on matters of public interest
obligation: statutory duty (exempt after human review with editorial responsibility)
if_not_met: Not stated here. Art. 99(4)(g) (outside this part).
note: Exempt where 'the AI-generated content has undergone a process of human review or editorial control and where a natural or legal person holds editorial responsibility', or law-enforcement authorised use. [inference] Relevant to public bodies publishing AI-drafted public information.

quote: the relevant provider shall notify the Commission without delay and in any event within two weeks after that requirement is met or it becomes known that it will be met
if_not_met: 'If the Commission becomes aware of a general-purpose AI model presenting systemic risks of which it has not been notified, it may decide to designate it as a model with systemic risk.' Fines for GPAI providers under Art. 101 (outside this part; see Recital 169).
note: Notification includes information demonstrating the threshold is met. Provider may argue the model exceptionally does not present systemic risks (52(2)); Commission rejects insufficiently substantiated arguments (52(3)).

quote: the Commission shall take the request into account and may decide to reassess whether the general-purpose AI model can still be considered to present systemic risks
holder: the Commission (on reasoned request of the designated provider)
note: Challenge route for providers: request must contain 'objective, detailed and new reasons'; earliest six months after designation and after any decision maintaining it.

quote: Upon a reasoned request of a provider whose model has been designated as a general-purpose AI model with systemic risk pursuant to paragraph 4, the Commission shall take the request into account and may decide to reassess
holder: a provider whose model has been designated (requests); the Commission (reassesses)
obligation: statutory right of request; Commission duty to take into account
note: Challenge route against designation. Request must contain 'objective, detailed and new reasons'; earliest six months after designation, and six months after any decision to maintain it.

quote: The Commission shall ensure that a list of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk is published and shall keep that list up to date
note: Publication, without prejudice to IP, confidential business information and trade secrets.

quote: draw up and keep up-to-date the technical documentation of the model, including its training and testing process and the results of its evaluation
if_not_met: Not stated here. Recital 169: GPAI provider obligations enforceable by fines (Art. 101, outside this part; amounts not checked).
note: Minimum content Annex XI, 'for the purpose of providing it, upon request, to the AI Office and the national competent authorities'. Also a recording (Delivery) duty. Not for open-source models without systemic risk (53(2)).
basis: AI pass A; different cell in pass B

quote: draw up and make publicly available a sufficiently detailed summary about the content used for training of the general-purpose AI model, according to a template provided by the AI Office
if_not_met: Not stated here. Fines under Art. 101 (outside this part; see Recital 169).
note: Publication; applies also to open-source models. Also coded Accountability/Resources (template).

quote: Providers of general-purpose AI models shall cooperate as necessary with the Commission and the national competent authorities in the exercise of their competences and powers pursuant to this Regulation.
if_not_met: Not stated here. Fines under Art. 101 (outside this part; see Recital 169).
note: Information obtained is treated confidentially (53(7), Art. 78).

quote: Providers of general-purpose AI models who do not adhere to an approved code of practice or do not comply with a European harmonised standard shall demonstrate alternative adequate means of compliance for assessment by the Commission.
if_not_met: Not stated here. Fines under Art. 101 (outside this part; see Recital 169).
note: Codes of practice may be relied on until a harmonised standard is published; harmonised standards give presumption of conformity. Assessed by the Commission.

quote: Prior to placing a general-purpose AI model on the Union market, providers established in third countries shall, by written mandate, appoint an authorised representative which is established in the Union.
holder: providers established in third countries (of general-purpose AI models)
if_not_met: Not stated here. Fines under Art. 101 (outside this part; see Recital 169).
note: Representative keeps Annex XI documentation 10 years for AI Office and NCAs, provides information on request, cooperates, and can be addressed instead of the provider (54(3)-(4)). Not for open-source models unless systemic risk (54(6)).
basis: AI pass A; different cell in pass B

quote: The mandate shall empower the authorised representative to be addressed, in addition to or instead of the provider, by the AI Office or the competent authorities, on all issues related to ensuring compliance with this Regulation.
holder: the authorised representative (of a GPAI model provider)
note: Answerable party in the EU. Tasks (54(3)): verify Annex XI documentation and Art. 53/55 obligations fulfilled (a Delivery check); keep documentation 10 years; provide AI Office information on reasoned request; cooperate 'including when the model is integrated into AI systems placed on the market or put into service in the Union'. 54(5): terminate mandate if provider acts contrary to obligations and 'immediately inform the AI Office'.

quote: In such a case, it shall also immediately inform the AI Office about the termination of the mandate and the reasons therefor.
note: Trigger: representative 'shall terminate the mandate if it considers or has reason to consider the provider to be acting contrary to its obligations'. Reports the model provider to the AI Office.

quote: keep track of, document, and report, without undue delay, to the AI Office and, as appropriate, to national competent authorities, relevant information about serious incidents and possible corrective measures to address them
holder: providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk
if_not_met: Not stated here. Fines under Art. 101 (outside this part; see Recital 169).
note: Answers to AI Office and, as appropriate, NCAs; consequence not stated here.

quote: Providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risks who do not adhere to an approved code of practice or do not comply with a European harmonised standard shall demonstrate alternative adequate means of compliance for assessment by the Commission.
holder: Providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risks
if_not_met: Not stated here. Fines under Art. 101 (outside this part; see Recital 169).
note: Codes of practice may be relied on until a harmonised standard is published. 55(3): confidentiality (Art. 78).

quote: The AI Office shall aim to ensure that participants to the codes of practice report regularly to the AI Office on the implementation of the commitments and the measures taken and their outcomes
holder: The AI Office (aims to ensure); participants to the codes of practice (report)
note: Including against KPIs; reporting reflects differences in size and capacity.

quote: They shall publish their assessment of the adequacy of the codes of practice.
holder: The AI Office and the Board
note: They also 'shall regularly monitor and evaluate the achievement of the objectives of the codes of practice by the participants' and assess coverage of Arts 53 and 55. Publication of assessment.

quote: If both the provider or prospective provider and the national competent authority explicitly agree, the exit report may be made publicly available through the single information platform referred to in this Article.
holder: the provider or prospective provider and the national competent authority
note: Publication is optional and needs both parties' agreement.

quote: Providers and prospective providers participating in the AI regulatory sandbox shall remain liable under applicable Union and national liability law for any damage inflicted on third parties
holder: Providers and prospective providers participating in the AI regulatory sandbox
if_not_met: liability under applicable Union and national liability law for damage inflicted on third parties
note: Answer to: third parties harmed, via liability law; consequence: civil liability. Also coded Accountability/Design (fine exemption).

quote: provided that the prospective providers observe the specific plan and the terms and conditions for their participation and follow in good faith the guidance given by the national competent authority, no administrative fines shall be imposed
holder: Prospective providers participating in the AI regulatory sandbox
if_not_met: [inference] the exemption from administrative fines no longer applies; fines under Art. 99 may then be imposed
note: Answer to: the national competent authority. The exemption extends to other Union and national law where other competent authorities were actively involved and gave guidance. Also coded Accountability/Design (liability).

quote: National competent authorities shall submit annual reports to the AI Office and to the Board
note: Answer to: AI Office and Board; consequence: not stated (the Commission 'shall, where appropriate, take the annual reports into account'). Timing: from one year after establishment, every year until termination, plus a final report. Content: progress and results, best practices, incidents, lessons learnt, recommendations on setup and on application or revision of the Regulation. Also coded Accountability/Design (publication).

quote: The national competent authorities shall make those annual reports or abstracts thereof available to the public, online.
note: Publication to the public. Abstracts are allowed instead of full reports.

quote: a short summary of the AI project developed in the sandbox, its objectives and expected results is published on the website of the competent authorities
if_not_met: [inference] the further processing is not permitted
note: Publication. Exception: 'this obligation shall not cover sensitive operational data in relation to the activities of law enforcement, border control, immigration or asylum authorities'. Passive; nearest named actor: the competent authorities.

quote: the provider or prospective provider has drawn up a real-world testing plan and submitted it to the market surveillance authority in the Member State where the testing in real world conditions is to be conducted
if_not_met: testing may not be conducted ('only where all of the following conditions are met')
note: Answer to: market surveillance authority. Also Delivery (drawing up the plan). Linked to Decision-making/Design (approval, Art. 60(4)(b)).

quote: has registered the testing in real world conditions in accordance with Article 71(4) with a Union-wide unique single identification number and with the information specified in Annex IX
note: Registration. For law enforcement, migration, asylum and border control (Annex III points 1, 6, 7): registered 'in the secure non-public section of the EU database'; for critical infrastructure (point 2): per Art. 49(5). Testing registrations are visible only to market surveillance authorities and the Commission unless the provider consents (Art. 71(4)).

quote: has registered the testing in real-world conditions in the secure non-public section of the EU database according to Article 49(4), point (d)
holder: Provider or prospective provider of high-risk AI systems in Annex III points 1, 6 and 7 (law enforcement, migration, asylum and border control management)
if_not_met: testing may not take place (Art. 60(4) conditions)
note: Public-sector carve-out: testing in law enforcement, migration, asylum and border control goes to a non-public section, so it is not published. Annex III point 2 (critical infrastructure) registers under Art. 49(5).

quote: the provider or prospective provider conducting the testing in real world conditions is established in the Union or has appointed a legal representative who is established in the Union
holder: Provider or prospective provider conducting the testing
note: [inference] Ensures someone answerable within Union jurisdiction. Point (e) adds: data transferred to third countries only with appropriate safeguards under Union law.

quote: the subjects of the testing in real world conditions have given informed consent in accordance with Article 61
note: Answerability to affected persons through consent. Law enforcement exception: where seeking consent would prevent testing, 'the testing itself and the outcome of the testing in the real world conditions shall not have any negative effect on the subjects, and their personal data shall be deleted after the test is performed'. Nearest named actor: provider or prospective provider.

quote: Any subjects of the testing in real world conditions, or their legally designated representative, as appropriate, may, without any resulting detriment and without having to provide any justification, withdraw from the testing at any time
holder: Subjects of the testing or their legally designated representative
note: Withdrawal by revoking consent; may also 'request the immediate and permanent deletion of their personal data'. Withdrawal does not affect activities already carried out.
basis: AI pass A; different cell in pass B

quote: Member States shall confer on their market surveillance authorities the powers of requiring providers and prospective providers to provide information, of carrying out unannounced remote or on-site inspections
obligation: statutory duty (Member States) creating statutory powers (market surveillance authorities)
note: Inspection and information powers, plus 'performing checks on the conduct of the testing'. Providers answer to the market surveillance authority. Authorities 'shall use those powers to ensure the safe development of testing'.

quote: Any serious incident identified in the course of the testing in real world conditions shall be reported to the national market surveillance authority in accordance with Article 73.
note: Incident reporting to the regulator. Passive; nearest named actor: provider or prospective provider. Also coded Decision-making/Design and Delivery/Design (same paragraph).

quote: Providers or prospective providers shall notify the national market surveillance authority
note: Notify the authority in the Member State where testing is conducted 'of the suspension or termination of the testing in real world conditions and of the final outcomes'.

quote: The provider or prospective provider shall be liable under applicable Union and national liability law for any damage caused in the course of their testing in real world conditions.
if_not_met: liability under applicable Union and national liability law
note: Answer to: persons harmed, via liability law.

quote: freely-given informed consent shall be obtained from the subjects of testing prior to their participation in such testing
note: Trigger: before participation. Subjects must be informed of: nature, objectives and possible inconvenience; conditions and expected duration; rights to refuse and withdraw without detriment; arrangements for requesting reversal of outputs; the unique identification number and contact details of the provider. Passive; nearest named actor: provider or prospective provider. Also coded Accountability/Design (61(1)(d)) and Delivery/Design (61(2)).
basis: AI pass A; different cell in pass B

quote: the arrangements for requesting the reversal or the disregarding of the predictions, recommendations or decisions of the AI system
obligation: statutory duty (information to be given before consent)
note: A route for subjects to challenge outputs during testing; the arrangements themselves are not specified. Nearest named actor: provider or prospective provider. Linked to Decision-making/Design (Art. 60(4)(k)).

quote: The advisory forum shall prepare an annual report on its activities. That report shall be made publicly available.
note: Publication. Answer to: the public; consequence not stated.

quote: Each expert shall draw up a declaration of interests, which shall be made publicly available.
holder: Experts on the scientific panel; AI Office
note: Publication of interests. Experts must act with impartiality and objectivity, keep information confidential and 'neither seek nor take instructions from anyone'. The AI Office 'shall establish systems and procedures to actively manage and prevent potential conflicts of interest'.

quote: Affected persons should have the right to obtain an explanation where a deployer’s decision is based mainly upon the output from certain high-risk AI systems
note: Where the decision produces legal effects or similarly significant adverse effects on health, safety or fundamental rights; explanation 'should be clear and meaningful'; not where Union or national law gives exceptions or already provides the right. Operative Art. 86 (outside this part).

quote: Conformity assessment bodies shall submit an application for notification to the notifying authority of the Member State in which they are established.
note: Application includes activities, modules, AI types and accreditation certificate (29(2)) or documentary evidence (29(3)). Notified bodies update documentation 'whenever relevant changes occur' so the authority can monitor continuous compliance (29(4)). Answers to notifying authority.

quote: A legal person also remains  a deployer if it involves third parties (e.g. contractors, external staff) in the operation of the system on its behalf and under its responsibility and control.
holder: Legal person deployer (examples: a law enforcement authority or a private security company)
note: Responsibility sits with the organisation, not with contractors or individual staff: 'the individual employees that act within the procedures and under the control of that person should not be considered to be the deployer'. To whom: not stated (market surveillance authorities, para 53). Consequence: not stated. Also bears on Coordination (contractors operating the system) [inference].

quote: if an operator develops its own AI system that it use s afterwards, it will be considered both the provider and the deployer of that system
holder: Operators, including a public authority that develops a system in-house and uses it
note: Allocates the provider and deployer roles, and so both sets of obligations, to the same body. Para (16): the provider 'could also be a public authority that develops the system in -house and puts it into service for its own use'. Para (13) example: 'a public authority develops a scoring system  in-house and deploys it to predict the risk of fraud of household allowance beneficiaries, thereby putting it into service.' To whom: not stated here; enforcement by market surveillance authorities (para 53). Consequence: provider and deployer obligations; fines (para 55).

quote: the provider’s obligation to ensure AI systems interacting with people are designed in a way to inform people that they are interacting with AI and not a human
holder: Providers of AI systems interacting with people
note: Disclosure to persons interacting with the system (e.g. chatbots). Visible labelling 'reduces the risk of deception'. Para (72): Art. 5(1)(a) may still apply to deceptive chatbot content, 'in particular if this has not been visibly disclosed'.

quote: must be notified  to the relevant market surveillance authority and the national data protection authority. Notification must take place after each use
holder: not stated in para 409 (passive); para 419 refers to authorities 'informed by deployers', i.e. the deployer (law enforcement authority)
note: Reporting to regulators. Answers to: the relevant market surveillance authority and the national data protection authority; consequence not stated. Trigger: after each use; purpose 'to be able to report about the number of authorisations and their result'. Need not include 'sensitive operational data'. Done 'in accordance with the national rules referred to in paragraph 5' (Art. 5(4) as quoted). Also coded Coordination/Design.

quote: The prohibition applies to deployers regardless of whether the provider (the supplier of the system) has excluded such use in its contractual relationships with the deployer (the employer), i.e. in the terms of use.
if_not_met: Fines under AI Act Art. 99 (para 55) [inference: not stated in this passage]
note: Allocates answerability to the deployer for prohibited use; the provider's contractual exclusion does not shift it. To whom: not stated in passage (market surveillance authorities enforce, para 53). Consequence: not stated in passage. Example concerns an employer inferring emotions at the workplace. Cross-ref Coordination/Design entry (para 40, providers to exclude prohibited use in terms of use).

quote: the individual employees that act within the procedures and under the control of that person should not be considered to be the deployer
holder: Legal person under whose authority the system is used (e.g. a law enforcement authority or a private security company)
note: Answerability as deployer sits with the organisation, not with individual officials or staff acting within its procedures. The paragraph continues: 'A legal person also remains a deployer if it involves third parties (e.g. contractors, external staff) in the operation of the system on its behalf and under its responsibility and control' (also relevant to Coordination: contractors [inference]). To whom and with what consequence: not stated in passage.

quote: the deployer should explain redress measures in case a risk materialises , including the governance procedures and the complaint mechanisms (such as in  the case of a misidentification).
location: page 118 (printed p. 113), section 10.1.1, para 375 (risk mitigation measures)
note: Redress and complaint routes to be described in the FRIA. To whom the deployer answers: not stated (affected persons, e.g. those misidentified [inference]). Consequence: not stated.

quote: Article 5(2) AI Act also obliges the deployer of a real-time RBI system used in publicly accessible spaces for law enforcement purposes  to register  the system in the EU database provided  for in Article 49 AI Act .
holder: the deployer of a real-time RBI system (law enforcement authority)
if_not_met: use may not be authorised without registration (Art. 5(2) as quoted), except in duly justified urgency with registration 'without undue delay'
note: Registration. 'Undue delay' means 'as soon as possible', case by case, not caused by deliberate action; example: registration within 24 hours after a live-shooter deployment 'might be considered a reasonable delay'. Registration is in a non-public section (Coordination/Resources entry, para 377), so this is not publication.

quote: Article 5(3) AI Act requires each individual request for the use of real-time RBI to be ‘reasoned’ and hence substantiated and motivated.
holder: the deployer, i.e. the competent (law enforcement) authority
note: The deployer answers to the authorising authority. Para 384: who requests is not specified in the Act; the Guidelines assume the deployer, including bodies entrusted under Art. 3(45)(b). Para 389: national law should set the exact content of the request, including evidence of strict necessity and proportionality. Para 394: the request goes to the authority competent under national law. Also a coordination link (request procedure).

quote: The supervisory authorities should also have the powers to do this post fact check and control.
obligation: recommended ('should'); to be provided in national law
note: Audit power over the stop-and-delete duty. Which supervisory authorities is not stated (nearest: market surveillance and data protection authorities, section 10.3).

quote: The logging of the processing activities should be made available to the authority to substantiate the timeliness of the request.
note: Answers to: the authorising authority; purpose: to show an urgent request came within 24 hours; consequence: not stated. Logging itself coded as Delivery/Design (fn 230). Also serves the authorising decision (Decision-making/Resources entry, para 416).
basis: AI pass B; different cell in pass A

quote: In such a case, the request should motivate why no prior request was submitted prior to starting using the system.
holder: the user (deployer) of the real-time RBI system
if_not_met: if rejected, use stops immediately and data are deleted (para 402)
note: Answer to the authorising authority after urgent use. Para 400: the 24 hours run from the moment the system is used, generally when cameras are switched on and the first comparison is made.

quote: Where the law enforcement authority challenges the rejection, the data may be kept by a trustee until a final decision has been taken  on the request.
holder: the law enforcement authority (may challenge); a trustee (holds the data)
note: Challenge route against refusal, with a trustee holding the data meanwhile; 'those data should normally not be placed at the disposal of the law enforcement authority'. The forum for the challenge is not stated.

quote: Notification must take place after each use in order to be able to report about the number of authorisations and their result.
note: Reporting to regulators (market surveillance authority and data protection authority), feeding their annual reports to the Commission (para 419). Consequence of not notifying: not stated. Quote spans a page break. Also coded: Coordination/Design (para 409).

quote: The Commission will publish the Member States’ laws on a public website.
note: Publication of national legal bases for real-time RBI.

quote: Member States shall notify their national laws to the Commission at the latest 30 days following the adoption thereof . Such notification does not provide a presumption of conformity of the Member States’ law with the AI Act
if_not_met: non-notification to the AI Office within the legal deadline of 30 days following the adoption  set out in Article 5(5) may imply that the national law is unenforceable in legal proceedings
note: Answers to: the Commission (AI Office), which 'will send a confirmation of receipt'. Notification does not presume conformity. Publication of the laws coded separately (Commission entry, same paragraph).
basis: AI pass B; different cell in pass A

quote: the possibility of auditing the submitted information, including the technical details and accuracy criteria any time ex ante and ex post by the authorising authority;
obligation: suggested content for national law; non-binding
note: Audit of deployers' submissions, before and after use. The deployer answers to the authorising authority; consequence not stated.

quote: sanctions for not complying with (formal and substantial) requirements;
obligation: suggested content for national law; non-binding
note: Sanctions to be set nationally; who is sanctioned and by whom is not stated.

quote: the name of the responsible personals of the deployers;
holder: Member States (national law); deployers' responsible persons
obligation: suggested content for national law; non-binding
note: Named accountable roles within deployers. To whom they answer and consequence: not stated.

quote: the right to appeal an authorisation that has been denied;
obligation: suggested content for national law; non-binding
note: Appeal route for the requesting authority against refusal (see para 405 trustee entry). Forum not stated.

quote: the rights of persons for which a search is conducted, the rights of persons whose data is captured, and the possible rights of third parties;
obligation: suggested content for national law; non-binding
note: Rights of affected persons; the rights themselves are not specified (fn 235 points to EDPB Guidelines 05/2022). Redress route not stated.

quote: the registration of the use of real-time RBI systems in a central register with  a summary of the substantive elements;
obligation: suggested content for national law; non-binding
note: National register of uses (also a coordination mechanism). Who keeps it and whether it is public: not stated. Same list adds 'possible further reporting obligations'.

quote: must submit annual reports on such use to the Commission. These reports shall be made on the basis of a template provided by the Commission.
holder: national market surveillance authorities; national data protection authorities
note: Regulators report to the Commission on notified uses, including the number and outcome of authorisation decisions (Art. 5(6) box). Para 421: only the data protection authority report covers 2 February to 2 August 2025. Para 422: individual or joint reports per Member State, as they choose. Template coded as Accountability/Resources.

quote: Where the deployer is an EU Institution, body, or agency, the EDPS is obliged to inform the Commission accordingly on an annual basis of the real -time RBI systems used in publicly accessible spaces for law enforcement purposes.
note: Annual reporting for EU institutions, bodies and agencies acting as deployers.

quote: The AI Act requires the Commission to publish annual reports of the uses of real-time RBI systems in publicly accessible spaces for law enforcement purposes in the Member states and by Union institutions, agencies and bodies, based on aggregated data.
note: Public reporting based on national reports. Para 424: no sensitive operational data; 'locations, camera’s used' may be withheld.

quote: the provisions on penalties for non-compliance with the prohibitions in Article 5 AI Act will not apply before 2 August 2025 .
note: Sanctions apply from 2 August 2025. Same para: until then 'there will also be no market surveillance authorities to monitor whether the prohibitions are being properly complied with'.

quote: prohibitions themselves have direct effect and  thus enable affected parties to enforce them in national courts and request interim injunctions against the prohibited practices.
holder: affected parties (may enforce); providers and deployers (answer)
if_not_met: interim injunctions against the prohibited practices
note: Redress route: operators answer to national courts at the suit of affected parties; available even before the penalty and monitoring provisions apply.

quote: the recipient national authorities and Union institutions, bodies, offices and agencies making use of such AI outputs in the Union remain accountable to ensure their use complies with Union law.
holder: Recipient national authorities and Union institutions, bodies, offices and agencies making use of AI outputs from third-country cooperation
obligation: accountability stated in a recital; restated in non-binding guidelines
note: To whom: not stated. Consequence: not stated. Applies where outputs come from AI used by excluded third-country authorities or international organisations.

quote: the prohibitions in the AI Act are without prejudice to any liability that the provider or deployer might incur for the harm caused according to applicable Union or national liability laws.
holder: Providers and deployers of AI systems
if_not_met: Liability for harm caused, under the applicable law
note: Redress route: civil liability to those harmed [inference: to whom is not stated]. Fn 43: conditions for liability 'will be determined by the applicable law'; also mentions the proposed AI Liability Directive (COM/2022/496).

quote: Market surveillance authorities  designated by the Member States as well as the European Data Protection Supervisor (as the market surveillance authority for the EU institutions, agencies and bodies) are responsible for the enforcement
holder: Market surveillance authorities designated by the Member States; European Data Protection Supervisor (for EU institutions, agencies and bodies)
note: Enforcement of the AI Act rules for AI systems, 'including the prohibitions', within the Regulation 2019/1020 market surveillance system. Providers and deployers (including public authorities, and EU institutions via the EDPS) answer to these authorities; consequence: enforcement action and fines (para 55). Authorities act 'on their own initiative or following a complaint'. Coded although it restates the AI Act's enforcement structure, because it is the accountability route the document sets out for Art. 5. Cross-ref Accountability/Design (complaints), Accountability/Resources (powers), Decision-making/Design (designation).

quote: a complaint, which every affected person or any other natural or legal person having grounds to consider such violations has the right  to lodge.
holder: Every affected person and any other natural or legal person having grounds to consider that a violation has occurred
note: Complaint route. To whom: market surveillance authorities, which 'can take enforcement actions in relation to the prohibitions on their own initiative or following a complaint'. Consequence for the complainant's case: not stated.

quote: Providers and deployers engaging in prohibited AI practices may be fined up to EUR 35 000 000 or, if the offender is an undertaking, up to 7% of its total worldwide annual turnover
holder: Providers and deployers engaging in prohibited AI practices
if_not_met: Fines up to EUR 35 000 000 or, for undertakings, up to 7% of total worldwide annual turnover for the preceding financial year, whichever is higher
note: Highest tier: non-compliance with Art. 5 is 'the most severe infringement'. To whom: the authority imposing the fine is not named in the passage (nearest: market surveillance authorities, para 53). Para 57: because violations give rise to the highest fines, the prohibitions' scope 'should be interpreted narrowly' (Decision-making/Design entry).

quote: Each Member State should lay down rules if and  to the extent that administrative fines may be imposed on public authorities and bodies established in that Member State  as providers and deplo yers of AI systems.
holder: Public authorities and bodies established in a Member State, as providers and deployers of AI systems
obligation: statutory sanction, conditional on national rules
if_not_met: Administrative fines only if and to the extent national rules provide; otherwise not stated
note: Consequence for public-sector providers and deployers depends on national law; the document states no default. To whom: not stated (nearest: market surveillance authorities, para 53). Cross-ref Decision-making/Design entry (same passage).

quote: EU institutions, bodies and agencies that vi olate the prohibitions may be subject to administrative fines of up to EUR 1 500 000.
note: To whom: not stated in passage; nearest named actor is the European Data Protection Supervisor, market surveillance authority for EU institutions (para 53) [inference].

quote: In such cases,  the principle of ne bis in idem should be respected. In any event, the criteria for determining the penalty as provided for in Article 99(7) AI Act must be taken into account.
obligation: statutory ('must be taken into account'); 'should be respected'
note: Passive: the authority setting penalties is not named (nearest: market surveillance authorities, para 53). Applies where one conduct breaches several AI Act provisions, e.g. non-labelling of deep fakes that is also a deceptive technique under Art. 5(1)(a).

quote: The same practice that falls within the prohibition  of Article 5(1)(a) or (b) AI Act may also constitute an infringement of other Union law legislation and be subject to enforcement under both the AI Act  and those other acts .
holder: Providers and deployers of AI systems
if_not_met: Enforcement under the AI Act and under the other acts
note: To whom: authorities enforcing the AI Act and those enforcing the other acts (not named). Paras 136-145 then describe interplay with consumer, data protection, non-discrimination, DSA, AVMSD, political advertising, financial and product safety law (reports of other instruments, not separately coded except para 144).

quote: Deployers of such systems remain responsible to ensure that employees are not adversely affected by their use.
note: Named responsibility. To whom the deployer answers: not stated. Consequence: not stated. Also coded: Delivery/Design (para 270).

quote: the deployer’s obligations in Article 50(4) AI Act to label ‘deep fakes’ and certain AI-generated text publications on matters of public interest
holder: Deployers (labelling deep fakes and certain AI-generated text on matters of public interest); providers (informing people they interact with AI)
note: Coded as Accountability (disclosure to the public) [inference]; could also be read as Delivery. Relevant where a public body publishes AI-generated text on matters of public interest [inference]. Same sentence: 'the provider’s obligation to ensure AI systems interacting with people are designed in a way to inform people that they are interacting with AI and not a human'. To whom: the people exposed to the content. Consequence: not stated; para 72 and fn 63: deception not visibly disclosed may in some cases fall under the Art. 5(1)(a) prohibition. Cross-ref Delivery/Design entry (provider design features, para 71).

quote: In the case of checks by competent market surveillance authorities, it is on the provider and the deployer of the AI system, each within their responsibilities, to demonstrate that the AI practice is legitimate and justified
holder: Provider and deployer of the AI system, each within their responsibilities
obligation: non-binding interpretation (burden on provider and deployer)
if_not_met: not stated (practice may be found to fall within the prohibition, fines para 55 [inference])
note: To whom: competent market surveillance authorities (who carry out the checks; trigger for checks not stated). What must be shown: 'transparency of the functioning of the AI system, and information about the types of data and data sources, ensuring that only data related to the social context in which the score is used are processed ..., the system is performing as intended, and any resulting detrimental or unfavourable treatment is justified and proportionate'. Bears on checking AI outputs ('performing as intended'). Cross-ref Delivery/Design entry (safeguards, same paragraph).

quote: the exercise of such powers be controlled through public administrative law
holder: the public sector (governments as users and producers of AI-based solutions)
obligation: restatement of existing legal principle (non-binding here)
note: Also: 'the public sector is required to conform to administrative law, and to ethical and human rights principles'. To whom the holder answers: not stated (no court, ombudsman or review body named); consequence: not stated. Close to a report of existing law; coded because the handbook presents it as a condition of AI use. Cross-ref Decision-making/Design entry at section 1.4.

quote: Developing and applying certification and labelling approaches based on common sustainability principles aligned with the EU environmental policies
note: Labelling as a public signal of compliance. To whom: not stated (users/citizens [inference]); consequence: not stated. Also coded Delivery/Design (certification).

quote: Citizens and businesses need to be able to understand when, where and which AI based solution is used, and to which extent AI use has influenced any decisions affecting them.
note: Preceding sentence: 'It is important that the use of AI by public administrations meets the highest possible level of transparency.' Following: citizens 'need to understand where AI systems are used by their government, and for which purpose.' Answers to: citizens and businesses. Consequence: not stated. No mechanism, such as a notice or register, is specified here.

quote: These success/failure cases would need to have fully enforced transparency procedures
holder: not stated (nearest: bodies whose cases the observatory collects)
note: A transparency condition on the success and failure cases shared through the observatory. To whom: not stated. Consequence: not stated. Also coded Accountability/Resources (pointer to the UK standard).

quote: how do we individuals/citizens know that an organisation or public administration is applying compliance models for sustainable AI?
note: One of three 'key questions' the handbook poses; none is addressed to a named actor. Answers to: individuals and citizens. Consequence: not stated. Context: most IT and software used by the public sector 'is provided by private organisations through procurement'.

quote: How and to what e xtent can procured solutions providers be held accountable?
note: Raises the accountability of providers in the value chain as an open question. To whom and with what consequence: not stated. Related description (p. 20): established procurement processes do not require 'vendors to assess the risk that their products pose to portions of the population'. That is a described gap and is not coded.

quote: where each actor operating in th e ecosystem provides added value, carries a clear role, and identifiable responsibilities.
location: page 9 (printed p. 7), Executive summary, 'Conclusions and next steps'
holder: each actor operating in the ecosystem
note: Full sentence: 'There is a need to provide a shared, concrete and actionable approach based on replication of good practices, and leadership of governance, where each actor ...'. Calls for identifiable responsibilities for every actor. To whom they answer: not stated; consequence: not stated. Executive summary only; I found no body-text counterpart (section 5.1 does not repeat it).

quote: may demonstrate compliance with the ir respective transparency obligations for AI-generated content under those provisions by adhering to a code of practice that is assessed as adequate pursuant to Article 50(7) AI Act
holder: Providers and deployers of AI systems within the scope of Art. 50(2) and (4)
if_not_met: Opting out of sections of an adequate code means 'losing the benefit of facilitating the demonstration of compliance in that respect' (para (147))
note: Answer to: the Commission and competent market surveillance authorities (para (147)). Adherents 'will benefit from increased trust from the Commission , the other competent market surveillance authorities, and other stakeholders (including the general public )'. The code itself is coded as Accountability/Resources.

quote: AI agents must be designed and developed in such a way that they disclose both their artificial nature and the person on whose behalf they are acting
note: Names the principal behind an agent, 'considering the need for transparency of the origin and the delegation of authority and accountability for the consequences of their actions' (same para). Footnote 21 points to EU Digital Identity Wallets for verifiable agent identity (coded under Resources). Also coded as Delivery/Design (architecture-level disclosure).
basis: AI pass A; different cell in pass B

quote: all natural persons interacting with such AI systems are explicitly informed about the artificial, non -human nature of the interacting counterpart.
if_not_met: fines (para 152); enforcement by market surveillance authorities, AI Office or EDPS (para 151)
note: Disclosure to the persons concerned that they deal with AI. Answers to: the natural persons interacting (informed) and the supervising authority (enforcement). Consequence: fines. Where vulnerable groups are foreseeable, information 'should be adapted accordingly and provided in an accessible format'. Also coded as Delivery/Design (para 28).

quote: providers will need to assess and demonstrate
obligation: condition for relying on an exception (non-binding interpretation)
if_not_met: exception unavailable; disclosure duty applies; fines (para 152)
note: Burden of proof on the provider. To whom: not stated ([inference] market surveillance authorities, para 151). Consequence: not stated beyond loss of the exception. Also coded as Delivery/Design.

quote: Such systems may be used , but they  remain subject to  the transparency obligation under Article  50(1) AI Act, so natural persons must be informed they are interacting with such systems.
holder: not stated (providers of public-facing crime-reporting systems)
note: Limit on the law-enforcement exception: public crime-reporting systems must disclose. Examples: police chatbots on official websites, police telephone hotlines, fraud-reporting portals 'operated by financial institutions or public authorities', witness-statement assistants. Examples describe human officers validating before action (page 20). Also a Delivery duty (see para 28 entry).
basis: AI pass A; different cell in pass B

quote: Such reliance is without prejudice to the responsibility of the provider of the AI system to demonstrate compliance with Article 50(2) AI Act.
note: Responsibility stays with the system provider when marking is outsourced upstream. To whom: not stated ([inference] market surveillance authorities, para 151). Also linked to the Delivery/Resources entry for para 74.

quote: Article 50(3) AI Act imposes an obligation on deployers of emotion recognition systems and biometric categorisation systems to inform natural persons who are exposed to those systems of the operation of the system.
holder: Deployers of emotion recognition systems and biometric categorisation systems
if_not_met: fines up to EUR 15 000 000 or 3% of worldwide annual turnover; EU institutions, bodies and agencies up to EUR 750 000 (para 152)
note: Disclosure to exposed persons, 'including children' (para 106), whether in real time or ex post (para 100). Answers to: exposed persons; enforced by market surveillance authorities (para 151). Emotion recognition systems are all high-risk and prohibited in workplace and education (para 102). The duty 'does not, in itself render the use ... lawful' (para 110). Also coded as Delivery/Design (para 108).

quote: Article 50(4), first subparagraph, AI Act obliges deployers of AI systems that generate or manipulate image, audio or video content constituting a deep fake to ‘disclose that the deep fake content has been artificially generated or manipulated ’.
holder: Deployers of AI systems generating or manipulating deep fakes, used for professional purposes
if_not_met: fines (para 152); non-adhering deployers may face requests for information on labelling (para 148)
note: Labelling/disclosure to the public. Conditions (para 112): professional use, deep fake, no law-enforcement exception. Deep fake test (para 113): resemblance, existing, persons/objects/places/entities/events, false appearance of authenticity. Examples include an 'AI-generated video of an individual resembling a politician' (page 37). Also coded as Delivery/Design (perceivable labels). 37 words.
basis: AI pass A; different cell in pass B

quote: obliges deployers of AI systems that generate or manipulate text which is published with the purpose of informing the public on matters of public interest to disclose that such text has been artificially generated or manipulated.
holder: Deployers of AI systems generating or manipulating text published to inform the public on matters of public interest
note: Publication/disclosure duty. Labels must be 'clear and perceivable' without technical tools. Example in scope (page 43): 'AI-generated message on a meteorological institute’s social media profile warning citizens about stormy weather'. Not published: 'organisation-internal texts or communications' (page 43). Exceptions: human review/editorial control with editorial responsibility; law enforcement. Texts generated before 2 August 2026 but published after must be labelled (para 154). [inference] Directly applies to public bodies' AI-drafted public communications.
basis: AI pass A; different cell in pass B

quote: This entails that said person must hold the ultimate legal responsibility over the publication of the content, including the human review or editorial control
holder: Legal or natural person holding editorial responsibility (e.g. an individual, editorial board, or the publishing company)
obligation: condition for relying on an exception (non-binding interpretation, 'must')
note: Named accountable role for AI-assisted publications. To whom: not stated beyond 'public accountability and trust' (same para). Consequence: not stated beyond loss of the exception. Also see the publication entry for para 138.

quote: the identity and contact details of the legal  person, the natural person or the function with editorial responsibility should be made publicly available on an easily findable location
holder: not stated (deployer relying on the exception)
note: Publication of who is responsible, 'To ensure public accountability and trust'; e.g. website terms and conditions or a colophon. Answers to: the public. Consequence: not stated.

quote: the Commission and the competent market surveillance authorities will focus their supervisory activities on assessing whether those signatories have adhered to the code of practice  and implemented the measures contained therein.
holder: Providers and deployers within scope of Article 50(2) and (4) that sign an adequate code of practice
obligation: voluntary route to demonstrate compliance (adhere to an adequate code or demonstrate by other means)
if_not_met: 'Any opt -out from sections by signatories of a code of practice that is deemed adequate will result in those providers and deployers losing the benefit of facilitating the demonstration of compliance in that respect.' (para 147)
note: Answers to: the Commission and competent market surveillance authorities. Signatories 'will benefit from increased trust'. Applies to Art. 50(2), (4) and (5) only, not 50(1) or 50(3). Paras 84, 118, 123, 132, 137 offer the same route for specific duties, including the human review condition.

quote: are expected to demonstrate how they have complied with their obligations under Article 50(2), (4) and (5) AI Act through other adequate means.
holder: Providers and deployers that are not signatories to an adequate code of practice
obligation: expected (non-binding interpretation); akin to comply or explain
if_not_met: 'providers not adhering to a code of practice may also be subject to a larger number of requests for information and requests for access'; deployers likewise for labelling (para 148)
note: Answers to: competent authorities 'including the AI Office'. Consequence: more scrutiny. They are also 'expected to explain how the measures they implement ensure compliance'. Also see the gap-analysis Delivery entry.

quote: Competent authorities may take commitments implemented in line with a code of practice that is deemed adequate into account  as a mitigating factor when fixing the amount of fines
note: Links code adherence to sanction size, 'depending on the specific circumstances'.

quote: which every affected person or any other natural or legal person having grounds to consider such violations has the right to lodge
holder: Every affected person or any other natural or legal person having grounds to consider a violation
note: Complaint route: complaints go to the market surveillance authorities (or AI Office/EDPS within competence). Consequence for the operator: possible enforcement action and fines.

quote: Market surveillance authorities designated by the Member States, the AI Office (47), and the European Data Protection Supervisor  (48) are responsible for supervising and enforcing the rule s for AI systems  falling within their competence
holder: Market surveillance authorities designated by the Member States; the AI Office; the European Data Protection Supervisor
note: Who providers and deployers answer to. Footnote 48: the EDPS acts 'As the market surveillance authority for the EU institutions, agencies and bodies'. Footnote 47: the AI Office covers AI systems built on GPAI models from the same provider. Other supervisors (data protection, consumer protection) keep their powers. Also coded as Decision-making/Design (enforcement actions). 34 words.

quote: Provider and deployers that do not comply with the applicable transparency obligations laid down in Article 50 AI Act may be fined up to EUR 15 000 000
if_not_met: fines up to EUR 15 000 000 or, for an undertaking, up to 3% of total worldwide annual turnover, whichever is higher; for SMEs whichever is lower
note: Consequence for all Art. 50 duties. Authorities weigh nature, gravity, duration, intent or negligence, and 'the degree of cooperation with market surveillance authorities'. [inference] Applies to member-state public authorities as operators unless national rules provide otherwise; the document does not say.

quote: EU institutions, bodies and agencies that violate the transparency obligations may be subject to administrativ e fines of up to EUR 750 000.
if_not_met: administrative fines of up to EUR 750 000
note: Sanction specific to EU public bodies as providers or deployers; supervisor is the EDPS (footnote 48). Relevant to EP2020 and EP2024 (European Parliament tools) [inference].

quote: Another example of a provider is a company or another organisation (e.g. a public authority) that has developed an interactive AI system (e.g. chatbot)  in-house and puts it into service in the Union for its own use
holder: A public authority that develops an interactive AI system (e.g. chatbot) in-house and puts it into service for its own use
note: Allocates the provider role, and with it responsibility for Art. 50(1)/(2) compliance, to a public body building its own chatbot; the preceding example says the provider is 'responsible for compliance with the transparency obligations in Article  50(1) and/or (2) AI  Act'. To whom it answers: market surveillance authorities, or the EDPS for EU institutions (para (151), fn (48)); consequence: fines (para (152)). An example box, but it illustrates the legal definition rather than practice. One body can be both provider and deployer (para (15)).
basis: AI pass B; different cell in pass A

quote: A legal person remains a deployer even if it involves third parties (e.g. contractors, freelancers) in the operation of the system on  its behalf and under its responsibility and control.
note: Allocates responsibility to the organisation: employees acting under its instructions 'should not be considered as separate deployers' (same para). [inference] For a public body, its officials' use of the tool is the body's responsibility. Answers to: market surveillance authorities (para 151). Consequence: fines (para 152).

quote: Any use by natural persons acting on behalf or under the authority of a deployer acting in a professional capacity will fall within the scope of the professional deployer’s transparency obligations
holder: Professional deployer, for use by natural persons acting on its behalf or under its authority
note: Staff (e.g. public officials) using AI in their work fall under their organisation's deployer obligations, not the personal-use exclusion [inference]. The exclusion covers only 'purely personal , non-professional activity'. Cross-ref para (14).
basis: AI pass B; different cell in pass A

quote: Such framework shall ensure consistency in the treatment of AI initiatives, with clear accountability and transparency
obligation: proposed: mandatory by policy (shall), awaiting Bureau approval
note: Stated aim only: no accountable role, answerability relationship or consequence is named here. To whom: not stated; consequence: not stated. The only reporting line in the note is the Board Chair's updates to the WG ICT (para 21).

quote: The reasoning behind AI algorithms and decision-making processes shall thus be made transparent and understandable so that it is then clear why a model led to a certain recommendation or suggestion.
location: page 3, II. Compliance and control, para 14
note: Explainability of outputs. To whom the holder answers: not stated. Consequence: not stated. Could also be read as Delivery. Nearest named actor: the administration. 33 words.
basis: AI pass A; different cell in pass B

quote: Regular updates on the advancement of the AI roadmap should be submitted to the WG ICT by the Governance Board Chair.
note: Reporting line: the Chair answers to the Bureau Working Group on ICT Innovation Strategy (WG ICT). Frequency: 'regular', not specified. Consequence: not stated.

quote: Non-compliance with the assessment process should lead to the suspension of the AI project.
location: page 4, III. Risk and impact assessment processes, para 25
note: Sanction. Who suspends and to whom the project answers: not stated. Also coded as Decision-making/Design (pausing a tool) and linked to the Delivery entry for para 25.

quote: Develop a specific communication process concerning explainability.
location: page 6, Transparent and explainable Artificial Intelligence, Requirements
note: Coded as Accountability because the same section states '“Explainability” is a pre -condition for accountability.' To whom the holder answers: not stated ([inference] users). Consequence: not stated. Could also be read as Coordination. Nearest named actor: Parliament's administration.

quote: to provide national competent authorities and notified bodies with the necessary information in a clear and comprehensive form to assess the compliance of the AI system with those requirements
location: Art. 1(10), replacing AI Act Art. 11(1) second subpara.; p. 19
note: Passive; nearest named actor: provider of the high-risk AI system (Art. 11). Technical documentation 'shall be drawn up in such a way as to demonstrate' compliance; minimum content Annex IV. Holder answers to national competent authorities and notified bodies; consequence not stated here. Cross-ref Resources/Accountability (simplified form) and Coordination/Design (notified bodies accept form).

quote: The notified body shall update the documentation referred to in paragraphs 2 and 3 of this Article whenever relevant changes occur, in order to enable the authority responsible for notified bodies to monitor and verify continuous compliance
location: Art. 1(15), replacing AI Act Art. 29(4); p. 21
note: Holder answers to the authority responsible for notified bodies; consequence not stated here. Trigger: whenever relevant changes occur; comparator: Art. 31 requirements. Also: documents and certificates from other designations 'may be used to support and expedite' designation; Section A notified bodies submit the single application to the sectoral notifying authority.

quote: The Commission shall publish its assessment of the adequacy of the codes of practice.
location: Art. 1(21), replacing AI Act Art. 56(6); p. 23
note: Publication. To whom: not stated (public). Consequence: not stated.

quote: (c) include effective governance and accountability arrangements;
location: Art. 1(25), inserting AI Act Art. 60a(5)(c); p. 25
holder: Member States (in their real-world testing frameworks)
note: Content of the arrangements, to whom, and consequences: not stated.

quote: providers of high-risk AI systems subject to the competence of the AI Office pursuant to paragraph 1 of this Article shall report any serious incidents to the AI Office.
location: Art. 1(31)(c), inserting AI Act Art. 75(1a); p. 27
holder: Providers of high-risk AI systems within AI Office competence (Art. 75(1))
note: Reporting to regulator (derogation from Art. 73). Art. 73(2)-(9) apply mutatis mutandis (not restated). Consequence not stated. Cross-ref Coordination/Design (AI Office transmits to MSA).

quote: If a notified body to which the Commission has delegated tasks under this paragraph does not perform those tasks adequately, the Commission may withdraw the delegation with immediate effect.
location: Art. 1(31)(c), inserting AI Act Art. 75(1e); p. 27
holder: Notified body (answers to the Commission); European Commission
obligation: statutory duty to entrust; statutory power to withdraw
if_not_met: for notified bodies not performing adequately: 'the Commission may withdraw the delegation with immediate effect'
note: Notified body answers to the Commission; consequence is withdrawal of delegation. 'Adequately' not defined.
basis: AI pass B; different cell in pass A

quote: no later than four months following receipt of the request, inform the single point of contact of its intention to exercise its powers in accordance with Article 75a or of its reasons for not exercising its powers.

note: To compel submission to investigation, compliance with information requests and inspections by decision, correct answers, corrective actions, commitments, or a non-compliance decision. Funds go to the Union general budget (75c(7)).

Art. 2(13) and 30(2) (power for five years from 27 July 2026, tacitly extended unless opposed); 'The Commission shall draw up a report in respect of the delegation of power not later than nine months before the end of the five-year period.' note: Holder answers to the Member State authorities enforcing Art. 99 penalties (not named here). Cross-ref Coordination/Design Art. 25(2) and (4).

quote: the records of processing activities pursuant to Regulations (EU) 2016/679 and (EU) 2018/1725 and Directive (EU) 2016/680 include the reasons why the processing of special categories of personal data was strictly necessary to detect and correct biases
