Also coded Delivery/Design (Art. 4a(1) and 4a(2)).
basis: AI pass B; different cell in pass A

quote: a provider applying Article 6(3) of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 remains obligated to document its assessment before that AI system is placed on the market or put into service. National competent authorities should be able to request that assessment.
holder: Providers applying Art. 6(3) (Annex III system assessed as not high-risk)
obligation: recital restating a statutory duty ('remains obligated'); NCA access 'should'
note: Holder answers to national competent authorities on request; consequence not stated. Registration of such systems in the EU database retained but simplified: 'it remains crucial for effective market surveillance and public accountability that such AI systems are registered in the EU database'. Content of deleted Annex VIII points 7 and 9 not shown in this document. Also relevant to Coordination (EU database).

quote: The AI Office may exercise the powers listed in Article 14(4), points (a), (b) and (c) of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 and Article 74(12) and (13) of this Regulation by simple request or by decision.
obligation: statutory power; duty to answer for operators where request is by decision
if_not_met: fines under Art. 99(5) for 'supplying incorrect, incomplete or misleading information'
note: Information requests must state legal basis, purpose, information required and period. Simple request: 'no obligation to provide the information requested' but a voluntary reply 'must be correct and not misleading'. Decision: indicate fines and 'the right to have the decision reviewed by the Court of Justice'. Copy sent to the national market surveillance authority.

quote: an operator falling within the scope of Article 75(1) does not comply with the relevant provisions of this Regulation or with commitments made binding pursuant to Article 75b, it shall adopt a decision establishing such non-compliance.
obligation: statutory duty (AI Office must decide); duty on operator to comply and report measures
note: Preliminary findings first (75c(2)); decision may order measures 'within a reasonable period'; 'The operator concerned shall provide the AI Office with a description of the measures it has taken'; optional 'structured dialogue'. No-grounds cases closed by decision (75c(9)). Limitation period five years (75c(8)).

quote: A decision adopted pursuant to paragraph 1 of this Article may be accompanied by the imposition of penalties in accordance with Article 99(3) to (7)
if_not_met: administrative fines under Art. 99(4); Art. 99(5) for incorrect, incomplete or misleading information
note: Fineable: '(a) infringement of any applicable provision of this Regulation, including those not listed in Article 99(4)'; failure to comply with decisions or measures; failure to comply with binding commitments. Fine levels are in Art. 99 (not reproduced). Fines go to the Union budget (75c(7)).

quote: may be revoked at any time by the European Parliament or by the Council. A decision of revocation shall put an end to the delegation of power specified in that decision.
holder: European Commission (answers to the European Parliament and the Council)
if_not_met: revocation of the delegation; delegated act does not enter into force if EP or Council objects
note: Covers the new delegated powers in Art. 2(13) and 30(2). Objection window three months (AI Act) or two months (Machinery Reg. Art. 47(6)). 'The Commission shall draw up a report in respect of the delegation of power not later than nine months before the end of the five-year period.' Recital 45: consultations 'including at expert level'; EP and Council 'receive all documents at the same time as Member States’ experts'.

quote: While it remains crucial for effective market surveillance and public accountability that such AI systems are registered in the EU database, the registration requirements should be simplified and made more proportionate.
obligation: recital (explanatory); the registration duty itself is in AI Act Art. 49(2), not reproduced
note: Registration of systems the provider has judged not high-risk under Art. 6(3) is kept but its content cut (Annex VIII section B points 7 and 9 deleted; their content is not given in this text). Recital 22 also says the provider 'remains obligated to document its assessment before that AI system is placed on the market' and 'National competent authorities should be able to request that assessment.'

quote: provide a list of those most relevant internet domains names (top and second -level domain, e.g. “example.com”) by listing the top 10 % of all  domain names determined by the size of the content scraped
holder: Providers of general-purpose AI models that crawl or scrape online content (or have it done on their behalf)
obligation: statutory duty via mandatory Template section; SME variant 'should'
note: SMEs 'should disclose top 5% of all domain names or 1 000 internet domain names, whichever is lower' (template text; fn 16 in body says 'top 5%, or the top 1000 domains'). Section 2.3 also requires crawler names, purposes, behaviour (e.g. 'respect of robot.txt'), period of collection, and description of website types incl. 'government portals'. Para 16: the Template does not require disclosure of specific works.

quote: Describe the measures implemented before model training to respect reservations of rights from the TDM exception or limitation before and during data collection, including the opt -out protocols and solutions hono ured by the provider
obligation: statutory duty via mandatory Template section; copyright-policy summary 'encouraged'
note: Disclosure of copyright compliance measures (the copyright policy duty itself is Art. 53(1)(c), not set out here). Template also asks whether the provider is a Signatory to the Code of Practice. 'Providers are also encouraged to disclose a summary of their copyright policy'.

quote: Information about the general-purpose AI model provided in the Summary should cover data used in all stages of the model training, from pre -training to post -training, including model alignment
obligation: non-binding interpretation ('should'), given legal weight by Art. 53(1)(d) reference to the template
note: Covers fine-tuning and 'all sources and types of data, regardless of whether the data are protected or not'. Exclusion: 'other input data used during the model’s operation (e.g. through retrieval augmented generation) are not required in the mandatory sections of the Template ... unless the model actively learns from this input data' (footnote 14: may be disclosed voluntarily). So data a public body feeds in through retrieval at run time is not in the Summary [inference].
basis: AI pass B; different cell in pass A

quote: The Template annexed to th is Explanatory Notice aims to provide a common minimal baseline for the information to be made publicly available in the Summary.
location: Section 3, para (15); p. 5 (file marker); Annex Template, pp. 9-14
obligation: statutory duty (summary 'according to a template provided by the AI Office'); mandatory sections of the Template; optional sections voluntary
if_not_met: fines as in para 26 (up to 3% of worldwide turnover or EUR 15 000 000)
note: Disclosure content (what the provider must make public). Three sections: (1) general information (provider, model, modalities, data size in broad ranges, latest data date, linguistic characteristics 'focusing in particular on EU official languages'); (2) list of data sources (public datasets, licensed and other private datasets, crawled data, user data incl. 'data from user interactions with the AI model (e.g. user input and prompts)', synthetic data, other); (3) data processing aspects (TDM opt-outs, illegal content removal). Para 16: providers 'may nevertheless decide on a voluntary basis to go beyond the minimum requirements'. Para 30: one Summary may cover several models if identical.

quote: it is recommended that providers act in good faith and on a voluntary basis enable parties with a legitimate interest including rightholders, upon requests, to obtain information whether the provider has scraped and used for training content
note: 'Upon request' answerability to rightholders for domains not listed in the Summary. Does not affect other remedies (e.g. Art. 8 IPR Enforcement Directive). Consequence not stated.

quote: Providers should ensure that the information included in the Summary is reported in good faith  and in an accurate and comprehensive manner.
if_not_met: AI Office may verify the Template and 'may request corrective measures'; fines as in para 26
note: Quality standard for the disclosure. 'Flexibility is provide d under specific sections ... to disclose only information that is relevant, necessary for the purpose of the Summary, and practicable to obtain'. Comparator: accuracy, comprehensiveness; metric not stated.

quote: The AI Office may verify whether the Template has been filled in correctly  in order to assess if the provider has complied with Article 53(1)(d) AI Act .
holder: AI Office (verifies); providers of general-purpose AI models (answer)
if_not_met: 'Non-compliance may be sanctioned with fines of up to 3% of the provider’s annual total worldwide turnover in the preceding financial year or EUR 15 000 000, whichever is higher.'
note: Providers answer to the AI Office. 'the AI Office has all enforcement powers under the AI Act and and may request corrective measures'. Scope of the check: 'without performing a work-by-work assessment or checks whether specific content has been used or not for the training'. Comparator: the Template; trigger not stated. Enforcement starts 2 August 2026 (para 33). 'The lawfu l collection and processing of the data remains the responsibility of the provider under other applicable Union law'.

quote: providers and parties with a legitimate interest , including rightsholders, are encouraged to use alternative dispute resolution mechanisms available at national level (such as mediation)
holder: Providers of general-purpose AI models; parties with a legitimate interest, including rightsholders
note: Redress route for disputes over the Summary; also 'other available remedies provided for by Union and national law (e.g. under Article 8 o f the Intellectual Property Rights Enforcement Directive)'. To whom/consequence not stated.

quote: the information reported by the modifying entity in the Template should be limited to the training content used for the model modification only23, and the name of the model(s) that was modified should be clearly indicated in the Summary
holder: Downstream entity that modifies an existing general-purpose AI model and thereby becomes its provider
note: Value chain: when modification makes the downstream entity the provider (per the Commission guidelines on GPAI models, not restated here). [inference] Could include a public body fine-tuning a GPAI model to the extent that makes it a provider. Cross-ref Coordination/Design (model dependencies).

quote: The Summary should also be updated whenever  the provider further train s its own general-purpose AI model placed on the market on additional data that requires an update of the content of the Summary.
holder: Providers of general-purpose AI models that further train a model already placed on the market
note: Trigger: further training on additional data; update 'at six-month intervanls [sic] or if in the meantime the additional data ... requires a material ly significant update ... whichever is sooner'; include date of update; publish 'alongside the modified model'. Template header requires version and 'Last update'.

quote: The Summary should be made publicly available at the latest when the model is placed on the Union market. It should be published on the provider’s official website in a clearly visible and accessible manner
obligation: statutory duty to publish (Art. 53(1)(d)); timing and manner are non-binding interpretation ('should')
if_not_met: 'Non-compliance may be sanctioned with fines of up to 3% of the provider’s annual total worldwide turnover in the preceding financial year or EUR 15 000 000, whichever is higher.' (para 26)
note: Publication to the public; 'also be made publicly available together with the model across all its public distribution channels'. Para (2) restates the Art. 53(1)(d) duty 'to draw up and make publicly available a sufficiently detailed public summary', 'according to a template provided by the AI Office'. Applies also to free and open-source models (fn 4). Stated purposes (paras 6-12): rightsholders, data subjects, downstream providers, researchers ('allow academic institutions and organisations to critically evaluate'), competition. Para 9: does not replace data-protection information duties. Model providers are coded as part of the value chain of public-sector tools.

quote: For models placed on the market before 2 August 2025, providers should take the necessary steps to make the corresponding Summary publicly available no later than 2 August 2027.
holder: Providers of general-purpose AI models placed on the market before 2 August 2025
if_not_met: not stated; AI Office supervision and enforcement for GPAI rules 'will start as of 2 August 2026'
note: Where information is unavailable or disproportionately burdensome to retrieve, 'the provider should clearly state and justify the corresponding information gaps in its Summary'.

quote: requires all providers of general -purpose AI models to draw up and make publicly available a  sufficiently detailed public summary of the content used for the training of the model
obligation: statutory duty (AI Act); the Notice's explanations are non-binding interpretation
if_not_met: 'Non-compliance may be sanctioned with fines of up to 3% of the provider’s annual total worldwide turnover in the preceding financial year or EUR 15 000 000, whichever is higher.' (para 26); AI Office 'may request corrective measures'
note: Publication duty, owed to the public and supervised by the AI Office. Para (3): applies to all GPAI models on the Union market, 'including providers of general -purpose AI models released under free and open -source licenses'; footnote 4: the open-source exception in Art. 53(2) does not apply. Must follow the AI Office template (coded Accountability/Resources). Quoted from body text rather than the 'RELEVANT LEGAL TEXT' box on page 3. Detailed content coded in the following Accountability/Design entries.

quote: this section requires disclosure of the main datasets that were used to train the model, such as large private or public databases, and a  comprehensive narrative description of the data scraped online by or on behalf of the provider
location: page 5, section 3, para (15) point 2; Template Section 2 (pages 10-14)
obligation: mandatory by statute (template content); level of detail varies by data source
if_not_met: fines up to 3% of worldwide turnover or EUR 15 000 000 (para 26)
note: Sub-sections: 2.1 publicly available datasets ('large' = over 3% of all publicly available data for that modality, listed with links); 2.2 private datasets (licensed data: modality only; other private data listed 'only if publicly known', para 19); 2.3 crawled and scraped data (crawler names, purposes, behaviour incl. robots.txt, period, type of sites incl. 'government portals'); 2.4 user data, including 'interaction with the providers’ AI models and/or systems' (yes/no plus general description); 2.5 synthetic data, naming the models used, 'in particular through model distillation'; 2.6 other sources. User data from public officials' use of a provider's model would appear only in this general form [inference].

quote: this section of the Template requires disclosure of certain data processing aspects that are relevant for the exercise of the rights of parties with legitimate interests under Union law
location: page 5, section 3, para (15) point 3; Template Section 3 (page 14)
obligation: mandatory by statute (template content); Section 3.3 optional
if_not_met: fines up to 3% of worldwide turnover or EUR 15 000 000 (para 26)
note: 3.1: whether the provider signed the GPAI Code of Practice, and measures 'to respect reservations of rights from the TDM exception or limitation before and during data collection'. 3.2: 'General description of measures taken' to remove illegal content (also coded Delivery/Design). 3.3: optional other information. Providers 'are also encouraged to disclose a summary of their copyright policy'.

quote: the Template requires a disclosure of a summary of the list of top domain names crawled and scraped from online sources in a summarised narrative form
location: page 5, section 3, para (16); footnote 16; Template Section 2.3 (page 12)
obligation: mandatory by statute (template content); lower threshold for SMEs
if_not_met: fines up to 3% of worldwide turnover or EUR 15 000 000 (para 26)
note: Metric: domains 'in the top 10 % of all domain names determined by the size of the content scraped'; SMEs 'top 5% of all domain names or 1 000 internet domain names, whichever is lower' (Template wording; footnote 16 words it differently). Not required: 'the details for the specific data and works used to train the model'. More detail may be given voluntarily.

quote: to reliably hit 24-hour notifications.
note: Incident notification deadline; to whom not stated [inference: NIS2 incident reporting to CSIRTs/competent authorities, mentioned on pp. 12-13]; consequence not stated. Cross-ref Delivery/Design same bullet.

quote: Require critical infrastructure operators to attest zero-trust baselines, resilient incident response capabilities during annual audits, and clear escalation paths for AI-accelerated incidents.
note: Attestation during annual audits; holder answers to national authorities [inference: the requiring body]; consequence not stated. Edge case: about AI used by attackers. Cross-ref Decision-making/Design same bullet.

quote: ENISA’s proposal for machine-processable security attestations and implementation of SBOM strategies can operationalise the CRA security requirements; embed threat modelling, least privilege, and lifecycle attestations from the outset.
obligation: n/a (provided); ENISA proposal, adoption not recorded
note: Attestation of product security. Nearest named actor: manufacturers ('Manufacturers must adjust their product lifecycles for compliance with the Cyber Resilience Act'). To whom attestations go and with what consequence: not stated. Covers products generally; AI is not singled out.
basis: AI pass B; different cell in pass A

quote: The latte r, in turn, refers to the obligation of the controller to provide meaningful information to data subjects.
obligation: statutory duty mentioned but not addressed
note: Answers to: data subjects. Consequence not stated. The document says it addresses only interpretability and explainability ('The present document addresses the former two notions'), not transparency.

quote: The AI system is auditable.
note: One of the outcomes explainability is 'necessary to ensure, among other considerations'. Others listed: the organisation can trust the system, errors and biases can be identified, the organisation can detect misuse, decision-making criteria match the organisation's objectives. Auditor and to whom: not stated.

quote: the controller must implement measures to actually rectify or erase the personal data it identified.
note: Redress route. Answers to: data subjects exercising access (Art. 17), rectification (Art. 16), erasure (Art. 19), restriction (Art. 20), portability (Art. 22) and objection (Art. 23). Consequence not stated. The section covers only cross-cutting technical issues, not all rights provisions.

quote: the controller must both identify whether and where personal data are used during the training phase, and assess whether the model, when answering certain prompts, might leak that data when making inferences.
location: p.36, s.5.5.1 Risk 1: Incomplete identification of the personal data processed
note: Trigger: a data subject's request to exercise rights. Two checks: where personal data were used in training; whether the model may leak them at inference. Answers to: the data subject.
basis: AI pass A; different cell in pass B

quote: The training personal datasets should include metadata so that the relevant records or files including personal data can be more easily identified
note: Serves the right of access. Metadata on sources, collection methods and pre-processing steps (cleaning, pseudonymisation, augmentation). Coded under Accountability because it serves data subject rights; it is also a recording measure.
basis: AI pass A; different cell in pass B

quote: When machine un-learning is not viable, output filtering can be used.
note: Measures to give effect to erasure or rectification inside models: machine unlearning (exact: retrain from scratch, costly; approximate: may not fully remove), otherwise output filtering (real-time scanning to block personal data in responses). Coded as Accountability because they serve data subject redress.
basis: AI pass A; different cell in pass B

quote: Ultimately, controllers remain fully responsible for performing their own comprehensive compliance
note: Continues p.40: 'assessments, complementing this framework with the necessary legal analysis, and ensuring that their decisions are consistent with the EUDPR'. Named accountable role: the controller. To whom and consequence: not stated.

quote: EUIs are responsible for identifying and mitigating risks to these rights and freedoms raised by their processing activities, and to demonstrate how they did so.
