quote: a Board composed of representatives of the Member States, a scientific panel to integrate the scientific community and an advisory forum to contribute stakeholder input to the implementation of this Regulation, at Union and national level, should be established
note: Governance framework 'to coordinate and support the application of this Regulation at national level'. The AI Office's mission (set by Commission Decision) not coded: report of another instrument / a body's own mandate.

quote: The Board should be responsible for a number of advisory tasks, including issuing opinions, recommendations, advice or contributing to guidance on matters related to the implementation of this Regulation
note: Advisory, not authority: it advises the Commission, the Member States and national competent authorities. Members are representatives from public entities 'who should have the relevant competences and powers to facilitate coordination at national level'. The Board 'should also cooperate' with Union bodies, expert groups and networks.

quote: The Board should establish two standing sub-groups to provide a platform for cooperation and exchange among market surveillance authorities and notifying authorities
note: The market surveillance sub-group acts as the administrative cooperation group (ADCO) under Art. 30 of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020. The Board 'may establish other standing or temporary sub-groups'. Cross-ref Coordination/Resources (Commission support, Recital 149).

quote: an advisory forum should be established to advise and provide technical expertise to the Board and the Commission.
note: A stakeholder channel into EU governance, with 'a varied and balanced stakeholder representation between commercial and non-commercial interest'. Advisory.

quote: each Member State should designate a market surveillance authority to act as a single point of contact.
note: Contact point 'vis-à-vis the public and other counterparts at Member State and Union levels'.

quote: The market surveillance authorities and the Commission should be able to propose joint activities, including joint investigations, to be conducted by market surveillance authorities or market surveillance authorities jointly with the Commission
holder: The market surveillance authorities and the Commission
note: For categories of high-risk AI systems found to present a serious risk across two or more Member States; aims: promoting compliance, identifying non-compliance, raising awareness, guidance. Per Art. 9 of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020. Also coded Coordination/Resources.

quote: should cooperate with the AI Office to carry out evaluations of compliance and inform the Board and other market surveillance authorities accordingly
note: Applies to general-purpose AI systems usable directly by deployers for at least one high-risk purpose. MSAs may request AI Office assistance where they cannot access information on the underlying GPAI model; mutual assistance under Ch. VI of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 applies mutatis mutandis.

quote: the scientific panel should support the monitoring activities of the AI Office and may, in certain cases, provide qualified alerts to the AI Office which trigger follow-ups, such as investigations
note: Triggers: panel suspects a GPAI model poses a concrete and identifiable risk at Union level, or meets criteria for classification as systemic risk. Also coded Accountability/Resources.

quote: all parties involved in the application of this Regulation should respect the confidentiality of information and data obtained in carrying out their tasks
holder: all parties involved in the application of this Regulation
note: Condition on information exchange, 'to ensure trustful and constructive cooperation of competent authorities on Union and national level'. Protects IP, trade secrets, public and national security, integrity of proceedings, classified information. Operative Art. 78 (outside this part).

quote: It is of particular importance that the Commission carry out appropriate consultations during its preparatory work, including at expert level
note: Per Interinstitutional Agreement on Better Law-Making (13 April 2016); Parliament and Council receive all documents with Member States' experts and access Commission expert group meetings.

quote: Member States shall notify those rules to the Commission at the latest 30 days following the adoption thereof.
note: Trigger: adoption of national authorisation rules.

quote: the identity and the contact details of the provider and, where applicable, of its authorised representative
if_not_met: Not stated here. Breach of Art. 16(a): fines up to EUR 15 000 000 or 3% (Art. 99(4)(a), outside this part).
note: Contact point between provider and deployer, in the instructions for use.

quote: the Commission and the Member States should facilitate the drawing up of voluntary codes of conduct to advance AI literacy
holder: the Commission and the Member States
obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital, 'should facilitate'); the codes themselves are voluntary
note: Done 'In cooperation with the relevant stakeholders'. Shared voluntary instruments connecting public and private actors on AI literacy.

quote: the handling of communication with national competent authorities, other relevant authorities, including those providing or supporting the access to data, notified bodies, other operators, customers or other interested parties
if_not_met: Not stated here. Art. 16(c) breach: Art. 99(4)(a) (outside this part).
note: Required QMS element on communication with authorities, notified bodies, operators and customers.

quote: They shall inform the distributors of the high-risk AI system concerned and, where applicable, the deployers, the authorised representative and importers accordingly.
if_not_met: Not stated here. Art. 16(j) breach: Art. 99(4)(a) (outside this part).
note: Notifies the value chain, including deployers, of corrective action.

quote: providers established in third countries shall, by written mandate, appoint an authorised representative which is established in the Union
if_not_met: Not stated here; 'no authorised representative has been appointed' is formal non-compliance under Art. 83(1)(f) (outside this part): MSA requires remedy, then restricts, prohibits, recalls or withdraws.
note: Creates an EU-based contact point for non-EU providers of high-risk systems, 'Prior to making their high-risk AI systems available on the Union market'. Provider must enable the representative to perform its tasks (22(2)).
basis: AI pass B; different cell in pass A

quote: The mandate shall empower the authorised representative to be addressed, in addition to or instead of the provider, by the competent authorities, on all issues related to ensuring compliance with this Regulation.
holder: The authorised representative (mandated by the provider)
if_not_met: Not stated here. Art. 99(4)(b) (outside this part).
note: EU contact point for competent authorities.
basis: AI pass A; different cell in pass B

quote: That initial provider shall closely cooperate with new providers and shall make available the necessary information and provide the reasonably expected technical access and other assistance
note: Not applicable where the initial provider clearly specified its system is not to be changed into a high-risk system. Without prejudice to IP and trade secrets (25(5)). Also coded Delivery/Resources.

quote: The provider of a high-risk AI system and the third party that supplies an AI system, tools, services, components, or processes that are used or integrated in a high-risk AI system shall, by written agreement, specify the necessary information
holder: The provider of a high-risk AI system and the third party that supplies an AI system, tools, services, components, or processes
note: Supplier contracts: specify information, capabilities, technical access and assistance 'based on the generally acknowledged state of the art' so the provider can comply. Not for free and open-source tools other than general-purpose AI models.

quote: Those procedures shall be developed in cooperation between the notifying authorities of all Member States.
holder: the notifying authorities of all Member States
note: Cross-national cooperation on designation procedures.

quote: Notifying authorities shall notify the Commission and the other Member States, using the electronic notification tool developed and managed by the Commission, of each conformity assessment body referred to in paragraph 1.
note: Notification includes activities, modules, AI types and attestation of competence; without accreditation, documentary evidence and monitoring arrangements (30(3)). Also coded Coordination/Resources.

quote: Notified bodies shall participate in coordination activities as referred to in Article 38.
if_not_met: Not stated here. Art. 99(4)(f) (outside this part).
note: Also take part in, or be represented in, European standardisation organisations, or keep up to date with standards.

quote: The Commission shall make publicly available the list of the bodies notified under this Regulation, including their identification numbers and the activities for which they have been notified.
note: Public register of notified bodies, kept up to date; Commission assigns a single identification number to each (35(1)). Also a publication (Accountability) element.

quote: The notifying authority shall notify the Commission and the other Member States of any relevant changes to the notification of a notified body via the electronic notification tool referred to in Article 30(2).
note: Extensions of scope follow Arts 29-30 procedures (36(2)).

quote: it shall inform the notifying authority and the providers concerned as soon as possible and, in the case of a planned cessation, at least one year before ceasing its activities
note: Trigger: notified body decides to cease activities. Certificates may stay valid nine months if another notified body confirms in writing it assumes responsibility and completes a full assessment; notifying authority withdraws the designation.

quote: appropriate coordination and cooperation between notified bodies active in the conformity assessment procedures pursuant to this Regulation are put in place and properly operated in the form of a sectoral group of notified bodies
note: Commission 'shall ensure'. 38(2): each notifying authority ensures its bodies participate, directly or through representatives.

quote: The Commission shall provide for the exchange of knowledge and best practices between notifying authorities.
note: Network among notifying authorities.

quote: When preparing a standardisation request, the Commission shall consult the Board and relevant stakeholders, including the advisory forum.
note: Consultation step in standard-setting.

quote: When drafting the common specifications, the Commission shall consult the advisory forum referred to in Article 67.
note: 41(2): Commission informs the committee under Art. 22 of Regulation (EU) No 1025/2012 before drafting.

quote: it shall inform the Commission thereof with a detailed explanation. The Commission shall assess that information and, if appropriate, amend the implementing act establishing the common specification concerned.
holder: a Member State (informs); the Commission (assesses, may amend)
note: Trigger: Member State considers a common specification does not entirely meet the requirements.

quote: Each notified body shall provide the other notified bodies carrying out similar conformity assessment activities covering the same types of AI systems with relevant information on issues relating to negative and, on request, positive conformity assessment results.
note: 45(2): inform other notified bodies of refused, suspended or withdrawn approvals and certificates. 45(4): confidentiality.

quote: The market surveillance authority shall inform the Commission and the other Member States of any authorisation issued pursuant to paragraphs 1 and 2.
note: Excludes sensitive operational data of law-enforcement authorities.

quote: Prior to placing a general-purpose AI model on the Union market, providers established in third countries shall, by written mandate, appoint an authorised representative which is established in the Union.
holder: providers established in third countries (of general-purpose AI models)
if_not_met: Not stated here. Fines under Art. 101 (outside this part; see Recital 169).
note: EU contact point for non-EU model providers. 54(6): not for qualifying open-source models 'unless the general-purpose AI models present systemic risks'.
basis: AI pass B; different cell in pass A

quote: The AI Office shall encourage and facilitate the drawing up of codes of practice at Union level in order to contribute to the proper application of this Regulation, taking into account international approaches.
note: Codes are a means for GPAI providers to show compliance (Arts 53(4), 55(2)). 56(8): AI Office also encourages review and adaptation of codes and assists in assessing available standards.
basis: AI pass A; different cell in pass B

quote: The AI Office may invite all providers of general-purpose AI models, as well as relevant national competent authorities, to participate in the drawing-up of codes of practice.
note: 'Civil society organisations, industry, academia and other relevant stakeholders, such as downstream providers and independent experts, may support the process.' 56(7): AI Office may invite providers to adhere; non-systemic providers may limit adherence to Art. 53.

quote: Member States shall ensure an appropriate level of cooperation between the authorities supervising those other sandboxes and the national competent authorities.
note: Also: 'Where appropriate, national competent authorities shall cooperate with other relevant authorities, and may allow for the involvement of other actors within the AI ecosystem.'

quote: pursuant to a specific sandbox plan agreed between the providers or prospective providers and the competent authority
holder: the providers or prospective providers and the competent authority
note: Formal agreement linking provider and authority (sandbox plan defined in Art. 3(54)). Sandboxes may include supervised real-world testing.

quote: the exit reports and the written proof provided by the national competent authority shall be taken positively into account by market surveillance authorities and notified bodies
holder: market surveillance authorities and notified bodies
note: Links sandbox outcomes to later checks, 'with a view to accelerating conformity assessment procedures to a reasonable extent'.

quote: the Commission and the Board shall be authorised to access the exit reports and shall take them into account, as appropriate, when exercising their tasks under this Regulation
note: Subject to Art. 78 confidentiality and the provider's agreement.

quote: the national data protection authorities and those other national or competent authorities are associated with the operation of the AI regulatory sandbox and involved in the supervision of those aspects
note: Verb: shall ensure. Links the sandbox to data protection authorities and other supervisors where systems process personal data. Sandboxes cover AI systems under development, including those developed by a public authority (Art. 59(1)(a)) [inference: relevant to public-sector tools before deployment]. Art. 57(1)-(9) begin before this part's line range and are not coded here.

quote: and shall inform the AI Office of such decision.
note: The decision is a suspension of testing or of sandbox participation. Also coded Decision-making/Design.

quote: The AI regulatory sandboxes shall be designed and implemented in such a way that, where relevant, they facilitate cross-border cooperation between national competent authorities.
note: Passive. Nearest named actors: national competent authorities that establish sandboxes.

quote: National competent authorities shall coordinate their activities and cooperate within the framework of the Board.
note: Board = European Artificial Intelligence Board (Art. 65).

quote: National competent authorities shall inform the AI Office and the Board of the establishment of a sandbox
note: Notification. Also coded Delivery/Resources (support and guidance on request) and Coordination/Design (public list).

quote: The AI Office shall make publicly available a list of planned and existing sandboxes and keep it up to date
note: Purpose stated: 'to encourage more interaction in the AI regulatory sandboxes and cross-border cooperation'. A public register; could also be read as Accountability (publication).

quote: The Commission shall proactively coordinate with national competent authorities, where relevant.
note: Also coded Coordination/Resources (single interface).

quote: providers and prospective providers may also submit applications in partnerships with deployers and other relevant third parties
holder: Providers and prospective providers (applying with deployers and other third parties)
note: [inference] Allows a public-sector deployer to enter a sandbox jointly with its supplier. Same point also requires broad and equal access.

quote: AI regulatory sandboxes facilitate the involvement of other relevant actors within the AI ecosystem, such as notified bodies and standardisation organisations
obligation: statutory duty (content the implementing acts 'shall ensure')
note: List continues: SMEs, enterprises, innovators, testing and experimentation facilities, research labs, European Digital Innovation Hubs, centres of excellence, individual researchers, 'in order to allow and facilitate cooperation with the public and private sectors'. Nearest named actor: national competent authorities.

quote: participation in an AI regulatory sandbox established by a Member State, or by the European Data Protection Supervisor is mutually and uniformly recognised and carries the same legal effects across the Union
obligation: statutory duty (content the implementing acts 'shall ensure')
note: Mutual recognition across Member States. The EDPS can run a sandbox [inference: for Union institutions, bodies, offices and agencies]. Also requires simple, intelligible procedures streamlined across the Union.

quote: Where appropriate, they shall cooperate with other national competent authorities with a view to ensuring consistent practices across the Union.
note: Also coded Decision-making/Design.

quote: the provider or prospective provider and the deployer or prospective deployer shall conclude an agreement specifying their roles and responsibilities
holder: Provider or prospective provider; deployer or prospective deployer
note: Supplier-deployer agreement 'with a view to ensuring compliance with the provisions for testing in real world conditions'. [inference] Where the deployer is a public body this is a contractual link with its supplier. Also coded Decision-making/Resources (information to deployers).

quote: facilitate the participation of SMEs and other relevant stakeholders in the standardisation development process.
note: Connects SMEs and stakeholders to standard setting.

quote: Member States shall facilitate the tasks entrusted to the AI Office, as reflected in this Regulation.
note: Links Member States to the AI Office; content of 'facilitate' not specified.

quote: The Board shall be composed of one representative per Member State. The European Data Protection Supervisor shall participate as observer.
note: Cross-government group established by Art. 65(1). AI Office attends without voting; other national and Union authorities, bodies or experts may be invited case by case. Representatives designated for three years, renewable once (Art. 65(3)).

quote: are designated as a single contact point vis-à-vis the Board and, where appropriate, taking into account Member States’ needs, as a single contact point for stakeholders
note: Contact point. Verb: Member States 'shall ensure'.

quote: are empowered to facilitate consistency and coordination between national competent authorities in their Member State as regards the implementation of this Regulation
note: Includes 'the collection of relevant data and information for the purpose of fulfilling their tasks on the Board'. Verb: Member States 'shall ensure'.

quote: The Board shall establish two standing sub-groups to provide a platform for cooperation and exchange among market surveillance authorities and notifying authorities
note: The market surveillance sub-group 'should act as the administrative cooperation group (ADCO)' under Art. 30 Regulation (EU) 2019/1020. The Board may set up other sub-groups; advisory forum representatives may be invited as observers. Art. 65(7): Board to safeguard objectivity and impartiality.

quote: The Board shall advise and assist the Commission and the Member States in order to facilitate the consistent and effective application of this Regulation.
note: Advisory, not authority. Listed tasks ('may in particular') include (a) contributing to coordination among NCAs and supporting joint market surveillance activities, (b) sharing expertise and best practices, (h) cooperating with other Union bodies, (i) cooperation with third countries.

quote: contribute to the coordination among national competent authorities responsible for the application of this Regulation
note: Chapeau: 'The Board shall advise and assist the Commission and the Member States'. Also supports joint market surveillance activities (Art. 74(11)) with the agreement of the authorities concerned; (b) collects and shares expertise and best practices among Member States.

quote: at the request of the Commission or on its own initiative, issue recommendations and written opinions on any relevant matters related to the implementation of this Regulation
note: Advisory input, incl. (vii) 'on the potential need for amendment to Annex III in accordance with Article 7' and on revising Art. 5; also on codes, standards, the EU database and serious incident reports. Advising is not authority; could also be read as Decision-making/Resources.
basis: AI pass B; different cell in pass A

quote: facilitate the development of common criteria and a shared understanding among market operators and competent authorities of the relevant concepts provided for in this Regulation, including by contributing to the development of benchmarks
note: Shared criteria and benchmarks across operators and authorities.
basis: AI pass A; different cell in pass B

quote: cooperate, as appropriate, with other Union institutions, bodies, offices and agencies, as well as relevant Union expert groups and networks
note: Fields: product safety, cybersecurity, competition, digital and media services, financial services, consumer protection, data and fundamental rights protection. (i) cooperation with third-country authorities and international organisations.

quote: facilitate cooperation and information-sharing among AI regulatory sandboxes
note: Also assists the AI Office in supporting national competent authorities to establish and develop sandboxes.

quote: receive opinions by the Member States on qualified alerts regarding general-purpose AI models, and on national experiences and practices on the monitoring and enforcement of AI systems
note: Two-way channel: (n) provides opinions to the Commission on qualified alerts about general-purpose AI models.

quote: The membership of the advisory forum shall represent a balanced selection of stakeholders, including industry, start-ups, SMEs, civil society and academia.
note: Advisory body to 'provide technical expertise and advise the Board and the Commission' (67(1)). 'The Commission shall appoint the members' (67(3)). Meets at least twice a year; may give opinions on request (67(7)-(8)).

quote: Member States shall designate a market surveillance authority to act as the single point of contact for this Regulation
note: Contact point. Member States also communicate the identity and tasks of their authorities to the Commission and 'make publicly available information on how competent authorities and single points of contact can be contacted' by 2 August 2025; 'The Commission shall make a list of the single points of contact publicly available'.

quote: must be notified  to the relevant market surveillance authority and the national data protection authority. Notification must take place after each use
holder: not stated in para 409 (passive); nearest: the deployer (law enforcement authority), per para 419
note: Notification channel linking deployers to market surveillance and data protection authorities, which feeds their annual reports to the Commission (para 419) and the Commission's annual reports (para 423). Also coded Accountability/Design.

quote: employers shall also consult with workers or their representatives, conform national procedures. Without respecting these procedural requirements, such systems cannot be introduced by reference to the AI Act as such.
obligation: statutory duty under other law, as stated by the guidelines ('shall')
if_not_met: 'such systems cannot be introduced by reference to the AI Act as such'
note: Consultation mechanism linking the employer with workers or their representatives before emotion recognition is introduced for medical or safety reasons. The footnote also says such systems 'will require also consent' under data protection law. Borderline report of another instrument; coded because it conditions introduction of the tool.

quote: ‘On behalf of’ means that a law enforcement authority has delegated the performance of a law enforcement activity (or part of it) to another entity or person, including private parties
holder: law enforcement authorities; entities or persons acting on their behalf, including private parties
note: Delegation or case-specific request linking a law enforcement authority with another body. Examples: public transport companies, sports federations, banks acting under police instructions and supervision. Entities acting 'on their own behalf' (e.g. against fraud) are not covered. Also coded: Decision-making/Design (instruct and supervise).

quote: If other actors are acting on behalf of the deployer/the law enforcement authority, they will have to contribute to the preparation of the FRIA with all relevant information to ensure it is properly carried out.
holder: other actors acting on behalf of the deployer / the law enforcement authority
note: Information flow from delegated actors to the deployer. The FRIA duty itself stays with the deployer.

quote: RBI systems used for the purpose of law enforcement will be registered in a se cure non -public section of the database, with limited information and limited access to that information.
note: EU database as a register linking deployers to EU-level oversight; for law enforcement RBI it is non-public with limited access, so it does not serve publication. Who may access it is not stated. Also coded Accountability/Design (registration duty).
basis: AI pass B; different cell in pass A

quote: Each use of an RBI system pursuing one of the objectives listed in Article 5(1)(h)(i)-(iii) AI Act must be notified  to the relevant market surveillance authority and the national data protection authority.
note: Notification channel. Trigger: after each use. Content: at minimum the Art. 5(6) information; no 'sensitive operational data' (Art. 3(38)). The 'i)-' and '(iii)' across a line break are joined without a space. Also coded: Accountability/Design (para 409).

quote: Prior to its adoption, Member States are also encouraged to send a preliminary version of the national (or regional) law proposed to the AI Office.
note: Voluntary pre-adoption exchange with the AI Office. What the AI Office does with drafts is not stated.

quote: Member States shall notify their national laws to the Commission at the latest 30 days following the adoption thereof .
if_not_met: non-notification to the AI Office within the legal deadline of 30 days following the adoption  set out in Article 5(5) may imply that the national law is unenforceable in legal proceedings
note: Notification channel to the Commission / AI Office. 'Such notification does not provide a presumption of conformity'. The AI Office 'will send a confirmation of receipt'. Draft-sharing and publication coded as separate entries (para 414).
basis: AI pass A; different cell in pass B

quote: the description of any cooperation with private or public authorities, including in other countries, and data transfers and exchanges;
obligation: suggested content for national law; non-binding
note: Cross-body and cross-border cooperation and data exchange to be described in requests. Same list: 'any need for formal notifications upon granting/refusal of the authorisation'.

quote: The Commission encourages providers and deployers of AI systems, national market surveillance authorities through the AI Board, the AI Advisory forum, the research community, and civil society organisations to contribute to this process by responding to future calls for public consultation.
holder: providers and deployers of AI systems; national market surveillance authorities through the AI Board; the AI Advisory forum; the research community; civil society organisations
note: Consultation channel feeding the review of the Guidelines; national authorities are routed through the AI Board.

quote: When those international agreements are revised or new ones are concluded in the future, the contracting parties should make utmost efforts to align those agreements with the requirements of th e AI Act.
holder: Contracting parties to international law-enforcement and judicial cooperation agreements
note: Formal mechanism connecting actors: international agreements. Trigger: revision or conclusion of agreements.

quote: In their contractual relationships with deployers (i.e. in the terms  of use of the AI system), providers are also expected to exclude use of their AI system for prohibited practices
note: Formal mechanism connecting provider and deployer: terms of use (supplier contract). Para 41: providers of general-purpose systems 'may nevertheless explicitly exclude such prohibited use in their terms of use'. Cross-ref para 14: the exclusion in the terms does not relieve the deployer (Accountability/Design entry).

quote: it enables effective cooperation between the competent authorities responsible for the enforcement of the AI Act and the authorities protecting fundamental rights pursuant to  Article 77 AI Act and other provisions of the AI Act.
holder: Competent authorities responsible for enforcing the AI Act; authorities protecting fundamental rights
obligation: statutory (enabling provision; Treaty duty to cooperate sincerely)
note: Formal link between AI Act enforcers and fundamental-rights authorities. The paragraph adds: 'in accordance with Article 4(3) TEU, the various authorities concerned are bound to cooperate sincerely when giving effect to their respective tasks under Union law.' The form of cooperation is not specified.

quote: Where there are cross-border implications beyond the territory of the market surveillance authority, the authority of the Member State concerned must inform the Commission and the market surveillance authorities  of other Member States .
holder: Market surveillance authority of the Member State concerned
note: Notification mechanism. Trigger: cross-border implications. Part of the AI Act procedure for AI systems presenting a risk at national level, which the document calls 'particularly relevant in the context of enforcing the prohibitions'. Cross-ref Decision-making/Design entry (Union safeguard procedure).

quote: national market surveillance authorities should also strive for a harmonized application of the prohibitions for comparable cases that do not cross the Member State’s territory by drawing inspiration from these Guidelines and cooperating within the AI Board.
note: Coordination mechanism: the AI Board (cross-government network) and the Guidelines as a shared reference. Trigger: comparable domestic cases. Cross-ref Coordination/Resources entry (para 4).

quote: In conformity with EU employment law, if such new technologies are introduced, employers shall also consult with workers or their representatives, conform national procedures.
obligation: statutory duty under other law ('shall'), restated in a footnote
if_not_met: Without respecting these procedural requirements, such systems cannot be introduced by reference to the AI Act as such.
note: Consultation mechanism linking employer and workers or their representatives. Footnote also says such systems 'will require also consent from the point of view of data protection legislation' (pointer to other law).

quote: Member States can and should learn from the successes and failures of these policies.
obligation: recommended ('can and should'; 'it is highly recommended')
note: Context: 'Monitoring the uptake of these strategies is extremely important'. Insights from successful initiatives, such as procurement processes and training programmes, should be shared to support policy learning. [scope doubt] Concerns national strategies for AI in government, not individual tools.

quote: co-creation and iteration -based development approaches  should be promoted to stimulate and reinforce active citizen involvement.
note: Connects citizens with those who build AI-enabled public services. 'This should be considered throughout the evolution process, from design to development, from testing to use, up to evaluation to allow iterative feedback'. Citizen participation may help identify 'potential biases in data'. Holder not stated: Annex 1 marks leading and contributing roles by shading, which the text does not keep. See also Decision-making/Design (government strategies) and Coordination/Design (representativeness).

quote: This int ervention should start with the setting up of a coordinated governance approach to identify, discuss, regulate and implement underpinning common values, needs and issues of interest to all stakeholders.
note: A coordinating mechanism. 'Regulate' implies some decision-making, but no body or authority is named. Holder not stated. See the Rec 2.1 entries.

quote: Setting up a European registry of AI algorithms by federating and promoting the creation of national registries to monitor the development and market around AI and help in meeting the relevant criteria set down by EU regulations.
obligation: suggested option ('could be taken into consideration')
note: Stated purpose: to monitor development and the market around AI, and to help meet criteria set by EU regulations. It is not framed as mandatory registration or as public transparency, so it is not coded as Accountability [inference: it could be read as registration]. Repeated in Rec 3.2, 3.4 and 4.1, each coded. Holder not stated (Annex 1 shading lost).

quote: Setting up an Artificial Intelligence Working Group  at European level  specifically dedicated to the public sector.
note: The Working Group 'would facilitate the coordination of policies and initiatives amongst EU institutions and European countries'. Its mandate 'could include coordination with institutional data governance bodies, mobilisation and sharing of resources amongst actors, and the transposition of ethical principles and regulations'. It acts by 'suggesting policy initiatives' and 'proposing concrete actions'. That role is advisory, so it is not coded as Decision-making. The text also says 'the setting up of joint governance mechanisms and coordination frameworks is needed.' Holder not stated; nearest: EU institutions.

quote: Member States should identify organisations at the national level  to represent AI in the public sector within the EU Working Group.
note: The designated bodies 'would act as both coordinators amongst national public administrations within their country and as the interface between national governments and EU institutions', that is, as contact points.

quote: the setting up of a shared governance mechanism  for developing and exchanging dedicated learning material around common needs.
obligation: suggested option ('what could provide great value')
note: A mechanism for producing and exchanging learning material. It serves capacity building (Resources). Holder not stated.

quote: interfacing experimenting facilities  at the national and local levels with international/cross -border facilities and networks, which would also require the development of common criteria for cross-operationalisation.
note: Links national and local experimentation facilities with international and cross-border facilities and networks. Holder not stated.

quote: Create an AI research and knowledge alliance of European universities  and other research and development institutions working with the public se ctor to promote the development of a common agenda and dedicated curricula for research
holder: not stated (who creates it); European universities and other research and development institutions (members)
note: A network linking research institutions with the public sector. Its aims include research on 'how to stimulate the use and assess the impact of AI in government'. [scope doubt] Concerns the research ecosystem, not the governance of a tool.

quote: Promote the implementation of a Common European Data Space 63 dedicated to public administrations providing not only data collected by the public sector, but also other relevant data acquired from both established and emerging actors
note: Shared data infrastructure linking public administrations (as data providers and users) with private actors (B2G data). It 'should not be a central repository' but 'an open and interactive window to promote access to non-sensitive data', 'including access to data to train or run AI applications'. Also a data resource. [scope doubt]

quote: Create AI algorithm registries , using catalogues of AI -enabled applications (for example, through the AI -on-demand platform), and by supporting public administrations in procuring trustworthy AI (activities coordinated by the living-in.EU68 movement).
note: Introduced as an action that the 2021 revision of the AI Coordinated Plan 'calls for'. The handbook adopts it as its own action (listed in Annex 1), so it is coded although it is partly a report. It also supports public administrations in procuring trustworthy AI. Nearby (p. 38), the city of Amsterdam's AI registry 'for transparency purposes' and its contract clauses are described as good practice; this is practice and not coded. See the registry entries for Rec 2.1, 3.4 and 4.1.

quote: Extend the setting up of the Networks of Local Digital Twins  to include cities as an impactful exercise in support of public sector resource efficiency.
note: A network of AI-enabled local digital twins. It responds to the Member States' Digital Day 2021 commitment, which is a report. [scope doubt] Promotes adoption.

quote: Dedicated European Data Spaces should grant t he necessary conditions for data access and governance
holder: Dedicated European Data Spaces (operators not named)
note: The conditions continue: data usable 'in an automatic fashion, with secured and transparent access, and in line with ethics and related access and use conditions.' The holder is the data space itself; its operators are not named. [scope doubt]

quote: There is also the need to identify and activate reference organisations for data trust and data cooperatives  to accommodate emerging forms of social innovation initiatives stemming from civil society
note: Annex 1: 'Establish and activate reference organisations for data trust and data cooperatives'. [scope doubt] Concerns the data governance ecosystem; only indirectly related to AI tools.

quote: Promote EU GovTech start -ups71  that would bring  innovative solutions to public services
note: The supplier ecosystem for public services. [scope doubt] Market development rather than governance of a tool.

quote: For the development of AI solutions reuse and sharing of components with other public administrations on open repositories  should be privileged, following the existing building blocks and guidelines developed within the relevant EU initiatives.
note: Sharing AI components between public administrations through open repositories. Holder not stated; nearest: public administrations developing AI solutions.

quote: Aligning components specifications to the areas they address (e.g., transportation, housing, etc.), so that dedicated directories  would help operators reuse existing component in other parts of Europe.
holder: GovTech initiatives working for different public administrations
note: Directories to help operators reuse components. Cross-reference Rec 3.5.

quote: Build an EU united AI registry based on national and local AI registries , adding (when available) the information and linking to the reusable parts involved: algorithms, models and datasets.
holder: not stated (the grammatical subject is the shared repositories of plug-and-play algorithms: 'These repositories could')
note: A registry of reusable parts: algorithms, models and datasets. See the registry entries for Rec 2.1, 3.2 and 4.1. Annex 1: 'Set up an EU AI registry based on local AI registries'.

quote: dedicated national repositories of standards, guidelines and performance metrics should be envisaged in combination with the above
note: Repositories as shared databases. 'Performance metrics' are not defined, and their use in evaluating tools is not stated (could serve Delivery).
basis: AI pass B; different cell in pass A

quote: Member States join forces and synchronise actions to support innovative GovTech companies that can provide innovative AI applications to the European public sector.
note: Support for GovTech suppliers. The text notes that the Commission has proposed to fund a GovTech Incubator under the Digital Europe Programme (a report). [scope doubt] Supplier market development.

quote: Public sector administrations are encouraged to keep abreast of and actively reach out to innovative companies whose available AI solutions could be beneficial to them.
note: Preceding: public administrations 'should envisage ways to become a more attractive market for GovTech companies and start-ups.' Connects public bodies with suppliers. [scope doubt]

quote: Specific procurement frameworks  and conditions dedicated to support start -ups could be envisaged
note: Example: use of Art. 32 of Directive 2014/24/EU during the pandemic (negotiated procedure without prior publication; footnote 80). Holder not stated. [scope doubt] Procurement to support start-ups.

quote: An EU observatory on AI dedicated to the public sector  could be set up. It would act as central hub of expertise to establish a community of practice, while joining up national observatories around Europe
note: It would act as a 'one-stop shop/central repository' where public bodies can follow developments and share knowledge, and 'should be interactive and open to the community'. It collects success and failure stories; footnote 81 is coded as Accountability. Also coded Delivery/Design (monitoring).

quote: it would be in the interest of the different stakeholders to keep it updated by conveying state- of-the-art information to the observatory’s managing authority on a regular basis.
obligation: not an obligation: framed as stakeholders' interest ('it would be in the interest')
note: Information flows to the observatory's managing authority, which is not named. Trigger: 'on a regular basis'. No answerability or consequence is stated, so this is coded Coordination rather than Accountability [inference].

quote: EU Member States could identify relevant bodies that would act as AI national observatories to represent their country, and actively p articipate in the activities of the EU Observatory
note: National observatories would represent their country in the EU observatory, forming 'a pan-European network of AI observatories dedicated to the public sector'.

quote: Setting up of a European registry of AI algorithms  by uniting and promoting the creation of interoperable national registries  to monitor digital transformation of both the public sector and the market around AI, to share relevant information
note: Purposes: to monitor the digital transformation of the public sector and the AI market, to share information, and to 'help to meet the relevant criteria set down by EU regulations'. 'The registries of algorithms could coincide and/or be hosted by the AI observatories themselves.' See the registry entries for Rec 2.1, 3.2 and 3.4. Not framed as a public transparency or mandatory registration duty.

quote: Coordination with international organisations  already operating in this area (e.g., OECD84, UNESCO 85) on critical topics like ethics and trustworthiness
note: Coordination with the OECD and UNESCO 'to avoid duplication'. Footnotes point to the OECD.AI Policy Observatory and UNESCO's AI page.

quote: Promote active civic engagement , expressed under different forms of involvement of citizens in the management of public good when addressing common challenges and fundamental civil rights.
note: Citizen involvement as 'an indispensable resource' to complement institutional sources of information. Citizen Science and Citizen Generated Data 'can be directly deployed as an important contribution to ex ante and ex post impact assessment exercises' (p. 45).

quote: the representativeness of samples of citizens involved in co-creation needs to be appropriately considered, in order to avoid input from samples of citizens that are biased.
note: Preceding: 'the design of co-creation processes needs to be carefully prepared.' A condition on the co-creation mechanism. Holder not stated.

quote: They may rely on the marking solution implemented by an upstream model provider or a third party providing the solution (e.g. as an open standard or a specialised service) to the extent that the marking solution is compliant
holder: Providers of generative AI systems (may rely on); upstream model providers or third parties providing marking solutions
note: Links the system provider to upstream model providers and third-party marking services along the value chain. Marking can be applied post hoc, at model level or in inference (para (74)). Also coded as Accountability/Design (system provider keeps responsibility to demonstrate compliance) and Delivery/Resources (third-party solutions).

quote: The responsibilities of the market surveillance authorities under the AI Act do not affect the powers and tasks of other supervisory authorities or fundamental rights authorities under their own legal framework
holder: Market surveillance authorities; other supervisory authorities and fundamental rights authorities (e.g. data protection, consumer protection)
note: A demarcation rather than a connecting mechanism: no procedure for cooperation, referral or joint action between these authorities is set out here.

quote: providers of other GPAI models and of other generative AI models are also encouraged to implement appropriate transparency measures at the model level for the identification of interactive AI systems and the marking of AI-generated and manipulated content
holder: Providers of other GPAI models and of other generative AI models
obligation: encouraged; for GPAI models with systemic risk, may form part of a statutory mitigation duty
note: Value-chain coordination: 'particularly beneficial to facilitate compliance by downstream AI system providers with their obligations under Article 50(1) and (2)'. Where one provider supplies model and system, measures 'could also be implemented at the model level'. For systemic-risk GPAI models such measures 'may, where appropriate, constitute part of a broader set of mitigating measures' under Art. 55(1)(b). Para (24) similarly encourages providers of free and open-source components.
basis: AI pass B; different cell in pass A

quote: The use of standardised visual indicators, including across services of a provider, is recommended, since such indicators can significantly reduce cognitive burden and increase recognisability.
note: Shared/standardised disclosure signals. Para 34 also says providers 'are recommended to use standardised disclosure practices and labels' (pages 14-15, across a page break). No standard named.

quote: Perceptible marks and labels are not excluded as a complementary measure, where appropriate, with a view to facilitating the compliance of deployers with their obligation to label deep fakes
note: Provider-to-deployer support along the value chain. Deployers cannot rely on machine-readable marks alone for their own Art. 50(4) duty (para 117).

quote: To ens ure full interoperability, providers must rely on publicly-available industry standard detection solution s that allow any third party to implement detection
note: Shared standard across providers. Where no standard exists, providers may use their own, a third-party or a shared detection solution if interoperable; this possibility 'should be limited in time until harmoni sed standards and a standardi sed provider -agnostic interoperable detection solution emerge'. Quote keeps 'ens ure' and 'solution s'.

quote: it must ensure that the detection solution complies with Article 50(2) and (5) AI  Act and that those actors display the detection results in compliance with Article 50(5) AI Act
holder: Provider of the AI system that depends on another actor for detection
note: Supplier relationship: the provider must ensure third-party detection providers comply. Whether the provider can stop the third party is not stated; mechanism (contract etc.) not stated.

quote: The Commission encourages providers and deployers of AI  systems, national market surveillance authorities through the AI Board, the AI Advisory  forum, the research community, and civil society organisations to contribute to this  process
holder: European Commission (inviting providers, deployers, national market surveillance authorities through the AI Board, the AI Advisory forum, the research community and civil society organisations)
note: Mechanism: future public consultations; AI Board as channel for national authorities. Also coded with Decision-making/Design (review). 35 words.

quote: Deployers involved in complex content production and distribution value chains should take proportionate measures to ensure that the labelling of the content they have implemented pursuant to  Article 50(4) AI  Act is displayed
holder: Deployers involved in complex content production and distribution value chains
note: Mechanisms named: 'contractual conditions with distributing partners, user experience (UX) settings and interfaces to be displayed'. Links deployers with distributors.

quote: They are, therefore, strongly encouraged to preserve the marking and labelling implemented pursuant to Article 50 AI Act
holder: Providers of hosting services, including online platforms, or broadcasters
if_not_met: n/a: the text says these actors are 'Without being responsible and liable under the AI Act'
note: Distributors preserving marks along the chain. Para 17 encourages other professional disseminators similarly; para 98 again encourages online platforms and search engines to 'preserve and enable identification of the marks'.

quote: This is particularly beneficial to facilitate compliance by downstream AI system providers  with their obligations under Article 50(1) and (2) AI Act
holder: Providers of other GPAI models and of other generative AI models
note: Upstream-downstream link between model providers and system providers (who may be public bodies). Also coded as Delivery/Design.

quote: Relevant use cases must be identified, tested and validated through an inclusive process, involving the end-users.
location: p. 2 (=== page 2), Section II, 'Scope: AI at the service of Members and the administration', para 7
obligation: proposed: mandatory by policy (must), awaiting Bureau approval
note: Mechanism connecting developers and end-users (Members). Para 20: 'Engagement and inclusion of end-users in the development of AI solutions will ensure that AI remains human centric.' Also coded as Delivery/Design.

quote: Dependency on external experts or external service providers must be limited and monitored.
note: Governs the relationship with external suppliers (outside the state: private companies). Also coded as Delivery/Design for the monitoring element. Nearest named actor: the administration.

quote: It shall approve the AI roadmap as well as ensure a transversal involvement of the administration's services and end users.
note: Cross-service involvement. Also coded as Decision-making/Design (roadmap approval).

quote: The Governance Board shall include the ICT services and key representatives of Parliament's administration.
note: Composition of a cross-service body. Which representatives: not stated.
basis: AI pass A; different cell in pass B

quote: An AI roadmap should be established by the ICT services of the administration in cooperation with the Inter-DG network to support the development of Parliament's AI capability.
location: page 4, III. Implementation tools, AI Roadmap, para 19
holder: ICT services of the administration, in cooperation with the Inter-DG network
note: Joint drafting mechanism; the Board approves the roadmap (para 16). The roadmap 'should address the technical readiness, the assessment process, as well as the end-user engagement' (para 20).
basis: AI pass B; different cell in pass A

quote: The Governance Board shall establish, within the current Parliament ICT governance structures, a network of AI business partners.
note: Cross-DG network. Next sentence: it 'should facilitate the exchange of best practices, identify common challenges and foster the reuse of AI solutions.'

quote: Establish a charter for responsible data handling by IT providers using or developing AI solutions.
location: page 6, Secure and privacy compliant Artificial Intelligence, Requirements
note: Mechanism linking Parliament with its IT suppliers (outside the state: private companies) [inference]. Also coded as Decision-making/Design (setting a standard for providers). Who establishes the charter is not stated; nearest: Parliament's administration.

quote: Notified bodies shall accept the form for the purposes of the conformity assessment.
location: Art. 1(10), replacing AI Act Art. 11(1) second subpara.; p. 19
holder: Notified bodies; SMEs (including start-ups) and SMCs opting for the simplified form
note: Shared template connecting providers and notified bodies. 'Where an SME, including a start-up, or an SMC, opts to provide the information required in Annex IV in a simplified manner, it shall use the form'. Cross-ref Resources/Accountability (form) and Accountability/Design (Art. 11(1)).

quote: That initial provider shall closely cooperate with new providers and shall make available the necessary information and provide the reasonably expected technical access and other assistance that are required for the fulfilment of the obligations
location: Art. 1(12)(a), replacing AI Act Art. 25(2); pp. 19-20
holder: Initial provider of the AI system; new providers
if_not_met: administrative fines as referred to in AI Act Art. 99(4), new point (da) (Art. 1(38)(b)); amounts not stated in this document
note: Value chain: where the circumstances in Art. 25(1) occur (not restated here) the initial provider is no longer the provider. Includes (a) technical documentation 'sufficient to assess compliance', (b) 'informing the new providers about known limitations and failure modes', (c) targeted technical access incl. testing and validation. Does not apply where the initial provider 'has clearly specified that its AI system is not to be changed into a high-risk AI system'. [inference] Relevant where a public body becomes provider by modifying a system. Also coded Resources/Delivery.

quote: shall, by written agreement, specify the necessary information, capabilities, technical access and other assistance based on the generally acknowledged state of the art, in order to enable the provider of the high-risk AI system to fully comply
location: Art. 1(12)(b), replacing AI Act Art. 25(4) first subpara.; p. 20
holder: Provider of a high-risk AI system; third party supplying an AI system, AI model, tools, services, components or processes
if_not_met: administrative fines as referred to in Art. 99(4)(da)
note: Supplier contract. Exemption: third parties making tools, services, processes or components public under a free and open-source licence, 'other than general-purpose AI models'. [inference] Applies where a public body is provider of a high-risk system built from procured components or models.

quote: To that end, notifying authorities designated pursuant to this Regulation and those designated pursuant to the Union harmonisation legislation listed in Section A of Annex I shall cooperate in their assessments.
location: Art. 1(14), inserting AI Act Art. 28(8); p. 20
holder: Notifying authorities under the AI Act and under Annex I Section A legislation
note: Designation of notified bodies that assess high-risk AI. Notifying authorities 'shall ensure' a single application and unified assessment procedure where the sectoral legislation provides for one; also open to already designated notified bodies. A body designated under several Section A acts 'shall have to apply only once'. Procedure 'shall avoid any unnecessary duplications'.

quote: Notifying authorities shall notify the Commission and the other Member States, based on the list of codes, categories, and corresponding types of AI systems referred to in Annex XIV
location: Art. 1(16), replacing AI Act Art. 30(2); p. 21; Annex XIV, pp. 36-38
holder: Notifying authorities; conformity assessment bodies (Annex XIV point 4)
note: Notification of each conformity assessment body. Annex XIV codes (AIP, AIB, AIH, incl. AIH 0301 generative/GPAI-based systems and AIH 0401 'including Agentic AI') set the scope of designation. Annex XIV point 4: conformity assessment bodies 'shall use the lists of codes' in applications. Cross-ref Resources/Coordination (notification tool) and Decision-making/Design (delegated acts on Annex XIV).

quote: That AI regulatory sandbox shall be implemented in close cooperation with relevant competent authorities, in particular where compliance with Union legislation other than this Regulation is supervised in the AI regulatory sandbox
location: Art. 1(22)(c), inserting AI Act Art. 57(3a); p. 23
note: Cross-ref Resources/Delivery Art. 57(3a).

quote: pursuant to a specific sandbox plan agreed between the providers or prospective providers and the competent authorities, ensuring that appropriate safeguards are in place.
location: Art. 1(22)(d), replacing AI Act Art. 57(5); p. 23
holder: Providers or prospective providers; competent authorities
note: Agreed plan links provider and authority. 'Where applicable, the sandbox plan shall incorporate the real-world testing plan referred to in Articles 60 and 60a.' Sandboxes facilitate 'development, training, testing and validation' before market.
basis: AI pass B; different cell in pass A

quote: the competent data protection authorities and those other national or competent authorities are associated with the operation of the AI regulatory sandbox and involved in the supervision of those aspects to the extent of their respective tasks and powers.
location: Art. 1(22)(f), replacing AI Act Art. 57(10); p. 24
holder: National competent authorities (shall ensure); competent data protection authorities and other national or competent authorities
note: Trigger: sandbox AI systems involve personal data or fall under other authorities' remit, including authorities 'providing or supporting access to data'.

quote: National competent authorities, the European Data Protection Supervisor and the AI Office, shall, as appropriate and within their respective competences, coordinate their activities and cooperate within the framework of the Board.
location: Art. 1(22)(g), replacing AI Act Art. 57(14); p. 24
holder: National competent authorities; European Data Protection Supervisor; AI Office
note: Network/forum: the Board. 'They may support the joint establishment and operation of AI regulatory sandboxes, including in different sectors, and exchange best practices on related matters.'

quote: Each Member State shall notify the Commission of any real-world testing framework it adopts before implementing it.
location: Art. 1(25), inserting AI Act Art. 60a(3); p. 25
note: Notification to the Commission; trigger: before implementing. Does not affect the Commission's competences under Section B legislation.

quote: cooperate closely with each other in good faith and remove any practical obstacles, including on procedural rules providing access to physical public infrastructure
location: Art. 1(25), inserting AI Act Art. 60a(4); p. 25
holder: Member States (shall ensure); national competent authorities, relevant authorities and public authorities managing infrastructure and products under Annex I Section B legislation
note: Applies to Member States that have adopted real-world testing frameworks. Also coded Resources/Delivery (access to public infrastructure).

quote: Whenever national competent authorities intend to provide guidance and advice with regard to an AI system in areas covered by other Union law, the national competent authorities under that Union law shall be consulted, as appropriate.
location: Art. 1(29), replacing AI Act Art. 70(8); p. 26
note: Consultation between national authorities across regimes.

quote: The AI Office shall promptly transmit the relevant information to the market surveillance authority of the Member State in the territory of which the provider or its legal representative is situated.
location: Art. 1(31)(c), inserting AI Act Art. 75(1a); p. 27
note: Information flow on serious incidents from EU to national level. Cross-ref Accountability/Design Art. 75(1a).

quote: The authorities involved in the application of this Regulation shall cooperate actively with the AI Office and provide the AI Office the necessary assistance for the exercise of its powers
location: Art. 1(31)(c), inserting AI Act Art. 75(1b); p. 27
holder: Authorities involved in the application of the AI Act
note: Including assistance with inspections or enforcement in a Member State; those authorities 'shall enjoy the powers provided for pursuant to this Regulation and Regulation (EU) 2019/1020' for this purpose.

quote: When taking investigatory or enforcement action in the territory of a Member State that involves access to a public authority’s data or AI system, the AI Office shall be assisted by the relevant market surveillance authority.
location: Art. 1(31)(c), inserting AI Act Art. 75(1c); p. 27
holder: AI Office; relevant market surveillance authority
note: Directly addresses a public authority's AI system or data as the object of AI Office enforcement.

quote: the AI Office shall, without undue delay, notify the market surveillance authority competent for that market of its intention to take such a decision.
location: Art. 1(31)(c), inserting AI Act Art. 75(1d); p. 27
holder: AI Office; market surveillance authority competent for that market
note: 'The AI Office shall consult the authorities involved in the application of this Regulation, where appropriate, on any matter relating to the application and enforcement of this Regulation.' Cross-ref Decision-making/Design Art. 75(1d).

quote: it may request, through the relevant single point of contact designated in accordance with Article 70(2), the AI Office to assess the matter in order to take the necessary supervisory and enforcement measures
location: Art. 1(31)(d), inserting AI Act Art. 75(2a); p. 28
holder: Market surveillance authorities (request); single point of contact; AI Office
obligation: statutory power to request; AI Office must take 'utmost account'
note: Referral between bodies. Trigger: 'well-founded and sufficient reasons to suspect' infringement by a provider or deployer within Art. 75(1). Request 'duly reasoned' with name of provider or deployer, facts, provisions, negative effects, requesting authority. MSA shall cooperate and assist. Cross-ref Accountability/Design (AI Office reply within four months).

quote: Prior to conducting an inspection, the AI Office shall inform the market surveillance authority of the Member State in the territory of which the operator or its legal representative is situated.
location: Art. 1(32), inserting AI Act Art. 75a(4); p. 29
holder: AI Office; market surveillance authority; national competent authority (assistance if obstructed)
note: If obstructed, 'the national competent authority of the Member State concerned shall afford it the necessary assistance, requesting, where appropriate, the assistance of the police or an equivalent enforcement authority'.

quote: the competent market surveillance authority of a Member State may in its own territory carry out any investigation, inspection or other fact-finding measure on behalf and for the account of the AI Office
location: Art. 1(32), inserting AI Act Art. 75a(5); p. 30
holder: Competent market surveillance authority of a Member State; AI Office (requests)
note: Delegated fact-finding; national officials act under their national law.

quote: Information obtained as a result of such monitoring actions shall be shared with the relevant competent authorities of the Member States.
location: Art. 1(32), inserting AI Act Art. 75a(7); p. 30
note: Passive; nearest named actor: AI Office. Art. 75a(8): information 'shall be used only for the purpose of this Regulation'.

quote: Market surveillance authorities and public authorities or bodies referred to in paragraph 1 shall cooperate closely and provide each other with the mutual assistance necessary to fulfil their respective mandates
location: Art. 1(34)(c), inserting AI Act Art. 77(1b); p. 33
holder: Market surveillance authorities; national public authorities or bodies protecting fundamental rights
note: Includes 'exchange of information where necessary for the effective supervision or enforcement'.

quote: The Board shall adopt recommendations, taking into account European competence frameworks, to support the Commission and Member States in the promotion of AI literacy required under paragraph 1, including by setting out common objectives.
location: Art. 1(5), replacing AI Act Art. 4(3); p. 16
note: Verb: shall adopt recommendations. Advisory, not authority. Coded Coordination because common objectives align Commission and Member States; recital 8: the Board should 'ensure regular exchange between the Commission and Member States on the topic, while the Apply AI Alliance should allow discussion with the wider community'. Could also be read as Resources (guidance) serving Art. 4(2).
basis: AI pass A; different cell in pass B

quote: the AI Office and the competent national authorities should, in accordance with Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, coordinate their enforcement efforts with the authorities competent for the supervision and enforcement of Regulation (EU) 2022/2065, including the Commission
holder: AI Office; competent national authorities; authorities enforcing the Digital Services Act, including the Commission
note: For AI systems in very large online platforms/search engines. Respect loyal cooperation, proportionality and ne bis in idem; information used across Regulations 'only provided the undertaking agrees'; 'exchange views regularly' and take account of fines for the same conduct. DSA services 'may seek the opinion of the AI Office'.

quote: In order to enable AI innovation in the private and public sectors, it is important that the Commission and Member States’ competent authorities ensure that the supervision, enforcement and monitoring of sectoral and national laws do not create overlaps
holder: European Commission; Member States' competent authorities
note: Coordination aim across regimes: avoid overlaps, 'inconsistent interpretations or divergent enforcement'. Names the public sector.

quote: Where the AI Office finds that a natural or legal person opposes or obstructs an inspection, the national competent authority of the Member State concerned shall afford it the necessary assistance
holder: National competent authority of the Member State concerned
note: Includes 'requesting, where appropriate, the assistance of the police or an equivalent enforcement authority'.

quote: Conformity assessment bodies shall use the lists of codes, categories and corresponding types of AI systems set out in this Annex when specifying the types of AI systems in the application for designation
location: p. 38, Art. 1(43) (AI Act Annex XIV point 4)
note: Shared typology: AIP codes (Annex I products), AIB codes (biometrics), AIH codes incl. 'AIH 0301 generative AI systems, including AI systems based on general-purpose AI models' and 'AIH 0401 ... including Agentic AI'. Recital 43: aims to ensure notified bodies 'are fully competent in regard to the AI systems they are required to assess'.

quote: specify the model (version) name(s) of that/those models and provide a link to their Summary(ies) where available.
location: Annex Template, Section 1.2 'Model dependencies'; p. 9 (file marker)
holder: Providers of general-purpose AI models that modify or fine-tune other general-purpose AI models
obligation: statutory duty via mandatory Template field ('where available')
note: Links Summaries along the model value chain. Section 2.5 likewise asks to 'Specify the name of the general -purpose AI model(s) and provide a link to their Summary(ies)' for models used to generate synthetic data. Para 30: summaries of model versions should reference and link the original model's Summary. Cross-ref Accountability/Design para (28).

quote: a clear reference should be made to the original model in the Summary for each relevant model or model version, and a link to the Summary of the original model included
holder: Providers of modified or fine-tuned models and model versions
note: Links Summaries along the value chain so readers can trace a model back to the one it was built on. Template 1.2 asks for 'Model dependencies' with 'a link to their Summary(ies) where available'; Section 2.5 asks for the names of models used to generate synthetic data.

quote: ENISA aims to further refine and expand these recommendations in close cooperation with Member States and EUIBAs and will align these to upcoming European Commission Action Plan.
note: Cooperation with Member States and EU institutions, bodies and agencies (EUIBAs) on future recommendations; Commission Action Plan not yet issued.

quote: Governments should act and integrate industry into its crisis planning, establishing surge capacity models, defining clear prioritisation and escalation frameworks, and stress-testing multi-incident scenarios.
note: Government-industry crisis planning. Edge case: AI-accelerated incidents (AI used by attackers). Preceding text poses questions: 'how to prioritise incidents when they all meet regulatory thresholds, which CSIRTs structures can operate without prioritisation, and how sectoral CSIRTs can be supported when national capacity is saturated' (good practice: question).

quote: Leverage and build on existing initiatives at European and Member State level that consider the use of future AI models for cybersecurity.
location: page 14, The way ahead, Recommendations, European Level (bullet 2)
note: Listed under 'European Level'; initiatives not named. Concerns public and other use of AI models for cyber defence.

quote: The EUIs’ staff involved in the procurement of AI systems will need to coordinate efforts with the EUIs’ staff involved in the deployment of these AI systems
location: p.11, s.3.3 Procuring an AI system
holder: EUIs' staff involved in the procurement of AI systems, with EUIs' staff involved in deployment (IT engineers, IT project managers, DPOs, Data Protection Coordinators)
note: Purpose: to draft the technical part of the call for tender, select the right product and execute implementation. Internal coordination between procurement and deployment staff.

quote: The tender specifications should contain requirements as to the capability of the prospective tenderer to procure the planned AI system
location: p.11-12, s.3.3 Procuring an AI system (step 2)
note: Nearest named actor: the EUI as contracting authority. Continues p.12: 'and all relevant technical and procedural quality guarantees. Among others, information to be required is described in Section 5.3.' The cross-reference seems wrong: provider information is in s.5.2.5. The other steps (publication, selection and award, execution 'Monitor implementation and ensure compliance') report the Financial Regulation procedure and are not coded separately. Connects the EUI with prospective tenderers (outside the state: private companies [inference]).

quote: Create feedback loops where users can report issues or anomalies in inferences.
note: Connects system users with those maintaining the model: 'Use this feedback to identify potential data quality problems or drift and make necessary adjustments'. 'Users' appear to be those operating the system, not data subjects [inference].

quote: The organisation should invite the provider to produce:
note: Documentation to request: (1) general documentation (what the system does, architecture, UI/API); (2) transparency, interpretability, explainability; (3) cybersecurity and model integrity; (4) the provider's personal data governance, including statistical properties of training data; (5) validation and testing procedures and results. The provider (outside the state: private companies [inference]) is invited, not obliged; 'Many AI providers might provide vague or limited information'. Consequence if the provider declines: not stated.

quote: the organisation should request from the provider a set of metrics that will allow for the evaluation of the AI system against the organisation’s objectives
note: Request to provider; the metrics serve a check against the organisation's objectives. Common fairness metrics listed (FPR parity, FNR parity, calibration fairness, equality of opportunity) are coded as Coordination/Resources; task-specific benchmarks in Annex 1.
basis: AI pass B; different cell in pass A

quote: In that case, the EUI would have to prior consult the EDPS pursuant to Article 40(1) EUDPR.
note: Formal referral mechanism between the EUI and the EDPS. Also coded as Accountability/Design.

quote: joint controllers are under an obligation to define their respective obligation s in a transparent manner by concluding an agreement in accordance with Article 28 of the Regulation.
location: PDF p.11 (printed p.10), s.3 Roles and responsibilities
note: Trigger: entities jointly decide purposes and means (e.g. a shared objective for developing, training and fine-tuning). Also allocates responsibilities (Accountability).

quote: it is crucial to ask about the specific controls that have been put in place to guarantee this.
note: Trigger: a developer or provider claims the system does not process personal data (e.g. anonymised or synthetic data). Information flow from provider (value chain) to EUI: 'EUIs may want to know what steps or procedures the provider uses'.

quote: controllers should liaise with all relevant functions within the organisation, notably the DPO, Legal Service, the IT Service and the Local Informatics Security Officer (LISO)
location: PDF p.15 (printed p.14), s.5 (conclusion box [inference from layout])
note: Internal coordination: 'should not be a one -person effort' and 'a continuous dialogue among all the stakeholders involved across the lifecycle'. Box content not in body.

quote: The creation of an AI task force, including the DPO, and the preparation of an action plan
location: PDF p.15 (printed p.14), s.5 (conclusion box [inference from layout])
note: Nearest named actor: controllers / the EUI. Cross-functional group. Action plan contents coded under Delivery/Resources (awareness raising, internal guidance).

quote: the DPO should be involved in the review of compliance issues in the context of data sharing agreements signed with model providers.
location: PDF p.15 (printed p.14), s.5 Role of DPOs
note: Links the DPO to agreements with model providers. The DPO advises; no authority. Statutory DPO tasks (Art. 45) are reported in the same section and not coded separately.

quote: The controller is obliged to seek the advice of the DPO when carrying out a DPIA.

quote: This initiative could be explored to enhance data availability also for the public sector.

note: Also in section 2.1.4 (twice). The Board 'would support cross -sectoral standardisation and interoperability of high -quality data'. Pointer only.

quote: Commission has proposed to fund a GovTech Incubator  under the Digital Europe Programme 79 that would enable cross-border and cross-domain experimentation in all related domains.
note: Funding for GovTech experimentation. Reports another body's proposal; coded as a resource the document points to.

quote: ensure that there is enough knowledge to guarantee effective procurement or collaboration

quote: it is also recommended to identify AI champions 46  who would raise awareness, provide advice and assistance to local administration in a given geographical context and on specific topics (e.g., coordination of AI procurement, collaboration in upskilling, etc.).

quote: Promote the use of international funding  together with national, regional and local funding in a complementary manner.

quote: examples of AI procurement guidelines  aiming to assist civil servants when addressing common public procurement challenges have been proposed by a number of international organisations,56

note: Existing guidance cited as examples. Non-state provider; a mention only. Footnote 58 also points to the EU's TED portal for preliminary market consultations.

The text says the Commission's Adopt AI programme 'will play a crucial role' (a report). Holder not stated.

quote: it is suggested to  earmark funding and grants to support dedicated research in this area

quote: Raise awareness to support a better understanding on the part of public service officials  of how sharing open data can assist society
note: Information and awareness to support sharing of open data (Coordination). [scope doubt] Concerns open data generally.

quote: envisaging some financial or in-kind benefits for opening up service data sets.

quote: Guidelines are needed to build reusable components based on common standards and best practices.

quote: the AI4EU 76 initiative, hosting AI components that can be freely reused in AI development

note: Same sentence names 'the European Commission’s Connecting Europe Facility (CEF)', ISA2 interoperability solutions and EDIH. 'the Big Data Testing Infrastructure77 and Context Broker78 act as two of the most relevant CEF building blocks' (the testing infrastructure could also serve Delivery). Pointer, not an offer by this document.
basis: AI pass B; different cell in pass A
