note: Repositories holding standards, guidelines and performance metrics. The performance metrics may also serve evaluation (Delivery) [inference]. Holder not stated; nearest: national authorities.
basis: AI pass A; different cell in pass B

quote: Existing experiences of registries of algorithms, such as those in the cities of Amsterdam and Helsinki, can provide guidance for establishing a united registry at the EU level.
holder: cities of Amsterdam and Helsinki (existing registries)
note: Existing algorithm registers cited as guidance for an EU registry. A mention only.

quote: A key requirement for creating an EU -wide registry is also the establishmen t of common standards (vocabulary/ontology)
note: A common vocabulary or ontology serving as a shared template for the EU registry. Suggests drawing on the federated catalogue of the INSPIRE initiative (footnote 83). The standard-setting element could also be read as Decision-making.

quote: Develop multilingual sets of AI procurement guidelines  in partnership with the national procurement authorities of the EU Member States.
holder: not stated (developer); national procurement authorities of the EU Member States (partners)
obligation: recommended ('There is therefore a clear need to')
note: Rationale: 'public administrations throughout Europe must be able to access and understand the complexity of AI procurement'. Could build on the Commission's AI-powered eTranslation portal (p. 37). Serves procurement (Coordination).

quote: the provider may rely on its own detection solution or on a third party or shared detection solution , so long as th ose solutions  ensure interoperability with the detection solutions used by other providers
holder: Providers of generative AI systems; third-party or shared detection solution providers (not named)

No provider of shared solutions is named; mention, not an official offer.

quote: publicly-available industry standard detection solution s that allow any third party to implement detection that is  ideally locally executable on the digital device
holder: Industry standard-setters and providers of publicly available detection solutions (not named)
obligation: n/a (mention of external solutions the holder may rely on)
note: Shared detection standards as a coordination resource; offered by non-state actors, named only generically. Serves the Coordination/Design entry for para 76. Not an official offer.

quote: using the electronic notification tool developed and managed by the Commission
location: Art. 1(16), replacing AI Act Art. 30(2); p. 21
note: Tool serving notifications under Art. 30(2). Official offer (use is mandatory for notifying authorities).

quote: The Board shall adopt recommendations, taking into account European competence frameworks, to support the Commission and Member States in the promotion of AI literacy required under paragraph 1, including by setting out common objectives.
location: Art. 1(5), replacing AI Act Art. 4(3); p. 16
note: Advisory, not authority: coded Coordination/Resources (guidance passed from the Board to Commission and Member States). Could be read as Decision-making (setting common objectives); I chose Coordination. Recital 8 adds (recital only) 'regular exchange between the Commission and Member States' and that 'the Apply AI Alliance should allow discussion with the wider community'.
basis: AI pass B; different cell in pass A

quote: ENISA’s current capacity, as well as that of manufacturers, national CSIRTs, and national coordinated disclosure processes, may need further reinforcement or reconsideration to manage a large wave of newly discovered vulnerabilities.
location: Impact on vulnerability and patch management; p. 7
holder: ENISA; manufacturers; national CSIRTs; national coordinated disclosure processes
note: Capacity of coordinated vulnerability disclosure mechanisms. Edge case: vulnerabilities found at scale by AI (used by attackers and defenders). Who would provide reinforcement is not stated.

quote: The CRA’s Single Reporting Platform (SRP) and EU Vulnerability Database (EUVD) can help support the operationalisation of some of these recommendations.
note: Shared reporting platform and database connecting national authorities and defenders; operator not named [inference: ENISA]. 'correlated EUVD data can help identify supply-chain hotspots'; NIS2 incident reporting and situational awareness reports 'can help close the gap between vulnerability disclosure to coordinated response'. Executive summary (stakeholder input): SRP 'must be leveraged, once it is functional'.

quote: a. False Positive Rate (FPR) Parity: The number of incorrect positive cases can be compared across different groups. This metric should be similar for these groups.
note: Information provided by the EDPS for use in the request for provider metrics (Coordination/Design, p29): FPR parity, FNR parity, calibration fairness, equality of opportunity. 'Although metrics are context-dependant' (fn 74 cites Barberá, EDPB SPE). Also serves Delivery checks of group performance.

quote: it is important to ensure that DPOs, within their role, advise and assist in an independent manner on the application of the Regulation, have a proper understanding of the lifecycle of the generative AI system
location: PDF p.15 (printed p.14), s.5 Role of DPOs
obligation: non-binding interpretation ('it is important to ensure'); required of the holder
note: Knowledge/information for the DPO: 'obtaining information on when and how these systems process personal data, and how the input and output mechanisms work, as well as the decision- making processes implemented through the model.' Serves the DPO's advisory role (Coordination/Design). Who must ensure it is not named; nearest: the controller.
basis: AI pass B; different cell in pass A

quote: the European Commission, through the “Procurement of AI Community” initiative, has brought together relevant stakeholders in procuring AI solutions to develop wid e model contractual clauses
holder: European Commission ('Procurement of AI Community' initiative)
note: Model contractual clauses 'for the procurement of Artificial Intelligence  by public organizations'. Given 'As an example of contractual clauses'. Serves supplier agreements (Art. 29 agreement; DPO review of agreements with model providers).

quote: It is also relevant to consider the standard contractual clauses between controllers and processors under the Regulation
note: Serves controller-processor agreements (Art. 29). Who issues the clauses is not stated.

quote: This Opinion provides a framework for competent SAs to assess specific cases where (some of) the questions raised in the Request would arise.
note: Shared framework provided to all SAs, serving the Coordination/Design entry ('utmost account', para 15) and consistent application across the EEA (para 8). Not exhaustive; not all scenarios covered (paras 15-16). Could also be read as a resource for SA decisions (Decision-making); I placed it here because its stated aim is consistency.
basis: AI pass B; different cell in pass A

quote: Signatories are encouraged to ensure that documentation and other relevant information (excluding business confidential information and  trade secrets) is provided to deployers and other expert users to support them in making informed decisions
holder: Signatories who are providers of generative AI systems
note: Information provided along the value chain to deployers (which may include public bodies [inference]) on choosing, accessing and interpreting marking and detection solutions; also end-user literacy resources, including for sensitive contexts. Serves Coordination between providers and deployers and the detection entry. May be developed jointly or with academia and civil society; support EU-level literacy initiatives.
basis: AI pass B; different cell in pass A

quote: The framework as a whole – it offers a shared language across technical, policy and management perspectives
note: For structuring 'a team discussion or strategic reflection'. [inference] Coordination within an administration across technical, policy and management staff.

quote: PSTW offers examples of AI use cases in public administrations, and EU GovTech catalogues provide information on European start-ups and SMEs active in the field.
holder: European Commission (Public Sector Tech Watch; EU GovTech initiative)
note: Official Commission offers (Box 1: PSTW repository of over 2 000 use cases; EU GovTech dataset of over 900 companies, which join via a form). Rec 3: support structures 'can help administrations access expertise, identify trusted providers and replicate successful solutions'. Rec 5: 'Observatories such as PSTW and the EU GovTech initiative can support public administrations in this process.'

quote: the AI on Demand platform provides a collaborative space to support European research and innovation on AI
holder: AI on Demand platform (listed in Box 1 among European Commission initiatives)
note: Official offer. Box 1: 'a hub for sharing data, tools and code, to support mutual learning processes involving public administrations and private actors'; will promote the Strategy's AI toolbox.

quote: The revised EIF, as announced in the Interoperable Europe Act and referred to in the Apply AI Strategy, will serve as a useful resource, enabling public administrations to embrace an interoperable by design approach.
note: Official offer, forthcoming ('will serve'). Section 2.2 lists revising the EIF as one of 'three flagship actions that the Commission will implement'. Serves the interoperability entries (3.3.1, 3.3.2).

quote: Collaboration with trusted suppliers and partners is essential to facilitate experimentation with and adoption of AI
note: Contextual enabling factor; outside support from suppliers (outside the state: private companies), required of the holder to secure. How 'trusted' is established: not stated ('reliable and ethical suppliers').
basis: AI pass B; different cell in pass A

quote: Establishing strong support systems and networks, including partnerships with other organisations and stakeholders, can facilitate knowledge sharing and resource pooling.
note: Networks and partnerships; verb 'can'. Required of the holder; no provider named.
basis: AI pass B; different cell in pass A

quote: invites providers to immediately and proactively contact the AI Office to ensure they are taking the right steps to ensure compliance
note: Official offer of support: 'The AI Office is therefore dedicated to supporting providers in taking the necessary steps to comply' (paras 107, 109). Serves providers' compliance with Chapter V duties.
basis: AI pass B; different cell in pass A

quote: Information about the model’s usage should also include the technical means (e.g. instructions for use, infrastructure, tools) required for the model to be integrated into AI systems
holder: Providers of GPAI models released under a free and open-source licence that seek the exceptions
obligation: condition for the exemption (non-binding interpretation; should)
if_not_met: [inference] exemption does not apply: para (87) says the information 'must be ‘made publicly available’' for the exceptions to apply
note: Required of the holder: instructions, infrastructure, tools for integration. Minimum: 'information about the model’s input and output modalities, capabilities, and limitations'. 'This information ensures that downstream providers of AI systems, developers, and users can use the model'. Serves downstream integration.

quote: we will continue to explore the adoption of solutions created and tested by other institutions.
holder: Other EU institutions (providers of tested solutions); ECA
note: Inter-institutional reuse; also API access to Commission tools and testing CJEU tools (para 69). Para 64: combining efforts to reduce costs and avoid duplication.

quote: We will share our training material, methodologies, and lessons learned, and we will organise practical workshops to support the wider community of public sector auditors in navigating the challenges and opportunities presented by AI.
note: Resources offered by the ECA to other public auditors. Para 60 also floats making the methodology chatbot 'potentially' available to external users via the ECA website.
basis: AI pass B; different cell in pass A

quote: This should use established inter - institutional channels and build on existing Member State cooperation fora su ch as the Network of Member State Chief Information Officers, the Interoperability Expert Group
holder: Inter-institutional channels; Network of Member State Chief Information Officers; Interoperability Expert Group
note: Fora serving the knowledge-sharing coordination entry; also GovTech cooperation proposed under the Interoperable Europe Act.

quote: law enforcement, border control, immigration or asylum authorities should be able to use information systems, in accordance with Union or national law, to identify persons who, during an identity check, either refuse to be identified
holder: law enforcement, border control, immigration or asylum authorities
obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital, 'should be able to'); describes a power
note: Preserves identity checks in the presence of the person, 'without being required by this Regulation to obtain prior authorisation'. Exemption from the authorisation gate for public authorities.

quote: should be deployed only to confirm the specifically targeted individual’s identity and should be limited to what is strictly necessary concerning the period of time, as well as the geographic and personal scope
note: Limits on permitted real-time remote biometric identification for law enforcement; the reference database 'should be appropriate for each use case'. Nearest named actor: the relevant law enforcement authority.

quote: should be subject to an express and specific authorisation by a judicial authority or by an independent administrative authority of a Member State whose decision is binding
holder: a judicial authority or ... an independent administrative authority of a Member State
obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital, 'should be subject to'); describes a mandatory approval gate
if_not_met: If authorisation is rejected, the use 'should cease with immediate effect and all the data related to such use should be discarded and deleted'
note: Each use of 'real-time' remote biometric identification in publicly accessible spaces for law enforcement. Trigger: in principle before use; in duly justified urgency, use may start and authorisation must be sought within 24 hours (see Accountability entry, Recital 35).

quote: as determined in national law and specified in the context of each individual urgent use case by the law enforcement authority itself
note: In urgency, use 'should be restricted to the absolute minimum necessary and should be subject to appropriate safeguards and conditions'; the authority itself specifies them per use. Also coded Accountability (retrospective request).

quote: Where Union institutions, bodies, offices or agencies fall within the scope of this Regulation, the European Data Protection Supervisor shall act as the competent authority for their supervision.
note: Designates the supervisor for EU public bodies that provide or deploy AI. Also see Accountability/Design (Art. 74(9)) and fines (Art. 100).
basis: AI pass A; different cell in pass B

quote: The market surveillance authority shall take appropriate measures, as provided for in Article 19 of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020, within seven days from the date it received the notification
note: Trigger: serious incident notification. The measures are those of another instrument (Art. 19 Regulation (EU) 2019/1020), not set out here.

quote: Member States shall designate as market surveillance authorities for the purposes of this Regulation either the competent data protection supervisory authorities under Regulation (EU) 2016/679 or Directive (EU) 2016/680
note: Appoints supervisors for core public-sector uses: Annex III point 1 (biometrics) 'in so far as the systems are used for law enforcement purposes, border management and justice and democracy', and points 6, 7 and 8 (law enforcement; migration, asylum and border control; justice and democratic processes). Alternative: another authority meeting Arts. 41-44 Directive (EU) 2016/680. Also coded Accountability/Design (judicial independence).

quote: the European Data Protection Supervisor shall act as their market surveillance authority, except in relation to the Court of Justice of the European Union acting in its judicial capacity.
note: Appoints the supervisor for Union institutions, bodies, offices and agencies. See Art. 70(9) (Accountability/Design) and Art. 100 (EDPS fines).
basis: AI pass B; different cell in pass A

quote: Those authorities may, as appropriate, allow the testing in real world conditions to be conducted by the provider or prospective provider, in derogation from the conditions set out in Article 60(4), points (f) and (g).
note: Exemption power for sandbox testing: (f) is the duration limit; (g) the protection of vulnerable groups.

quote: to suspend or terminate the testing in real world conditions;
note: Authority to stop. Trigger: informed by the provider, prospective provider or 'any third party' of a serious incident, or other grounds that Arts. 60 and 61 conditions are not met. Alternative (b): require provider and deployer 'to modify any aspect of the testing'.

quote: it shall without undue delay require the relevant operator to take all appropriate corrective actions to bring the AI system into compliance, to withdraw the AI system from the market, or to recall it
note: Authority to require correction, withdrawal or recall. Trigger: evaluation finds non-compliance. Period: as prescribed, 'in any event within the shorter of 15 working days' or as in harmonisation legislation. Notified body informed; Art. 18 Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 applies. [inference] 'Operator' can include a public-sector deployer.

quote: the market surveillance authority shall take all appropriate provisional measures to prohibit or restrict the AI system’s being made available on its national market or put into service
note: Authority to stop or restrict, or withdraw or recall. Trigger: operator fails to take adequate corrective action in the period. The notification (Art. 79(6)) must say whether non-compliance stems from Art. 5 prohibitions, Chapter III Section 2 requirements, shortcomings in harmonised standards or common specifications, or Art. 50.

quote: The market surveillance authorities shall ensure that appropriate restrictive measures are taken in respect of the product or the AI system concerned, such as withdrawal of the product or the AI system from their market, without undue delay.
note: Union-wide effect. Art. 79(8): a provisional measure is 'deemed justified' if no objection within three months (30 days for Art. 5 breaches), without prejudice to the operator's procedural rights.

quote: it shall without undue delay require the relevant provider to take all necessary actions to bring the AI system into compliance with the requirements and obligations laid down in this Regulation
note: Reclassification as high-risk. Also requires corrective action within a prescribed period. If use extends beyond national territory, the authority informs the Commission and other Member States (Art. 80(3)).

quote: Where the Commission considers the measure taken by the relevant Member State to be justified, all Member States shall ensure that they take appropriate restrictive measures in respect of the AI system concerned
if_not_met: Member State withdraws its measure if the Commission finds it unjustified (Art. 81(2))
note: Union safeguard procedure. Trigger: objection by another Member State's authority, or Commission view that the measure is contrary to Union law. The Commission consults the authority and the operators, evaluates, and decides within six months (60 days for Art. 5). If unjustified, the Member State 'shall withdraw the measure'. If due to shortcomings in standards, Art. 11 Regulation (EU) No 1025/2012 applies (Art. 81(3)).

quote: all Member States shall ensure that they take appropriate restrictive measures in respect of the AI system concerned, such as requiring the withdrawal of the AI system from their market without undue delay
note: Trigger: Commission finds the national measure justified. If unjustified, 'the Member State concerned shall withdraw the measure'. 81(3): where standards are at fault, the Commission applies Regulation 1025/2012 Art. 11.

quote: it shall require the relevant operator to take all appropriate measures to ensure that the AI system concerned, when placed on the market or put into service, no longer presents that risk
holder: Market surveillance authority of a Member State
note: Applies even where the high-risk system complies but 'nevertheless presents a risk to the health or safety of persons, to fundamental rights, or to other aspects of public interest protection'. Also coded Coordination/Design (consultation).

quote: it nevertheless presents a risk to the health or safety of persons, to fundamental rights, or to other aspects of public interest protection, it shall require the relevant operator to take all appropriate measures
holder: Market surveillance authority of a Member State
note: Authority over a compliant but risky high-risk system. Trigger: Art. 79 evaluation, 'after consulting the relevant national public authority referred to in Article 77(1)'. Period set by the MSA.

quote: the Commission shall decide whether the measure is justified and, where necessary, propose other appropriate measures.
note: After consulting the Member States and operators and evaluating the national measures. Member States must 'immediately inform the Commission and the other Member States' of a finding (Art. 82(3)); the Commission communicates its decision (Art. 82(5)).

quote: it shall require the relevant provider to put an end to the non-compliance concerned, within a period it may prescribe
holder: Market surveillance authority of a Member State
if_not_met: 'appropriate and proportionate measures to restrict or prohibit the high-risk AI system being made available on the market or to ensure that it is recalled or withdrawn from the market without delay' (Art. 83(2))
note: Formal non-compliance findings include CE marking, EU declaration of conformity, '(e) the registration in the EU database referred to in Article 71 has not been carried out', missing authorised representative, '(g) technical documentation is not available'.
basis: AI pass B; different cell in pass A

quote: the market surveillance authority of the Member State concerned shall take appropriate and proportionate measures to restrict or prohibit the high-risk AI system being made available on the market
holder: Market surveillance authority of the Member State concerned
note: Trigger: formal non-compliance persists. Includes recall or withdrawal 'without delay'.

quote: no decision producing an adverse legal effect on a person should be taken based solely on the output of the remote biometric identification system.
note: Limits decisions taken on system output alone (a human decision is required [inference]). Nearest named actor: the law enforcement authority.

quote: Member States remain free under this Regulation not to provide for such a possibility at all or to only provide for such a possibility in respect of some of the objectives
obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital); describes a Member State option
note: Real-time remote biometric identification for law enforcement is possible only where and in so far as the Member State 'has decided to expressly provide for the possibility to authorise such use in its detailed rules of national law'. Also coded Coordination/Design (notification of national rules).

quote: Such use for purposes other than law enforcement should therefore not be subject to the requirement of an authorisation under this Regulation
obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital); describes scope of the authorisation regime
note: Real-time remote biometric identification in publicly accessible spaces for purposes other than law enforcement, 'including by competent authorities', falls outside the AI Act authorisation regime; Recital (39) says data protection law (e.g. Art. 9(1) GDPR) continues to apply. Nearest named actor: competent authorities.

quote: should only be possible where and in as far as the Member State concerned has decided to expressly provide for the possibility to authorise such use in its detailed rules of national law
note: 'Member States remain free under this Regulation not to provide for such a possibility at all' or to allow it only for some objectives.

quote: The Commission shall have exclusive powers to supervise and enforce Chapter V, taking into account the procedural guarantees under Article 94.
holder: Commission (implementation entrusted to the AI Office)
note: Assigns authority over general-purpose AI model obligations (Chapter V, outside this part). 'The Commission shall entrust the implementation of these tasks to the AI Office'.

quote: The Commission shall adopt implementing acts setting out the detailed arrangements and the conditions for the evaluations, including the detailed arrangements for involving independent experts, and the procedure for the selection thereof.
note: Sets the evaluation standard; examination procedure (Art. 98(2)).

quote: restrict the making available on the market, withdraw or recall the model.
if_not_met: fines for failing to comply with a requested measure (Art. 101(1)(c))
note: Authority over general-purpose models: may also request (a) measures to comply with Arts. 53-54, (b) mitigation where an Art. 92 evaluation gives 'serious and substantiated concern of a systemic risk at Union level'. A structured dialogue may precede; the Commission 'may, by decision, make those commitments binding' (Art. 93(3)).

quote: the Commission may, by decision, make those commitments binding and declare that there are no further grounds for action.
note: Trigger: a systemic-risk model provider offers mitigation commitments in a structured dialogue.

quote: Codes of conduct may be drawn up by individual providers or deployers of AI systems or by organisations representing them or by both
holder: Individual providers or deployers of AI systems, or organisations representing them
note: Voluntary self-set standards, possibly with stakeholders 'including civil society organisations and academia'. [inference] A public-sector deployer could adopt its own code.

quote: The power to adopt delegated acts is conferred on the Commission subject to the conditions laid down in this Article.
note: Covers delegated acts under Arts. 6(6)-(7), 7(1) and (3), 11(3), 43(5)-(6), 47(5), 51(3), 52(4), 53(5)-(6) [inference: including amending Annex III and the high-risk classification conditions]. Five years from 1 August 2024, tacitly extended. Also coded Accountability/Design.

quote: Each Member State shall lay down rules on to what extent administrative fines may be imposed on public authorities and bodies established in that Member State.
note: Scope decision held by each Member State. Also coded Accountability/Design.

quote: When adopting detailed measures related to technical specifications and procedures for approval and use of security equipment concerning Artificial Intelligence systems
note: Chapter III, Section 2 requirements 'shall be taken into account' in civil aviation security rules. Passive; nearest named actor: the body adopting the measures [inference: the Commission]. [inference] Aviation security screening equipment is often run by or for public authorities.

quote: When adopting delegated acts pursuant to the first subparagraph concerning artificial intelligence systems which are safety components within the meaning of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689
note: Agricultural and forestry vehicles: Chapter III, Section 2 requirements 'shall be taken into account'. Nearest named actor: the Commission (adopts delegated acts) [inference]. Product safety component; public-sector link weak [coder judgement].

quote: When adopting delegated acts pursuant to the first subparagraph concerning Artificial Intelligence systems which are safety components within the meaning of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689
note: Two- or three-wheel vehicles and quadricycles. Same mechanism as Art. 103. Nearest named actor: the Commission [inference]. Public-sector link weak [coder judgement].

quote: the Commission shall take into account the requirements set out in Chapter III, Section 2, of that Regulation.
note: Marine equipment: applies when the Commission carries out its activities and adopts technical specifications and testing standards for AI safety components. Public-sector link weak [coder judgement].

quote: When adopting delegated acts pursuant to paragraph 1 and implementing acts pursuant to paragraph 11 concerning Artificial Intelligence systems which are safety components
note: Rail interoperability: Chapter III, Section 2 requirements 'shall be taken into account'. Nearest named actor: the Commission [inference]. [inference] Rail operators and infrastructure managers are often public bodies.

quote: Natural persons should never be judged on AI-predicted behaviour based solely on their profiling, personality traits or characteristics
obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital, 'should be prohibited'); describes a prohibition
note: Prohibits individual crime-risk assessments based solely on profiling or personality traits 'without a reasonable suspicion ... based on objective verifiable facts and without human assessment thereof'. Not covered: risk analytics not based on profiling individuals, e.g. tools 'to predict the likelihood of the localisation of narcotics or illicit goods by customs authorities'. Nearest named actors: law enforcement and customs authorities.

quote: AI systems that create or expand facial recognition databases through the untargeted scraping of facial images from the internet or CCTV footage, should be prohibited
obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital, 'should be prohibited'); describes a prohibition
note: Applies to placing on the market, putting into service for that purpose, or use. Nearest named actors: providers and deployers.

quote: the placing on the market, the putting into service, or the use of AI systems intended to be used to detect the emotional state of individuals in situations related to the workplace and education should be prohibited.
obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital, 'should be prohibited'); describes a prohibition
note: Applies to public employers and public education bodies among others [inference]. Exception: systems placed on the market strictly for medical or safety reasons. Nearest named actors: providers and deployers.

quote: High-risk AI systems should only be placed on the Union market, put into service or used if they comply with certain mandatory requirements.
obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital, 'should only be'); describes a precondition for market access and use
note: Gate on use: covers 'used' as well as placing on the market, so it reaches public deployers. Nearest named actors: providers and deployers. High-risk classification should be limited to systems with a significant harmful impact on health, safety and fundamental rights.

quote: to predict the occurrence of an actual or potential criminal offence based solely on profiling them or on assessing their personality traits and characteristics should be prohibited
holder: European Parliament and Council (legislator, through this Regulation)
obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital) of a prohibition; 'should be prohibited'
note: Individual crime-risk assessment based solely on profiling. Principle: no judgement on AI-predicted behaviour 'without human assessment thereof'. Carve-out: risk analytics not based on profiling individuals, e.g. tools 'by customs authorities' to locate narcotics or illicit goods.

quote: When adopting delegated acts pursuant to paragraph 3 concerning Artificial Intelligence systems which are safety components within the meaning of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689
note: Motor vehicle type-approval. Nearest named actor: the Commission [inference]. Public-sector link weak [coder judgement].

quote: when adopting implementing acts pursuant to paragraph 1 concerning Artificial Intelligence systems which are safety components within the meaning of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689
note: Civil aviation (EASA Regulation): six provisions amended so Chapter III, Section 2 requirements 'shall be taken into account' in delegated and implementing acts on AI safety components. Nearest named actor: the Commission [inference]. [inference] Some of the amended provisions concern air traffic management and unmanned aircraft, where providers are often public.

quote: When adopting the implementing acts pursuant to paragraph 2, concerning artificial intelligence systems which are safety components within the meaning of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689
note: Vehicle general safety type-approval. Nearest named actor: the Commission [inference]. Public-sector link weak [coder judgement].

quote: that have been placed on the market or put into service before 2 August 2027 shall be brought into compliance with this Regulation by 31 December 2030.
note: Applies to 'AI systems which are components of the large-scale IT systems established by the legal acts listed in Annex X' (EU freedom, security and justice systems such as SIS, VIS, Eurodac, EES, ETIAS, ECRIS-TCN), without prejudice to Art. 5. Passive; operators not named [inference: EU agencies and Member State authorities running these systems]. Also coded Delivery/Design (evaluation).

quote: In any case, the providers and deployers of high-risk AI systems intended to be used by public authorities shall take the necessary steps to comply with the requirements and obligations of this Regulation by 2 August 2030.
holder: Providers and deployers of high-risk AI systems intended to be used by public authorities
note: Other high-risk systems placed on the market or put into service before 2 August 2026 are covered only if 'subject to significant changes in their designs' from that date; this sentence removes that exemption for systems intended for public authorities from 2 August 2030. Without prejudice to Art. 5.
basis: AI pass A; different cell in pass B

quote: Providers of general-purpose AI models that have been placed on the market before 2 August 2025 shall take the necessary steps in order to comply with the obligations laid down in this Regulation by 2 August 2027.
holder: Providers of general-purpose AI models placed on the market before 2 August 2025
note: Transition for existing model providers whose models sit inside public-sector tools.
basis: AI pass A; different cell in pass B

quote: The Commission shall assess the need for amendment of the list set out in Annex III and of the list of prohibited AI practices laid down in Article 5, once a year
note: Annual review of scope (high-risk list and prohibitions) until the end of the delegation period. 'The Commission shall submit the findings of that assessment to the European Parliament and the Council' (accountability element). 112(10): the Commission 'shall, if necessary, submit appropriate proposals to amend this Regulation'.
basis: AI pass B; different cell in pass A

quote: This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.
note: Application dates: generally 2 August 2026; Chapters I-II from 2 February 2025; Chapter III Section 4, Chapters V, VII, XII and Art. 78 from 2 August 2025, except Art. 101; Art. 6(1) obligations from 2 August 2027. Applies to all addressees.

quote: It shall apply from 2 August 2026.
note: Timing of scope. Exceptions: (a) Chapters I and II from 2 February 2025; (b) Chapter III Section 4, Chapter V, Chapter VII, Chapter XII and Art. 78 from 2 August 2025, except Art. 101; (c) Art. 6(1) and corresponding obligations from 2 August 2027. 'This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.'

quote: Regulation (EU) 2017/745 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 5 April 2017 on medical devices
location: p. 124, Annex I, Section A, point 11
note: Annex I lists Union harmonisation legislation: Section A (machinery, toys, recreational craft, lifts, explosive atmospheres equipment, radio equipment, pressure equipment, cableways, protective equipment, gas appliances, medical devices, in vitro diagnostics) and Section B (aviation security, vehicles, marine equipment, rail, civil aviation). [inference] AI safety components of these products are high-risk under Art. 6(1); medical devices are the clearest public-service case (e.g. diagnostic tools in public health services).

quote: Criminal offences referred to in Article 5(1), first subparagraph, point (h)(iii):
note: Sixteen offences, including terrorism, trafficking in human beings, child sexual exploitation, drugs and weapons trafficking, murder, kidnapping, rape, environmental crime, organised or armed robbery, sabotage. [inference] Defines when law enforcement may rely on the Art. 5 exception for real-time remote biometric identification. Nearest named actors: law enforcement authorities.

quote: High-risk AI systems pursuant to Article 6(2) are the AI systems listed in any of the following areas
note: Decides which tools are high-risk and so carry the full set of duties. Areas: 1 biometrics; 2 critical infrastructure; 3 education; 4 employment; 5 essential private and public services; 6 law enforcement; 7 migration, asylum, border control; 8 justice and democratic processes (incl. 8(b) influencing elections). Public-sector items coded separately. Commission may amend by delegated act (Art. 97 lists Art. 7(1) and (3)).

quote: Biometrics, in so far as their use is permitted under relevant Union or national law:
note: Chapeau: 'High-risk AI systems pursuant to Article 6(2) are the AI systems listed in any of the following areas'. Point 1: (a) remote biometric identification (not verification); (b) biometric categorisation by sensitive or protected attributes; (c) emotion recognition. Classification set by the Regulation; applies to providers and deployers of listed systems.

quote: AI systems intended to be used as safety components in the management and operation of critical digital infrastructure, road traffic, or in the supply of water, gas, heating or electricity.
note: Critical infrastructure; often run by public bodies or utilities [inference]. Point 2 systems are excluded from the Art. 86 right to explanation.

quote: AI systems intended to be used to determine access or admission or to assign natural persons to educational and vocational training institutions at all levels;
note: Education: also (b) evaluating learning outcomes, (c) assessing the level of education a person will receive, (d) monitoring prohibited behaviour during tests. [inference] Covers public schools and universities.

quote: AI systems intended to be used for the recruitment or selection of natural persons, in particular to place targeted job advertisements, to analyse and filter job applications, and to evaluate candidates;
note: Employment: also (b) decisions on terms, promotion or termination, task allocation, and monitoring and evaluation of workers. [inference] Covers public employers.

quote: AI systems intended to be used by public authorities or on behalf of public authorities to evaluate the eligibility of natural persons for essential public assistance benefits and services, including healthcare services
note: Explicitly public-sector: also 'to grant, reduce, revoke, or reclaim such benefits and services'. Points 5(b) creditworthiness (except fraud detection) and 5(c) life and health insurance pricing concern private services.

quote: AI systems intended to evaluate and classify emergency calls by natural persons or to be used to dispatch, or to establish priority in the dispatching of, emergency first response services, including by police, firefighters and medical aid
note: Emergency services; also 'emergency healthcare patient triage systems'.

quote: Law enforcement, in so far as their use is permitted under relevant Union or national law:
note: Systems used 'by or on behalf of law enforcement authorities, or by Union institutions, bodies, offices or agencies in support of' them: (a) risk of a person becoming a victim; (b) polygraphs and similar tools; (c) reliability of evidence; (d) risk of offending or re-offending, personality traits or past criminal behaviour; (e) profiling in detection, investigation or prosecution.

quote: Migration, asylum and border control management, in so far as their use is permitted under relevant Union or national law:
note: Systems used 'by or on behalf of competent public authorities or by Union institutions, bodies, offices or agencies': (a) polygraphs and similar tools; (b) security, irregular-migration or health risk assessment of persons entering; (c) assisting examination of asylum, visa and residence applications and complaints, including reliability of evidence; (d) detecting, recognising or identifying persons, 'with the exception of the verification of travel documents'.

quote: AI systems intended to be used by a judicial authority or on their behalf to assist a judicial authority in researching and interpreting facts and the law and in applying the law to a concrete set of facts
note: Administration of justice, also 'used in a similar way in alternative dispute resolution'. Point 8(b): systems for influencing election or referendum outcomes or voting behaviour, excluding administrative or logistical campaign tools.

quote: The quality management system shall be assessed by the notified body, which shall determine whether it satisfies the requirements referred to in Article 17.
note: Approval of the provider's quality management system; decision notified with 'the reasoned assessment decision'. Provider must keep the approved system 'adequate and efficient' (3.3). Assessment is also a check (Delivery).
basis: AI pass B; different cell in pass A

quote: The proposed changes shall be examined by the notified body, which shall decide whether the modified quality management system continues to satisfy the requirements referred to in point 3.2 or whether a reassessment is necessary.
note: Trigger: on change; the provider must bring intended changes to the notified body's attention. Point 3.3: the provider keeps the approved system 'adequate and efficient'.

quote: Where the AI system is not in conformity with the requirements set out in Chapter III, Section 2, the notified body shall refuse to issue a Union technical documentation assessment certificate
if_not_met: certificate refused with detailed reasons; where training data fails, 're-training of the AI system will be needed prior to the application for a new conformity assessment'
note: Approval decision. Where conforming, the certificate is issued and must allow conformity to be evaluated 'and to allow for control of the AI system while in use'.

quote: Any change to the AI system that could affect the compliance of the AI system with the requirements or its intended purpose shall be assessed by the notified body which issued the Union technical documentation assessment certificate.
holder: Notified body that issued the certificate
note: Trigger: on change. The provider must inform the notified body of intended changes. The body decides whether a new conformity assessment (Art. 43(4)) is needed or a certificate supplement suffices.

quote: Union legislative acts on large-scale IT systems in the area of Freedom, Security and Justice
note: Lists the acts for: Schengen Information System; Visa Information System; Eurodac; Entry/Exit System; ETIAS; ECRIS-TCN; interoperability frameworks. Sets which public systems get the 31 December 2030 transition (Art. 111(1)). Operators not named [inference: EU agencies and Member State authorities].

quote: any future amendments of the list of high-risk AI systems that the Commission should be empowered to adopt, via delegated acts
obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital, 'should be empowered'); describes a delegated power
note: Authority to change which stand-alone systems are high-risk. Criteria: severity and probability of harm to health, safety or fundamental rights, in pre-defined areas; amendments follow 'the same methodology and criteria'.

quote: The first such condition should be that the AI system is intended to perform a narrow procedural task, such as an AI system that transforms unstructured data into structured data, an AI system that classifies incoming documents into categories
holder: European Parliament and Council (legislator, through this Regulation); applied by the provider
obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital) of a derogation from high-risk classification
note: Annex-listed systems that do not materially influence decision-making may be non-high-risk. Four conditions: narrow procedural task; improving a previously completed human activity; detecting decision patterns or deviations (not replacing human assessment 'without proper human review'); preparatory task (e.g. file handling, translation). The provider makes the determination (see Delivery and Accountability entries for this recital). Directly relevant to public-sector document classification tools.

quote: an AI system that does not materially influence the outcome of decision-making should be understood to be an AI system that does not have an impact on the substance, and thereby the outcome, of decision-making
holder: a provider who considers that an AI system is not high-risk
obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital); describes a derogation from high-risk classification
note: The provider decides whether an annex-listed system falls under the derogation. Four conditions: (1) narrow procedural task, e.g. 'an AI system that classifies incoming documents into categories' or detects duplicates among applications; (2) improves the result of a completed human activity, e.g. improving language in drafted documents; (3) detects decision-making patterns or deviations, e.g. checking a teacher's grading ex post; (4) preparatory task, e.g. file handling, indexing, searching, translation. Systems that imply profiling are always high-risk. Many of the examples are public-administration tasks. Cross-ref Delivery/Design and Accountability/Design (Recital 53).

quote: For the purpose of determining that a general-purpose AI model has capabilities or an impact equivalent to those set out in Article 51(1), point (a), the Commission shall take into account the following criteria:
obligation: statutory criteria for a Commission decision
note: Criteria: parameters; data set size; training compute; modalities; benchmarks and evaluations, including autonomy, scalability and tool access; reach, presumed high when made available to at least 10 000 registered business users in the Union; registered end-users. Decides which models carry systemic-risk obligations.

quote: Remote biometric identification systems should therefore be classified as high-risk in view of the risks that they pose.
obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital); describes high-risk classification set by the Regulation
note: Classification is made by the Regulation; obligations then fall on providers and deployers (nearest named actors). Also high-risk: biometric categorisation by sensitive attributes and emotion recognition not otherwise prohibited. Not high-risk: biometric verification, and systems used solely for cybersecurity and personal data protection.

quote: it is appropriate to classify as high-risk the AI systems intended to be used as safety components in the management and operation of critical digital infrastructure
obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital); describes high-risk classification set by the Regulation
note: Also road traffic and the supply of water, gas, heating and electricity. Components used solely for cybersecurity are not safety components. Relevant to public utilities and road authorities [inference]. Nearest named actors: providers and deployers.

quote: AI systems used in high-risk use-cases listed in an annex to this Regulation should be considered to pose significant risks of harm to the health, safety or fundamental rights if the AI system implies profiling
holder: European Parliament and Council (legislator, through this Regulation)
obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital); limit on the derogation
note: Profiling (GDPR/LED/EUDPR definitions) always keeps an annex-listed system high-risk.

quote: for monitoring and detecting prohibited behaviour of students during tests should be classified as high-risk AI systems
obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital); describes high-risk classification set by the Regulation
note: Education and vocational training: also determining access or admission, assigning persons to institutions or programmes, evaluating learning outcomes, and assessing the appropriate level of education. Nearest named actors: providers and deployers (including public education bodies [inference]).

quote: for monitoring or evaluation of persons in work-related contractual relationships, should also be classified as high-risk
obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital); describes high-risk classification set by the Regulation
note: Employment and workers management: also recruitment and selection, decisions on terms, promotion and termination, and task allocation based on behaviour or traits. Applies to public bodies as employers [inference]. Nearest named actors: providers and deployers.

quote: If AI systems are used for determining whether such benefits and services should be granted, denied, reduced, revoked or reclaimed by authorities
obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital); describes high-risk classification set by the Regulation
note: The sentence concludes that such systems 'should therefore be classified as high-risk'. Covers essential public assistance benefits and services from public authorities (healthcare, social security, social services, housing assistance), including whether beneficiaries are legitimately entitled. Also: 'this Regulation should not hamper the development and use of innovative approaches in the public administration' where no high risk arises. Credit scoring and life/health insurance pricing are also high-risk; fraud detection in financial services is not. Nearest named actors: public authorities as deployers; providers.

quote: AI systems used in employment, workers management and access to self-employment, in particular for the recruitment and selection of persons, for making decisions affecting terms of the work-related relationship
holder: European Parliament and Council (legislator, through this Regulation)
note: These 'should also be classified as high-risk'; includes task allocation and monitoring/evaluation of workers. Applies to public bodies as employers [inference].

quote: AI systems used to evaluate and classify emergency calls by natural persons or to dispatch or establish priority in the dispatching of emergency first response services, including by police, firefighters and medical aid
obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital); describes high-risk classification set by the Regulation
note: These 'should also be classified as high-risk', as should emergency healthcare patient triage systems. Public emergency services [inference]. Nearest named actors: providers and deployers.

quote: those high-risk AI systems should include in particular AI systems intended to be used by or on behalf of law enforcement authorities or by Union institutions, bodies, offices, or agencies in support of law enforcement authorities
obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital); describes high-risk classification set by the Regulation
note: Insofar as use is permitted under Union and national law: assessing a person's risk of becoming a victim; polygraphs and similar tools; evaluating the reliability of evidence; offending or reoffending risk not solely based on profiling; profiling in detection, investigation or prosecution. Nearest named actors: law enforcement authorities and EU bodies supporting them.

quote: for administrative proceedings by tax and customs authorities as well as by financial intelligence units carrying out administrative tasks analysing information pursuant to Union anti-money laundering law should not be classified as high-risk
obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital); describes an exclusion from high-risk classification
note: Exclusion for public bodies: tax and customs administrative proceedings and FIU administrative analysis are not law-enforcement high-risk uses. Nearest named actors: tax and customs authorities, financial intelligence units.

quote: AI systems intended to be used by or on behalf of competent public authorities or by Union institutions, bodies, offices or agencies charged with tasks in the fields of migration, asylum and border control management
obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital); describes high-risk classification set by the Regulation
note: High-risk when used as polygraphs and similar tools, for assessing risks posed by persons entering or applying for visa or asylum, for assisting examination of asylum, visa and residence applications, and for detecting, recognising or identifying persons (except verification of travel documents). Must also comply with procedural requirements of the Visa Code, Directive 2013/32/EU and other Union law. Nearest named actors: competent public authorities and EU bodies.

quote: AI systems specifically intended to be used for administrative proceedings by tax and customs authorities as well as by financial intelligence units
holder: European Parliament and Council (legislator, through this Regulation)
obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital) of a classification exemption
note: These 'should not be classified as high-risk AI systems used by law enforcement authorities' for criminal-offence purposes. Public-sector scope exemption.

quote: should, in no circumstances, be used by Member States or Union institutions, bodies, offices or agencies as a means to circumvent their international obligations under the UN Convention relating to the Status of Refugees
holder: Member States or Union institutions, bodies, offices or agencies
note: Limit on how public authorities use AI in migration, asylum and border control; nor to infringe non-refoulement or deny safe and effective legal avenues into the Union.

quote: The use of AI tools can support the decision-making power of judges or judicial independence, but should not replace it: the final decision-making must remain a human-driven activity.
obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital; verbs 'should not replace' and 'must remain')
note: Reserves final decision-making in the administration of justice to humans. Bears on checking AI outputs used by courts.

quote: AI systems intended to be used by a judicial authority or on its behalf to assist judicial authorities in researching and interpreting facts and the law and in applying the law to a concrete set of facts.
obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital); describes high-risk classification set by the Regulation
note: Qualified as high-risk; also alternative dispute resolution bodies where outcomes produce legal effects. Excluded: 'purely ancillary administrative activities', e.g. anonymisation or pseudonymisation of judicial decisions, communication between personnel, administrative tasks. Nearest named actors: judicial authorities. Cross-ref Decision-making/Design (human final decision, Recital 61).

quote: AI systems intended to be used to influence the outcome of an election or referendum or the voting behaviour of natural persons in the exercise of their vote in elections or referenda should be classified as high-risk AI systems
obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital); describes high-risk classification set by the Regulation
note: Excludes tools whose output persons are not directly exposed to (e.g. campaign logistics). Relevance to public-sector tools is indirect [inference]. Nearest named actors: providers and deployers.

quote: Given the specificities of the areas of law enforcement, migration, border control and asylum, this requirement should not apply where Union or national law considers the application of that requirement to be disproportionate.
obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital); describes an exemption decided by Union or national law
note: Exemption from the two-person verification (Delivery/Design, Recital 73) for public authorities in these areas, if the legislator so decides.

quote: a natural person to whom human oversight has been assigned to make informed decisions if, when and how to intervene in order to avoid negative consequences or risks, or stop the system
holder: a natural person to whom human oversight has been assigned
note: Authority to intervene or stop the system; systems should 'include mechanisms to guide and inform' that person. Who assigns oversight: not stated here (see Recital 91, deployers). Bears on checking AI outputs.
basis: AI pass A; different cell in pass B

quote: Instructions for use should be made available in a language which can be easily understood by target deployers, as determined by the Member State concerned.
note: Member State sets the language; providers make instructions available.

quote: the system is subject to in-built operational constraints that cannot be overridden by the system itself and is responsive to the human operator
holder: the provider of the system (measures); the human operator (control)
note: Human control over the system built into design; authority sits with the human operator.

quote: Post-remote biometric identification systems should always be used in a way that is proportionate, legitimate and strictly necessary, and thus targeted, in terms of the individuals to be identified, the location, temporal scope
note: Limits on use; based on 'a closed data set of legally acquired video footage'; 'should not be used in the framework of law enforcement to lead to indiscriminate surveillance'. Nearest named actors: deployers, especially law enforcement.

quote: In light of the risks identified, deployers should determine measures to be taken in the case of a materialisation of those risks, including for example governance arrangements in that specific context of use
holder: deployers (that carry out a fundamental rights impact assessment)
note: Deployers decide governance arrangements, 'such as arrangements for human oversight according to the instructions of use or, complaint handling and redress procedures' (the latter also bear on Accountability). Cross-ref Delivery/Design (FRIA, Recital 96).

quote: should in any case not apply when an own model is used for purely internal processes that are not essential for providing a product or a service to third parties
note: General-purpose AI model obligations do not apply to an own model used purely internally, provided also that 'the rights of natural persons are not affected'. Models with systemic risk 'should always be subject to the relevant obligations'. Could bear on public bodies that build models for internal use [inference]. Nearest named actor: provider of a general-purpose AI model.

quote: The Commission should be empowered to amend those annexes by means of delegated acts in light of evolving technological developments.
obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital, 'should be empowered'); describes a delegated power
note: Authority to change the documentation standard for general-purpose AI models.

quote: should be subject to exceptions as regards the transparency-related requirements imposed on general-purpose AI models, unless they can be considered to present a systemic risk
holder: European Parliament and Council (legislator, through this Regulation)
note: Applies to providers of GPAI models released under free and open-source licence with public weights, architecture and usage information. Exception does not cover the training-content summary or the copyright policy.

quote: In the case of a modification or fine-tuning of a model, the obligations for providers of general-purpose AI models should be limited to that modification or fine-tuning
obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital); describes the scope of obligations
note: For example, complementing existing technical documentation with information on the modifications and new training data sources. Also: no compliance needed for non-professional or scientific research use (these persons are 'encouraged to voluntarily comply'); simplified compliance for SMEs. Could bear on public bodies that fine-tune models [inference]. Nearest named actor: whoever modifies or fine-tunes a model.

quote: there should be a possibility for the Commission to take individual decisions designating a general-purpose AI model as a general-purpose AI model with systemic risk if it is found that such model has capabilities or an impact equivalent
obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital, 'there should be a possibility'); describes a designation power
note: Complements a FLOPs threshold that creates a presumption of systemic risk; the threshold 'should be adjusted over time' and supplemented with benchmarks. The decision rests on annex criteria (data size, number of users, modalities, autonomy, tools). Recital (113): the Commission 'should be empowered to designate' where the provider failed to notify. Cross-ref Accountability/Design (reassessment on request, Recital 111).

quote: By means of implementing acts, the Commission may decide to approve a code of practice and give it a general validity within the Union, or, alternatively, to provide common rules for the implementation of the relevant obligations
obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital, 'may decide'); describes an implementing power
note: Standard-setting for GPAI providers. Common rules apply if a code 'cannot be finalised or is not deemed adequate by the AI Office'. Providers can rely on codes, or on harmonised standards assessed as suitable by the AI Office (presumption of conformity), or on 'alternative adequate means'.

quote: the Commission should be able to establish, via implementing acts, and after consultation of the advisory forum, common specifications for certain requirements under this Regulation.
obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital, 'should be able to'); describes an implementing power
note: Fallback standard-setting when harmonised standards are absent, rejected, delayed, non-compliant with the request, or 'insufficiently address fundamental rights concerns'. The Commission 'is encouraged to cooperate with international partners and international standardisation bodies'.

quote: the standardisation requests should be issued by the Commission without undue delay. When preparing the standardisation request, the Commission should consult the advisory forum and the Board in order to collect relevant expertise.
note: Standard-setting: harmonised standards are 'a means for providers to demonstrate conformity'. A balanced representation of interests in standard development 'should therefore be encouraged'. Consulting the advisory forum and the Board is also a Coordination link.

quote: those systems should be subject to a conformity assessment prior to their placing on the market or putting into service.
obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital, 'should be subject to'); describes a mandatory pre-market gate
note: Gate on market access and putting into service for high-risk systems. Nearest named actor: provider. Cross-ref Delivery/Design (who carries out the assessment, Recital 125).
basis: AI pass A; different cell in pass B

quote: notified bodies should be notified under this Regulation by the national competent authorities, provided that they comply with a set of requirements, in particular on independence, competence, absence of conflicts of interests and suitable cybersecurity requirements.
note: Appointing who carries out third-party checks. Cross-ref Coordination/Design (notification tool, Recital 126).

quote: market surveillance authorities could authorise the placing on the market or the putting into service of AI systems which have not undergone a conformity assessment.
obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital, 'could authorise'); describes an exceptional power
note: Grounds: 'exceptional reasons of public security or protection of life and health of natural persons, environmental protection and the protection of key industrial and infrastructural assets'.

quote: law enforcement authorities or civil protection authorities may put a specific high-risk AI system into service without the authorisation of the market surveillance authority, provided that such authorisation is requested during or after the use without undue delay.
holder: law enforcement authorities or civil protection authorities
note: Public-sector-specific power to deploy an unassessed high-risk system 'In duly justified situations'. Cross-ref Accountability/Design (same quote).

quote: Member States should not create unjustified obstacles to the placing on the market or the putting into service of high-risk AI systems that comply with the requirements laid down in this Regulation and bear the CE marking
note: Limits Member State authority over compliant systems.

quote: Any significant risks identified during the development and testing of such AI systems should result in adequate mitigation and, failing that, in the suspension of the development and testing process.
if_not_met: suspension of the development and testing process
note: Authority to suspend; the holder is not named here (nearest named actors: national competent authorities supervising the sandbox).

quote: additional safeguards to ensure that the predictions, recommendations or decisions of the AI system can be effectively reversed and disregarded
note: Override of AI outputs during real-world testing; personal data deleted when consent is withdrawn. Nearest named actors: prospective providers and deployers.

quote: requesting informed consent of natural persons to participate in testing in real world conditions, with the exception of law enforcement where the seeking of informed consent would prevent the AI system from being tested
holder: providers or prospective providers (request); natural persons (consent)
obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital, 'should include'); law enforcement exception
note: Consent as a gate on participation in real-world testing outside sandboxes; law-enforcement exception.
basis: AI pass B; different cell in pass A

quote: each Member State should designate at least one notifying authority and at least one market surveillance authority as national competent authorities for the purpose of supervising the application and implementation of this Regulation.
note: Appointing who supervises. 'Member States may decide to appoint any kind of public entity' to do these tasks. Cross-ref Coordination/Design (single point of contact, Recital 153).

quote: The national competent authorities should exercise their powers independently, impartially and without bias
note: A condition on how supervisory authority is exercised. Members 'should refrain from any action incompatible with their duties' and are subject to confidentiality rules.
basis: AI pass A; different cell in pass B

quote: market surveillance authorities may take measures in relation to all AI systems when they present a risk in accordance with this Regulation.
obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital, 'may take measures'); describes a power
note: Authority over all AI systems presenting a risk, not only high-risk ones, 'Although the majority of AI systems are not subject to specific requirements'. The measures are not specified here.

quote: should be designated, within their respective competences, as competent authorities for the purpose of supervising the implementation of this Regulation, including for market surveillance activities, as regards AI systems provided or used by regulated and supervised financial institutions
holder: the competent authorities for the supervision and enforcement of [Union financial services] legal acts
note: Appoints financial supervisors as AI Act supervisors for financial institutions 'unless Member States decide to designate another authority'. Credit-institution supervisors in the Single Supervisory Mechanism should report relevant information to the ECB; limited derogations on providers' quality management systems and deployers' monitoring for credit institutions. Relevance to public-sector tools is indirect (financial institutions) [inference]. The recital begins on line 2092 (in range) and ends on line 2129; it was read to its end.
basis: AI pass A; different cell in pass B

quote: any natural or legal person, including a public authority, agency or other body, using an AI system under its authority
obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital, 'should be interpreted'); describes scope set by the Regulation
note: Scope: the notion of 'deployer' expressly includes public authorities, agencies and other bodies, so public bodies using AI carry deployer obligations; personal non-professional use excluded. Scope is set by the Regulation itself (legislator: European Parliament and Council); nearest named actor: 'a public authority, agency or other body'. See also Recital (23) on EU institutions.

quote: should have effective investigative and corrective powers, including at least the power to obtain access to all personal data that are being processed
holder: Each market surveillance authority for high-risk AI systems in the area of biometrics
note: Verb: should. Applies where biometric high-risk systems are used for law enforcement, migration, asylum and border control, or administration of justice and democratic processes. Recital adds MSAs 'should be able to exercise their powers by acting with complete independence'. Corrective powers = authority to stop or correct tools. Also coded Accountability/Resources (access to data). Operative provisions are in the market surveillance chapter (outside this part).
basis: AI pass A; different cell in pass B

quote: the powers of supervision and enforcement of the obligations on providers of general-purpose AI models should be a competence of the Commission
note: Allocates competence over GPAI model providers. AI Office 'should be able to carry out all necessary actions to monitor the effective implementation of this Regulation as regards general-purpose AI models', on own initiative or on MSA request. Operative Art. 88 (outside this part). Also coded Accountability/Design.

quote: through requests to take appropriate measures, including risk mitigation measures in the case of identified systemic risks as well as restricting the making available on the market, withdrawing or recalling the model
note: Passive ('Compliance with the obligations should be enforceable'); nearest named actor: the AI Office. Authority to restrict, withdraw or recall a GPAI model. Operative provisions outside this part.
basis: AI pass A; different cell in pass B

quote: Providers of AI systems that are not high-risk should be encouraged to create codes of conduct, including related governance mechanisms, intended to foster the voluntary application of some or all of the mandatory requirements applicable to high-risk AI systems
holder: Providers of AI systems that are not high-risk
note: Voluntary self-set standards. Codes 'should be based on clear objectives and key performance indicators' and developed inclusively with business, civil society, academia, research organisations, trade unions and consumer organisations.

quote: Providers and, as appropriate, deployers of all AI systems, high-risk or not, and AI models should also be encouraged to apply on a voluntary basis additional requirements
holder: Providers and, as appropriate, deployers of all AI systems
note: Examples: elements of the Union's Ethics Guidelines for Trustworthy AI, environmental sustainability, AI literacy, inclusive and diverse design incl. accessibility, stakeholder participation, diversity of development teams. Deployers include public authorities.
basis: AI pass A; different cell in pass B

quote: the power to adopt acts in accordance with Article 290 TFEU should be delegated to the Commission to amend the conditions under which an AI system is not to be considered to be high-risk
note: Also the list of high-risk systems, technical documentation, EU declaration content, conformity assessment procedures, GPAI systemic-risk thresholds, benchmarks, indicators and GPAI documentation. Also coded Coordination/Design.

quote: the Commission should carry out an assessment of the need to amend the list of high-risk AI systems and the list of prohibited practices once a year
note: Annual review of scope (which tools are prohibited or high-risk). Trigger: yearly.

quote: In order to ensure uniform conditions for the implementation of this Regulation, implementing powers should be conferred on the Commission.
note: Exercised under Regulation (EU) No 182/2011.

quote: operators of high-risk AI systems that are intended to be used by public authorities should, respectively, take the necessary steps to comply with the requirements of this Regulation by end of 2030 and by 2 August 2030
holder: operators of high-risk AI systems that are intended to be used by public authorities
note: 'Respectively': operators of AI components of large-scale EU IT systems (listed in an annex) by end of 2030; operators of high-risk AI systems intended for public authorities by 2 August 2030. Stated 'On an exceptional basis and in light of public accountability'. Sets the compliance timing for the public-sector object.

quote: applies to the high-risk AI systems that have been placed on the market or put into service before the general date of application thereof, only if, from that date, those systems are subject to significant changes
note: Existing systems are caught only on significant change in design or intended purpose (equivalent to 'substantial modification'). Also coded Decision-making/Design (public-authority deadline).

quote: Providers of high-risk AI systems are encouraged to start to comply, on a voluntary basis, with the relevant obligations of this Regulation already during the transitional period.
note: Voluntary early compliance.
basis: AI pass A; different cell in pass B

quote: the prohibitions as well as the general provisions of this Regulation should already apply from 2 February 2025
note: General application 2 August 2026; notified bodies and governance from 2 August 2025; GPAI provider obligations from 2 August 2025; penalties from 2 August 2025; codes of practice ready by 2 May 2025; Member States to notify penalty rules.

quote: The AI Office should ensure that classification rules and procedures are up to date in light of technological developments.
note: [inference] Refers to GPAI model classification, given the surrounding text.

quote: providers placing on the market or putting into service AI systems or placing on the market general-purpose AI models in the Union, irrespective of whether those providers are established or located within the Union or in a third country
note: Scope set by the Regulation itself. Brings non-EU model and system providers into scope. Art. 2(1)(c): also third-country providers and deployers where output is used in the Union.

quote: deployers of AI systems that have their place of establishment or are located within the Union
note: With Art. 3(4) ('deployer' includes 'public authority, agency or other body'), brings public bodies that use AI into scope.

quote: This Regulation does not apply to AI systems where and in so far they are placed on the market, put into service, or used with or without modification exclusively for military, defence or national security purposes
note: Exclusion applies 'regardless of the type of entity carrying out those activities'; does not affect Member State national-security competences; also excludes systems not placed in the Union whose output is used exclusively for these purposes. Removes these public uses from the Regulation.

quote: applies neither to public authorities in a third country nor to international organisations falling within the scope of this Regulation pursuant to paragraph 1, where those authorities or organisations use AI systems in the framework of international cooperation
note: Condition: international cooperation or agreements for law enforcement and judicial cooperation with the Union or Member States, with adequate safeguards for fundamental rights.

quote: This Regulation applies neither to public authorities in a third country nor to international organisations
holder: not stated (the Regulation sets its scope)
note: Condition: where they use AI systems 'in the framework of international cooperation or agreements for law enforcement and judicial cooperation with the Union or with one or more Member States, provided that such a third country or international organisation provides adequate safeguards with respect to the protection of fundamental rights and freedoms of individuals'. Who judges adequacy is not stated.

quote: does not preclude the Union or Member States from maintaining or introducing laws, regulations or administrative provisions which are more favourable to workers
note: Regarding the use of AI systems by employers; also collective agreements more favourable to workers. [inference] Covers public bodies as employers.

quote: does not apply to AI systems released under free and open-source licences, unless they are placed on the market or put into service as high-risk AI systems
note: Exclusion also does not apply to systems under Art. 5 (prohibited) or Art. 50 (transparency).

quote: This Regulation does not apply to any research, testing or development activity regarding AI systems or AI models prior to their being placed on the market or put into service.
note: 'Testing in real world conditions shall not be covered by that exclusion.' Art. 2(6) also excludes systems/models developed and put into service solely for scientific research and development.

quote: ‘provider’ means a natural or legal person, public authority, agency or other body that develops an AI system or a general-purpose AI model or that has an AI system or a general-purpose AI model developed
note: Definition continues: 'and places it on the market or puts the AI system into service under its own name or trademark'. [inference] A public authority that develops or commissions a system and puts it into service under its own name (incl. own use, Art. 3(11)) holds provider obligations.

quote: ‘deployer’ means a natural or legal person, public authority, agency or other body using an AI system under its authority except where the AI system is used in the course of a personal non-professional activity
note: Makes public authorities that use AI 'deployers', holding deployer obligations (e.g. Arts 4, 26, 27, 49(3), 50).
