[inference] Relevant where a public body builds an AI system on a GPAI model.

quote: The upstream actor should then be considered the provider of the model , unless the upstream actor has excluded, in a clear and unequivocal way, the distribution and use of  the model  on the Union  market
holder: European Commission (interpretation); applies to upstream and downstream actors
note: Applies when the model was first made available outside the Union. If the upstream actor excluded Union use, the downstream actor that integrates it and places the system on the Union market 'should be considered the provider of the model' (spans a page break). [inference] A public-sector integrator could then carry model-provider duties.

quote: the Commission considers a downstream modifier to become the provider of the mo dified general -purpose AI model only if the modification lead s to a significant change in the model’s generality, capabilities, or systemic risk.
holder: European Commission (interpretation); applies to downstream modifiers
note: Indicative criterion (para (60)): modification compute 'greater than a third of  the training compute of the original model'. Fallbacks (para (61)): a third of 10^25 FLOP (systemic-risk original) or of 10^23 FLOP. Footnote 13: who modifies is case by case; control over weights matters. [inference] A public body that heavily fine-tunes a GPAI model could become a provider.

quote: For providers meeting the conditio ns referred to in Section 4.2,  the following obligations do not apply, unless their model is a general -purpose AI model with systemic risk
holder: not stated (exception set by the AI Act; conditions interpreted by the European Commission)
obligation: statutory exemption; its conditions are non-binding interpretation
note: Exempted: Art. 53(1)(a), (b) documentation and Art. 54 representative. Not exempted: copyright policy, training summary (para (72)). Conditions: licence allowing access, use, modification, distribution (paras (73)-(81); disqualifying restrictions para (80)); no monetisation (paras (82)-(86)); public weights, architecture, usage information (paras (87)-(89)). Safety-oriented use limits allowed if proportionate (para (81)).

quote: Nevertheless, t hese guidelines set out  the Commission’s interpretation and application of the AI Act, on which it will base its enforcement action.
note: 'These guidelines are not binding for providers of general -purpose AI models; an authoritative interpretation of the AI Act may only be given by the Court of Justice'. 'a case -by-case assessment will always be necessary'. The Commission sets the scope it will enforce; the scope entries below follow.

quote: The Commission may also approve a code of practice via implementing act, thereby giving it general validi ty within the Union (Article 56(6) AI Act).
note: 'If a code of practice cannot be finalised by 2 August 2025, the Commission may adopt common rules via implementing act'. Adequacy of a code is assessed 'by the AI Office and the Board' (para (91)), which is also decision-making.

quote: If, after a standardi sation request, harmonised standards are not developed in time or in a satisfactory manner, the Commission may adopt common specifications via an implementing act
note: Standard-setting. 'compliance with harmonised standards grants a presumption of conformity'; codes of practice are temporary until standards exist.

quote: The committee is responsible for guiding the implementation of the ECA’s AI strategy and roadmap and prioritising cross-departmental AI initiatives.
location: AI governance at the ECA, para 18 (p. 7)
note: Established 2025 'to oversee the development and deployment of AI systems within the ECA'. Composition not stated.

quote: In 2025, the ECA also established an AI Steering Committee to oversee the development and deployment of AI systems within the ECA.
location: AI governance at the ECA, para 18, p. 7
note: Body with authority over AI development and deployment in the ECA. Same para: 'The committee is responsible for guiding the implementation of the ECA’s AI strategy and roadmap and prioritising cross-departmental AI initiatives.' Already established, so possibly a report; coded because it is the strategy's statement of who decides. Composition not stated.

quote: Based on future developments, the AI Steering Committee will decide on the appropriate mix and allocation and monitor the progress of this action.
note: Decides which general-purpose AI tools staff get and how they are allocated; also monitors progress (Delivery element).

quote: the ECA will acquire sufficient licences to provide all staff with access to at least one general-purpose AI tool. We will continually evaluate costs and benefits.
note: Decision to deploy general-purpose AI to all staff (para 3: 'by early 2026'; para 22: half of staff had access by November 2025). Ongoing cost-benefit evaluation. Para 40: the ECA will 'explore the adoption of solutions created and tested by other institutions' and 'consider running on-site AI models to enable automation and ensure strict data confidentiality when needed'.
basis: AI pass B; different cell in pass A

quote: we will issue clear guidelines and organise awareness sessions, focusing in particular on the ethical implications and concerns associated with AI adoption.
note: Internal guidelines for staff use of AI tools; content not stated. Awareness sessions are also a resource.
basis: AI pass A; different cell in pass B

quote: define standards and request that data be provided in a structured way whenever possible;
note: Standard-setting for data the ECA receives (including from auditees); also a coordination element with auditees.

quote: It is equally essential to review and enhance our data classification policy, to ensure that it is consistent (on AI and other aspects) with the policies of our auditees, especially the European Commission
note: Setting internal data policy; consistency with the Commission is also a coordination element.
basis: AI pass A; different cell in pass B

quote: we will systematically review the market to identify solutions that best meet our institutional requirements. When evaluating proposed AI enhancements, we will carefully assess their potential added value relative to associated costs.
note: Tool selection criteria: institutional requirements; added value relative to cost. Same para: benchmark against 'other supreme audit institutions and the European Commission'.

quote: We will regularly review and, when needed, revise our guidance, incorporating best practices from the wider audit profession, including those emerging from organisations such as the INTOSAI community and ISACA.
note: Setting the ECA's own standards for auditing AI. Trigger: regular review. Also para 30: monitor international developments and incorporate them into audit methodology.
basis: AI pass A; different cell in pass B

quote: We will ensure that all AI tools and processes deployed at the ECA comply with the requirements of the EU AI Act and other relevant EU legislation.
note: 'Ensure': [inference] the ECA as deployer can approve or stop its own tools, so coded as decision-making; what it involves is coded under Delivery/Design and Accountability/Design (same para). Para 65: compliance is 'critical ... to maintain the trust, integrity, and legality of our operations'.
basis: AI pass B; different cell in pass A

quote: In addition, we could consider adopting relevant elements of ISO/IEC 42001, the Artificial Intelligence Management System standard (see Annex I).
note: Optional adoption of a management-system standard 'for managing AI risks and opportunities'.

quote: Any such use would be limited to a preliminary assessment, with human review and final decision‑making remaining fully with the selection panels
note: Human final decision over AI screening of candidates' eligibility. Also coded as Delivery/Design (human review). Edge: candidates are external applicants; AI used by the body on them.

quote: For performance audits, we will adopt a dynamic approach by regularly reviewing pilot initiatives, assessing their outcomes, and scaling up those which demonstrate clear success across the organisation.
note: Decision to scale based on pilot review. Trigger: regular review. Metric: 'clear success' (not defined).

quote: We are also planning a mid-term strategy review to ensure that we are making proper progress toward achieving our objectives.
note: Review of the strategy itself, allowing direction to be revisited in light of 'significant developments ... in the field of AI'. Trigger: mid-term. Could also be read as Delivery (evaluation).

quote: the operational details will be shaped and formalised through annual work programmes developed by the relevant departments.
note: The strategy itself does not specify projects; detail delegated to annual work programmes.

quote: Following further analysis and approval by the AI Steering Committee, the identified strategic actions may be developed into specific projects.
if_not_met: action not developed into a project [inference]
note: Approval gate before projects. Operational planning goes into directorates' annual work programmes. Cross-ref Delivery/Design (project performance indicators).

quote: the Commission itself will already now, set a positive example and subject itself to the envisaged rules.
note: Decision to apply AI Act rules to itself before they apply. Footnote 1: references to be read as the Commission's proposal until adoption.

quote: This vision and these operational solutions must be of a living nature, they will be reviewed and updated regularly to reflect:
note: Triggers for review: dynamic nature of AI, lessons learned, changes in regulatory and policy framework.

quote: Put in place organisati onal structures (a governance) to fulfil the obligations of the Commission in relation to AI.
note: Appointing who decides; structure set out in 2.2.1. Extraction spacing ('organisati onal') quoted as is.

quote: Develop internal operational guidelines that give staff – users, developers or procurers of AI systems – clear and pragmatic guidance how to put such systems in operation.
note: Standard-setting. Guidelines to build on the AI Act, existing legislation, Commission policy, HLEG Ethics guidelines and best practice (p. 5). The Commission will consider planned EU initiatives, applicable legislation (non-discrimination, accessibility, information security, data protection) and best practice.

quote: Refrain from using any AI systems that are considered incompatible with European values or that represent a threat to the security, safety, health, and fundamental rights of people.
location: 2.1 The Commission as an early adopter of the AI Act’s risk-based approach (PDF p. 5)
note: Stop/prohibition rule. Who decides that a system is 'considered incompatible' is not stated.

quote: this existing board oversees investments in AI information technology ensuring alignment with the Commission’s digital strategy and business needs.
note: Investment authority over AI IT. Also coded as Delivery/Design (compliance check at initiation).

quote: this existing board ensures that AI-related initiatives are aligned with the Commission’s information and data policies.
note: 'Ensures' read as authority over alignment [inference]; power to stop not stated.

quote: The Network will suggest any projects and investments to the Interservice Steering Group on AI for assessment and decision via the existing corporate IT governance.
holder: ISG-AI (assessment and decision) via corporate IT governance; AI@EC Network (suggests)
note: Decision route for new AI projects; the Network only suggests (also a coordination/referral mechanism).

quote: The ISG -AI will set policies, create fra meworks, identify synergies, and draft operational guidelines for the use of AI in the Commission.
note: New subgroup of the Information Management Steering Board; in charge of coordinating and implementing AI@EC and overseeing the AI@EC Network.

quote: Draw up guidelines on the use of specific AI systems : rules for the use of specific tools, such as the internal guidelines already been drawn up for the use of third -party online generative Artificial Intelligence tools.
note: Tool-specific use rules, incl. third-party online generative AI (value chain). Timeline: existing, review by Q2/2024, then update as appropriate.

quote: Develop concrete operational guidelines : thematic guidelines for staff, to be applied for the selection, acquisition, development, testing and deployment of AI solutions (at corporate and policy level), taking a risk-based approach
note: Includes AI cybersecurity topics. Timeline: Q2/2024, then updates as appropriate.

quote: the Commission will now ensure a clear prioritisation of AI projects and related investments.

note: Transitional deadline for existing models, which may sit inside public-sector tools.
basis: AI pass B; different cell in pass A

quote: The technical documentation referred to in Article 11(1) shall contain at least the following information, as applicable to the relevant AI system:
if_not_met: not stated in the Annex; formal non-compliance if 'technical documentation is not available' (Art. 83(1)(g))
note: Recording. Nearest named actor: the provider (Annex IV 2(a) 'modified by the provider'). Contents: general description; development process and design; monitoring, functioning and control; appropriateness of performance metrics; risk management system; lifecycle changes (item 6); standards applied; EU declaration of conformity; post-market evaluation system and plan (item 9). Specific items coded separately.

quote: including, where relevant, recourse to pre-trained systems or tools provided by third parties and how those were used, integrated or modified by the provider;
note: Records value-chain dependence (e.g. on a third-party model). Nearest named actor: the provider.

quote: what the system is designed to optimise for, and the relevance of the different parameters; the description of the expected output and output quality of the system
note: Records design specifications: general logic, key design choices with rationale and assumptions, including about the persons or groups the system is used on, main classification choices, and trade-offs made to meet Chapter III, Section 2. Nearest named actor: the provider.

quote: the key design choices including the rationale and assumptions made, including with regard to persons or groups of persons in respect of who, the system is intended to be used; the main classification choices
if_not_met: Art. 83(1)(g): if technical documentation 'is not available' the MSA requires the provider to end the non-compliance
note: Record of design and specification choices. Nearest named actor: the provider (Annex IV 1(a) 'the name of the provider'; duty in Art. 11(1), outside part 3). Same point: 'what the system is designed to optimise for', expected output quality, and 'decisions about any possible trade-off'. Point 2(d): training data provenance, labelling, cleaning.

quote: assessment of the human oversight measures needed in accordance with Article 14, including an assessment of the technical measures needed to facilitate the interpretation of the outputs of AI systems by the deployers
note: Assessment supporting deployers' human oversight. Nearest named actor: the provider. Point 3 also records 'the human oversight measures needed'.

quote: metrics used to measure accuracy, robustness and compliance with other relevant requirements set out in Chapter III, Section 2, as well as potentially discriminatory impacts
note: Validation and testing record. Trigger: development, and pre-determined changes (point 2(f)). Compared against: Chapter III, Section 2 requirements. Metrics: accuracy, robustness, potentially discriminatory impacts (specific metrics not prescribed). Also records validation and testing data and their characteristics. Also coded Accountability/Design (signed test reports).

quote: its capabilities and limitations in performance, including the degrees of accuracy for specific persons or groups of persons on which the system is intended to be used and the overall expected level of accuracy
note: Records performance limits by group, foreseeable unintended outcomes and risks to health, safety, fundamental rights and discrimination, oversight measures, and input-data specifications. Nearest named actor: the provider.

quote: A description of the appropriateness of the performance metrics for the specific AI system;
note: Justification of the metrics chosen. Nearest named actor: the provider.

quote: A detailed description of the system in place to evaluate the AI system performance in the post-market phase in accordance with Article 72, including the post-market monitoring plan referred to in Article 72(3).
note: Documentation of ongoing monitoring. Point 6: 'relevant changes made by the provider to the system through its lifecycle'. Point 7: harmonised standards applied, or solutions adopted.

quote: The provider examines the information contained in the technical documentation in order to assess the compliance of the AI system with the relevant essential requirements set out in Chapter III, Section 2.
note: Self-assessment with no third party. Also verifies the quality management system against Art. 17 (point 2) and that design, development and post-market monitoring are consistent with the documentation (point 4). Trigger: before placing on the market [inference]. [inference] When this route applies is set by Art. 43, outside this part.

quote: The quality management system shall be assessed by the notified body, which shall determine whether it satisfies the requirements referred to in Article 17.
note: Third-party check. Compared against: Art. 17. Decision notified with 'the reasoned assessment decision'. Provider's application contents in point 3.1. [inference] When this route applies is set by Art. 43, outside this part.
basis: AI pass A; different cell in pass B

quote: The technical documentation shall be examined by the notified body.
note: Third-party check of Annex IV documentation, on application by the provider (4.1-4.2). Also coded Delivery/Resources (data access).

quote: Where the notified body is not satisfied with the tests carried out by the provider, the notified body shall itself directly carry out adequate tests, as appropriate.
note: Independent testing. May also require the provider to supply further evidence or carry out further tests. Compared against: Chapter III, Section 2.

quote: The technical documentation referred to in Article 53(1), point (a) shall contain at least the following information as appropriate to the size and risk profile of the model:
if_not_met: not stated in the Annex; [inference] Commission information requests and fines (Arts. 91, 101)
note: Model documentation: intended tasks and AI systems it can be integrated into; acceptable use policies; release and distribution; architecture and parameters; modalities; licence; integration means; design and training choices; training, testing and validation data, including 'methods to detect identifiable biases'; compute; energy consumption.

quote: A detailed description of the evaluation strategies, including evaluation results, on the basis of available public evaluation protocols and tools or otherwise of other evaluation methodologies.
holder: Providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk
note: Model evaluation record: 'Evaluation strategies shall include evaluation criteria, metrics and the methodology on the identification of limitations'. Trigger: not stated in the Annex. Metrics: chosen by the provider. Also coded Delivery/Design (adversarial testing).

quote: a detailed description of the measures put in place for the purpose of conducting internal and/or external adversarial testing (e.g. red teaming), model adaptations, including alignment and fine-tuning.
holder: Providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk
note: Red-teaming record. Point 3: system architecture where applicable.

quote: a provider who considers that an AI system is not high-risk on the basis of the conditions referred to above should draw up documentation of the assessment before that system is placed on the market or put into service
holder: a provider who considers that an AI system is not high-risk
note: Recording the provider's classification assessment. Trigger: before placing on the market or putting into service; compared against: the four derogation conditions and the profiling rule; metric: not stated. Cross-ref Decision-making/Design and Accountability/Design (Recital 53).

quote: The measures adopted by the providers to comply with the mandatory requirements of this Regulation should take into account the generally acknowledged state of the art on AI, be proportionate and effective
note: Comparator for all provider checks: 'generally acknowledged state of the art'. Providers of products under NLF legislation may fold testing and documentation into existing procedures.

quote: The risk-management system should consist of a continuous, iterative process that is planned and run throughout the entire lifecycle of a high-risk AI system.
note: Recital (64) says the system is 'to be established by the provider' and measures should reflect 'the generally acknowledged state of the art'. Trigger: ongoing over the lifecycle, 'regularly reviewed and updated'; compared against: known and reasonably foreseeable risks to health, safety and fundamental rights in light of intended purpose and reasonably foreseeable misuse; metric: not stated.

quote: When identifying the most appropriate risk-management measures, the provider should document and explain the choices made and, when relevant, involve experts and external stakeholders.
note: Recording and justifying risk-management choices; involving outside experts and stakeholders is also a Coordination mechanism (not separately coded). Providers are 'encouraged' to consider additional training measures for foreseeable misuse.
basis: AI pass A; different cell in pass B

quote: Data sets for training, validation and testing, including the labels, should be relevant, sufficiently representative, and to the best extent possible free of errors and complete in view of the intended purpose of the system.
note: Data governance check. Trigger: development (training, validation, testing); compared against: intended purpose and the persons or groups on whom the system is used, with 'specific attention to the mitigation of possible biases' including feedback loops; metric: not stated ('appropriate statistical properties'). Nearest named actor: provider.

quote: This process should ensure that the provider identifies risks or adverse impacts and implements mitigation measures for the known and reasonably foreseeable risks of AI systems to the health, safety and fundamental rights
note: Risk-management system: 'continuous, iterative process ... throughout the entire lifecycle', 'regularly reviewed and updated'. Covers intended purpose and reasonably foreseeable misuse. Trigger: ongoing. Comparator: state of the art. Metric: not stated.

quote: the providers should, exceptionally, to the extent that it is strictly necessary for the purpose of ensuring bias detection and correction in relation to the high-risk AI systems, subject to appropriate safeguards
obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital, 'should ... be able to'); describes a power
note: Permits providers to 'process also special categories of personal data' for bias detection and correction, as a substantial public interest under GDPR Art. 9(2)(g) and EUDPR Art. 10(2)(g), subject to safeguards.
basis: AI pass A; different cell in pass B

quote: The technical documentation should be kept up to date, appropriately throughout the lifetime of the AI system.
note: Contents: general characteristics, capabilities and limitations, algorithms, data, training, testing and validation processes, and risk-management documentation. Purpose: traceability, verifying compliance, post-market monitoring (also serves Accountability). Trigger: ongoing. Nearest named actor: provider.

quote: high-risk AI systems should technically allow for the automatic recording of events, by means of logs, over the duration of the lifetime of the system.
note: Logging capability built into the system. Nearest named actor: provider. Trigger: continuous over the lifetime.

quote: Measures taken by providers to ensure compliance with those principles may include not only anonymisation and encryption, but also the use of technology that permits algorithms to be brought to the data
note: Principles are data minimisation and data protection by design and by default from Union data protection law, which 'are applicable'; privacy 'must be guaranteed throughout the entire lifecycle'.

quote: High-risk AI systems should be designed in a manner to enable deployers to understand how the AI system works, evaluate its functionality, and comprehend its strengths and limitations.
note: Transparency 'should be required for high-risk AI systems before they are placed on the market or put it into service'. Nearest named actor: provider. Serves deployers' evaluation and correct use.

quote: appropriate human oversight measures should be identified by the provider of the system before its placing on the market or putting into service.
note: Trigger: before placing on the market or putting into service. Where appropriate, measures include 'in-built operational constraints that cannot be overridden by the system itself' and responsiveness to the human operator. Cross-ref Decision-making/Design and Decision-making/Resources (Recital 73).

quote: no action or decision may be taken by the deployer on the basis of the identification resulting from the system unless this has been separately verified and confirmed by at least two natural persons.
obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital); describes an enhanced human oversight requirement
note: Human review of output for certain biometric identification systems. Trigger: each identification; compared against: separate verification by two persons; recording: 'could be sufficient' that verifications are 'automatically recorded in the logs'. Also limits decisions (Decision-making). Exemption for law enforcement, migration, border control and asylum: see next entry.

quote: High-risk AI systems should perform consistently throughout their lifecycle and meet an appropriate level of accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity, in light of their intended purpose and in accordance with the generally acknowledged state of the art.
note: Trigger: throughout the lifecycle; compared against: intended purpose and state of the art; metric: 'The expected level of performance metrics should be declared in the accompanying instructions of use' (no specific metric set). Nearest named actor: provider. Cross-ref Delivery/Resources (Recital 74).

quote: technical and organisational measures should be taken to ensure robustness of high-risk AI systems, for example by designing and developing appropriate technical solutions to prevent or minimise harmful or otherwise undesirable behaviour.
note: Examples include 'fail-safe plans' to safely interrupt operation in anomalies or outside predetermined boundaries. Nearest named actor: provider.

quote: suitable measures, such as security controls, should therefore be taken by the providers of high-risk AI systems, also taking into account as appropriate the underlying ICT infrastructure.
holder: the providers of high-risk AI systems
note: Cybersecurity against data poisoning, adversarial attacks, membership inference and attacks on ICT infrastructure. Trigger and metric: not stated.

quote: It is therefore essential that providers ensure full compliance with accessibility requirements, including Directive (EU) 2016/2102 of the European Parliament and of the Council (38) and Directive (EU) 2019/882. Providers should ensure compliance with these requirements by design.
note: Accessibility by design; Directive 2016/2102 concerns public sector bodies' websites and apps (footnote 38). Trigger: design stage.

quote: The provider should establish a sound quality management system, ensure the accomplishment of the required conformity assessment procedure, draw up the relevant documentation and establish a robust post-market monitoring system.
note: Bundle of provider delivery duties. Cross-ref Recital (81) public-authority option (next entry), Recitals (123), (125) and (155).

quote: Public authorities which put into service high-risk AI systems for their own use may adopt and implement the rules for the quality management system as part of the quality management system adopted at a national or regional level
holder: Public authorities which put into service high-risk AI systems for their own use
note: Public-sector-specific flexibility for public bodies acting as providers of their own systems, 'taking into account the specificities of the sector and the competences and organisation of the public authority concerned'.

quote: Deployers should in particular take appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure they use high-risk AI systems in accordance with the instructions of use
note: Also 'certain other obligations' on 'monitoring of the functioning of the AI systems and with regard to record-keeping'. Trigger: ongoing use; compared against: the provider's instructions of use; metric: not stated. Cross-ref Delivery/Resources (Recital 91).

quote: should carry out a fundamental rights impact assessment prior to putting it into use.
holder: deployers of high-risk AI systems that are bodies governed by public law, or private entities providing public services and deployers of certain high-risk AI systems listed in an annex to this Regulation, such as banking or insurance entities
obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital, 'should carry out'); one duty at two levels: public bodies and private providers of public services, and certain other deployers (e.g. banking, insurance)
note: Fundamental rights impact assessment. Trigger: before deployment; 'should be updated when the deployer considers that any of the relevant factors have changed'. Content: the deployer's processes, period and frequency of use, categories of persons and groups likely affected, specific risks of harm to fundamental rights; take into account 'the information given by the provider ... in the instructions for use'. Compared against: fundamental rights; metric: not stated. Cross-ref Decision-making/Design, Accountability/Design, Coordination/Design and Delivery/Resources (Recital 96).

quote: providers of general-purpose AI models should put in place a policy to comply with Union law on copyright and related rights
note: In particular to identify and comply with rights reservations under Art. 4(3) of Directive (EU) 2019/790, 'regardless of the jurisdiction in which the copyright-relevant acts underpinning the training ... take place'. Recital (104): the open-source exception does not cover this duty.

quote: this Regulation should require providers to perform the necessary model evaluations, in particular prior to its first placing on the market, including conducting and documenting adversarial testing of models, also, as appropriate, through internal or independent external testing.
holder: providers of general-purpose AI models presenting systemic risks
note: Model evaluation and adversarial testing. Trigger: in particular before first placing on the market; compared against: systemic risks; metric: not stated. Applies whether the model is standalone or embedded in a system or product.

quote: providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risks should continuously assess and mitigate systemic risks, including for example by putting in place risk-management policies, such as accountability and governance processes, implementing post-market monitoring
holder: providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risks
note: Ongoing risk assessment, mitigation and post-market monitoring 'along the entire model’s lifecycle', and 'cooperating with relevant actors along the AI value chain'. Trigger: continuous.

quote: providers should ensure an adequate level of cybersecurity protection for the model and its physical infrastructure, if appropriate, along the entire model lifecycle.
holder: providers (of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk)
note: Covers accidental model leakage, unauthorised releases, circumvention of safety measures, cyberattacks, unauthorised access and model theft; e.g. securing model weights.

quote: those systems should be subject to a conformity assessment prior to their placing on the market or putting into service
obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital, 'should be subject to'); describes a mandatory pre-market gate
note: Nearest actor: provider (recital (125)). Trigger: before placing on market or putting into service. Compares against the Regulation's requirements.
basis: AI pass B; different cell in pass A

quote: the conformity assessment of such systems should be carried out as a general rule by the provider under its own responsibility, with the only exception of AI systems intended to be used for biometrics.
note: For high-risk systems not related to products (the annex use cases, which include most public-sector uses [inference]), self-assessment by the provider; third-party assessment by notified bodies only for biometrics, 'at least in an initial phase'. Trigger: before placing on the market or putting into service (Recital 123).

quote: when the intended purpose of the system changes, that AI system should be considered to be a new AI system which should undergo a new conformity assessment
note: Trigger for a re-check: any change that may affect compliance (e.g. 'change of operating system or software architecture') or a change of intended purpose. Not a substantial modification: learning changes 'pre-determined by the provider and assessed at the moment of the conformity assessment'. Nearest named actor: provider.

quote: it is appropriate to require providers of those systems to embed technical solutions that enable marking in a machine readable format and detection that the output has been generated or manipulated by an AI system and not a human
holder: providers of those systems (AI systems generating synthetic content)
obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital, 'it is appropriate to require')
note: Techniques: watermarks, metadata, cryptographic provenance, logging, fingerprints; 'sufficiently reliable, interoperable, effective and robust as far as this is technically feasible'; may be done at model level incl. GPAI. Not for assistive standard editing. Edge case: marking lets others, including public bodies, check whether incoming content is AI-generated.
basis: AI pass B; different cell in pass A

quote: requesting informed consent of natural persons to participate in testing in real world conditions, with the exception of law enforcement where the seeking of informed consent would prevent the AI system from being tested.
holder: providers or prospective providers (testing high-risk AI systems in real world conditions)
obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital, 'should include'); law enforcement exception
note: Condition of real-world testing outside a sandbox. Consent here is distinct from data-protection consent. Public-sector exception for law enforcement. Cross-ref Accountability, Coordination and Decision-making entries for Recital (141).
basis: AI pass A; different cell in pass B

quote: all providers should have a post-market monitoring system in place. Where relevant, post-market monitoring should include an analysis of the interaction with other AI systems including other devices and software.
note: Monitoring use after deployment. Trigger: ongoing; also addresses systems that 'continue to ‘learn’'. Public-sector carve-out: 'Post-market monitoring should not cover sensitive operational data of deployers which are law enforcement authorities.' Cross-ref Accountability/Design (incident reporting, Recital 155).

quote: Providers and, as appropriate, deployers of all AI systems, high-risk or not, and AI models should also be encouraged to apply on a voluntary basis additional requirements
holder: Providers and, as appropriate, deployers of all AI systems, high-risk or not, and AI models
note: Examples given: elements of the Union's Ethics Guidelines for Trustworthy AI, environmental sustainability, AI literacy measures, inclusive and diverse design, attention to vulnerable persons and accessibility, stakeholder participation, diversity of development teams. Encouraged only; deployers include public bodies.
basis: AI pass B; different cell in pass A

quote: Providers of high-risk AI systems are encouraged to start to comply, on a voluntary basis, with the relevant obligations of this Regulation already during the transitional period.
note: Verb 'are encouraged'. Voluntary early compliance.
basis: AI pass B; different cell in pass A

quote: The use of the ‘real-time’ remote biometric identification system in publicly accessible spaces shall be authorised only if the law enforcement authority has completed a fundamental rights impact assessment as provided for in Article 27
if_not_met: use is not to be authorised ('shall be authorised only if')
note: Check: fundamental rights impact assessment (Art. 27); trigger: before use; compares against: not stated here; metric: not stated. Also coded Accountability/Design (registration).

quote: A provider who considers that an AI system referred to in Annex III is not high-risk shall document its assessment before that system is placed on the market or put into service.
note: Check trigger: before placing on market/putting into service; compares against Art. 6(3) conditions; metric not stated. [inference] The provider in effect self-classifies; no prior external approval. Provider must register under Art. 49(2). Also coded Accountability/Design.

quote: High-risk AI systems shall comply with the requirements laid down in this Section, taking into account their intended purpose as well as the generally acknowledged state of the art on AI and AI-related technologies.
if_not_met: Not stated here. Providers must ensure compliance with Section 2 (Art. 16(a)); breach of Art. 16 attracts fines up to EUR 15 000 000 or 3% of worldwide turnover (Art. 99(4)(a), outside this part); Union bodies up to EUR 750 000 (Art. 100(3)).
note: Passive; nearest named actor: providers (Art. 16(a)). Umbrella for Arts 9-15; standard = intended purpose and state of the art. Art. 8(2): for Annex I Section A products providers are responsible for full compliance and may integrate testing and documentation into existing procedures.

quote: providers shall be responsible for ensuring that their product is fully compliant with all applicable requirements under applicable Union harmonisation legislation
obligation: statutory duty (with option to integrate procedures)
if_not_met: not stated here; Art. 99(4)(a) (outside this part) for provider obligations
note: Applies where a product contains an AI system subject to Annex I Section A legislation. Providers may integrate testing, reporting, information and documentation into existing procedures under that legislation, to 'avoid duplication and minimise additional burdens'.

quote: A risk management system shall be established, implemented, documented and maintained in relation to high-risk AI systems.
if_not_met: Not stated here. Providers must ensure compliance with Section 2 (Art. 16(a)); breach of Art. 16 attracts fines up to EUR 15 000 000 or 3% (Art. 99(4)(a), outside this part); Union bodies up to EUR 750 000 (Art. 100(3)).
note: Passive; nearest named actor: providers (Art. 9(9), 16(a)). Art. 9(2): 'a continuous iterative process planned and run throughout the entire lifecycle', with 'regular systematic review and updating'. Steps: identify/analyse known and foreseeable risks to health, safety, fundamental rights; estimate/evaluate under intended use and foreseeable misuse; evaluate risks from post-market monitoring data (Art. 72); adopt targeted measures. Trigger: ongoing.

quote: the relevant residual risk associated with each hazard, as well as the overall residual risk of the high-risk AI systems is judged to be acceptable
if_not_met: Not stated here. Breach of Art. 16(a) (Section 2 compliance): fines up to EUR 15 000 000 or 3% (Art. 99(4)(a), outside this part).
note: Acceptance criterion: residual risk 'judged to be acceptable'; who judges and against what threshold is not stated. Order of measures: (a) eliminate or reduce through design; (b) mitigation and control; (c) information (Art. 13) and training to deployers. Due consideration to the deployer's 'technical knowledge, experience, education, the training to be expected' and context of use. Also coded Delivery/Resources (9(5)(c)).
basis: AI pass B; different cell in pass A

quote: Training, validation and testing data sets shall be subject to data governance and management practices appropriate for the intended purpose of the high-risk AI system.
if_not_met: Not stated here. Breach of Art. 16(a): fines up to EUR 15 000 000 or 3% (Art. 99(4)(a), outside this part).
note: Passive; nearest actor: provider. For systems trained with data (10(1)); otherwise testing data only (10(6)). Practices cover design choices, data collection and origin, preparation, assumptions, availability and suitability, bias examination and mitigation, data gaps.

quote: examination in view of possible biases that are likely to affect the health and safety of persons, have a negative impact on fundamental rights or lead to discrimination prohibited under Union law
if_not_met: Not stated here. Breach of Art. 16(a): fines up to EUR 15 000 000 or 3% (Art. 99(4)(a), outside this part).
note: Check: bias examination, 'especially where data outputs influence inputs for future operations'; (g) measures to detect, prevent and mitigate biases. Trigger: not stated (development). Compares against discrimination prohibited under Union law. Metric: not stated.

quote: Training, validation and testing data sets shall be relevant, sufficiently representative, and to the best extent possible, free of errors and complete in view of the intended purpose.
obligation: statutory duty ('to the best extent possible')
if_not_met: Not stated here. Breach of Art. 16(a): fines up to EUR 15 000 000 or 3% (Art. 99(4)(a), outside this part).
note: Appropriate statistical properties incl. for persons or groups on whom used. 10(4): account for geographical, contextual, behavioural or functional setting. Art. 42(1): data reflecting the setting gives presumption of compliance with 10(4).

quote: Testing shall be carried out against prior defined metrics and probabilistic thresholds that are appropriate to the intended purpose of the high-risk AI system.
if_not_met: Not stated here. Breach of Art. 16(a): fines up to EUR 15 000 000 or 3% (Art. 99(4)(a), outside this part); Union bodies up to EUR 750 000 (Art. 100(3)).
note: Trigger: 'as appropriate, at any time throughout the development process, and, in any event, prior to their being placed on the market or put into service'. Compares against prior defined metrics and probabilistic thresholds (values set by the tester, not stated). Purpose (9(6)): identify risk measures, ensure consistent performance and Section 2 compliance. May include real-world testing (9(7), Art. 60).

quote: providers shall give consideration to whether in view of its intended purpose the high-risk AI system is likely to have an adverse impact on persons under the age of 18 and, as appropriate, other vulnerable groups
if_not_met: Not stated here. Breach of Art. 16(a): fines up to EUR 15 000 000 or 3% (Art. 99(4)(a), outside this part).
note: Art. 9(10): may be combined with risk procedures under other Union law.

quote: The technical documentation of a high-risk AI system shall be drawn up before that system is placed on the market or put into service and shall be kept up-to date.
if_not_met: Not stated here. Breach of Art. 16 obligations: fines up to EUR 15 000 000 or 3% (Art. 99(4)(a), outside this part).
note: Passive; nearest actor: provider (Arts 16, 18). Recording duty; trigger before placing/putting into service, kept up to date. Minimum content Annex IV. Art. 11(2): single set for Annex I Section A products. Also coded Accountability/Design.

quote: High-risk AI systems shall technically allow for the automatic recording of events (logs) over the lifetime of the system.
if_not_met: Not stated here. Breach of Art. 16(a): fines up to EUR 15 000 000 or 3% (Art. 99(4)(a), outside this part).
note: Passive; nearest actor: provider (builds the capability). Logs must allow recording events relevant to identifying risk or substantial modification, post-market monitoring (Art. 72) and deployer monitoring (Art. 26(5)). Trigger: continuous.

quote: the identification of the natural persons involved in the verification of the results, as referred to in Article 14(5).
if_not_met: Not stated here. Breach of Art. 16(a): fines up to EUR 15 000 000 or 3% (Art. 99(4)(a), outside this part).
note: Minimum logs for remote biometric identification systems (Annex III point 1(a)): period of each use, reference database, matching input data, and the persons who verified results. Records who checked outputs, supporting later accountability.

quote: The authorities competent for supervision of the law enforcement and judicial authorities under this Regulation should assess whether those frameworks for cooperation or international agreements include adequate safeguards
holder: The authorities competent for supervision of the law enforcement and judicial authorities under this Regulation
note: Check: whether cooperation frameworks or international agreements with third-country public authorities and international organisations include adequate safeguards. Trigger: not stated; compared against: 'adequate safeguards with respect to the protection of fundamental rights and freedoms of individuals'; metric: not stated. The result conditions the exclusion of those third-country authorities from the Regulation (bears on Decision-making: scope).

quote: High-risk AI systems shall be designed and developed in such a way, including with appropriate human-machine interface tools, that they can be effectively overseen by natural persons during the period in which they are in use.
if_not_met: Not stated here. Breach of Art. 16(a): fines up to EUR 15 000 000 or 3% (Art. 99(4)(a), outside this part).
note: Passive; nearest actor: provider. Oversight aims to prevent or minimise risks to health, safety, fundamental rights (14(2)); measures commensurate with risk, autonomy, context (14(3)). Trigger: throughout use.

quote: measures identified by the provider before placing the high-risk AI system on the market or putting it into service and that are appropriate to be implemented by the deployer
if_not_met: Not stated here. Provider breach: Art. 99(4)(a); deployer breach of Art. 26: Art. 99(4)(e) (outside this part).
note: Splits oversight delivery: (a) measures built in by the provider; (b) measures for the deployer to implement. Trigger: before placing/putting into service.

quote: to remain aware of the possible tendency of automatically relying or over-relying on the output produced by a high-risk AI system (automation bias)
holder: natural persons to whom human oversight is assigned (enabled by the provider's design)
if_not_met: Not stated here. Breach of Art. 16(a): fines up to EUR 15 000 000 or 3% (Art. 99(4)(a), outside this part).
note: System must enable overseers (a) to understand capacities and limitations and monitor operation, detecting anomalies; (b) to remain aware of automation bias, esp. where outputs inform decisions by natural persons; (c) to correctly interpret output. Duty sits on the system design (provider); persons are named as those enabled.
basis: AI pass A; different cell in pass B

quote: unless that identification has been separately verified and confirmed by at least two natural persons with the necessary competence, training and authority
holder: the deployer (verification by at least two natural persons)
if_not_met: Not stated here. Breach of Art. 16(a) or 26: Art. 99(4)(a)/(e) (outside this part).
note: Human review of outputs for remote biometric identification (Annex III point 1(a)): no action or decision by the deployer on an identification without two-person verification. Not applicable to law enforcement, migration, border control or asylum where Union or national law considers it disproportionate.

quote: High-risk AI systems shall be designed and developed in such a way that they achieve an appropriate level of accuracy, robustness, and cybersecurity, and that they perform consistently in those respects throughout their lifecycle.
if_not_met: Not stated here. Breach of Art. 16(a): fines up to EUR 15 000 000 or 3% (Art. 99(4)(a), outside this part).
note: Metric: 'appropriate level', not quantified; levels and metrics declared in instructions (15(3)). Trigger: throughout lifecycle.

quote: shall be developed in such a way as to eliminate or reduce as far as possible the risk of possibly biased outputs influencing input for future operations (feedback loops)
if_not_met: Not stated here. Breach of Art. 16(a): fines up to EUR 15 000 000 or 3% (Art. 99(4)(a), outside this part).
note: For systems that continue to learn after placing on market. Also: be as resilient as possible to errors, faults, inconsistencies; may use technical redundancy, backup or fail-safe plans.

quote: High-risk AI systems shall be resilient against attempts by unauthorised third parties to alter their use, outputs or performance by exploiting system vulnerabilities.
if_not_met: Not stated here. Breach of Art. 16(a): fines up to EUR 15 000 000 or 3% (Art. 99(4)(a), outside this part).
note: 'where appropriate', measures against data poisoning, model poisoning, adversarial examples or model evasion, confidentiality attacks, model flaws.

quote: ensure that the high-risk AI system complies with accessibility requirements in accordance with Directives (EU) 2016/2102 and (EU) 2019/882.

note: Trigger: before, during and after development; frequency set by the provider in its QMS. Compares against: not stated here (see Art. 9(8)).

quote: the logs shall be kept for a period appropriate to the intended purpose of the high-risk AI system, of at least six months
if_not_met: Not stated here. Art. 16(e) breach: fines up to EUR 15 000 000 or 3% (Art. 99(4)(a), outside this part).

note: Trigger: system presents a risk within Art. 79(1) and provider becomes aware. Also coded Accountability/Design.

quote: verify that the EU declaration of conformity referred to in Article 47 and the technical documentation referred to in Article 11 have been drawn up
if_not_met: Not stated here. Art. 99(4)(b) (outside this part): fines up to EUR 15 000 000 or 3%.
note: Also verify that an appropriate conformity assessment was carried out by the provider. Trigger: not stated.

quote: Before placing a high-risk AI system on the market, importers shall ensure that the system is in conformity with this Regulation by verifying that:
if_not_met: Not stated here. Art. 99(4)(c) (outside this part): fines up to EUR 15 000 000 or 3%.
note: Trigger: before placing on market. Compares against: conformity assessment done (Art. 43), technical documentation (Art. 11, Annex IV), CE marking, EU declaration and instructions, authorised representative appointed.

quote: distributors shall verify that it bears the required CE marking, that it is accompanied by a copy of the EU declaration of conformity referred to in Article 47 and instructions for use
