note: Trigger: before making available. Also check provider and importer complied with Art. 16(b), (c) and 23(3). 24(3): storage/transport conditions.

quote: Deployers of high-risk AI systems shall take appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure they use such systems in accordance with the instructions for use accompanying the systems
if_not_met: Not stated here. Art. 99(4)(e) (outside this part): fines up to EUR 15 000 000 or 3% of worldwide turnover for breach of Art. 26; national public authorities only as each Member State lays down (Art. 99(8)); Union bodies up to EUR 750 000 (Art. 100(3)).
note: Use per provider's instructions (Art. 13). Compares against: instructions for use.

quote: that deployer shall ensure that input data is relevant and sufficiently representative in view of the intended purpose of the high-risk AI system
obligation: statutory duty (where deployer controls input data)
if_not_met: Not stated here. Art. 99(4)(e) (outside this part).
note: Only 'to the extent the deployer exercises control over the input data'. Compares against the intended purpose; metric not stated.

quote: Deployers shall monitor the operation of the high-risk AI system on the basis of the instructions for use and, where relevant, inform providers in accordance with Article 72.
if_not_met: Not stated here. Art. 99(4)(e) (outside this part).
note: Check: ongoing monitoring during use; compares against instructions for use; metric not stated. Financial institutions deemed compliant via sectoral governance rules. Also coded Decision-making/Design and Accountability/Design.

quote: shall keep the logs automatically generated by that high-risk AI system to the extent such logs are under their control, for a period appropriate to the intended purpose of the high-risk AI system, of at least six months
if_not_met: Not stated here. Art. 99(4)(e) (outside this part).
note: Unless other Union or national law (esp. data protection) provides otherwise. Financial institutions keep logs in sectoral documentation.

quote: deployers of high-risk AI systems shall use the information provided under Article 13 of this Regulation to comply with their obligation to carry out a data protection impact assessment
if_not_met: Not stated here. Art. 99(4)(e) (outside this part).
note: Points to the DPIA under Art. 35 GDPR or Art. 27 Directive (EU) 2016/680; provider's Art. 13 information is the resource.

quote: each use of such high-risk AI systems shall be documented in the relevant police file and shall be made available to the relevant market surveillance authority and the national data protection authority upon request
holder: not stated (passive); nearest: the deployer of a post-remote biometric identification system
if_not_met: not stated in Art. 26; Art. 99(4)(e) (outside this part)
note: Recording each use, 'Regardless of the purpose or deployer'. Also coded Accountability/Design (available to MSA and DPA). Excludes disclosure of sensitive operational data related to law enforcement.

quote: deployers that are bodies governed by public law, or are private entities providing public services, and deployers of high-risk AI systems referred to in points 5 (b) and (c) of Annex III, shall perform an assessment
holder: deployers that are bodies governed by public law, or are private entities providing public services, and deployers of high-risk AI systems referred to in points 5 (b) and (c) of Annex III
if_not_met: Not stated here; Art. 27 is not among the provisions listed in Art. 99(4) (outside this part); Member States lay down penalty rules for infringements generally (Art. 99(1)); Union bodies up to EUR 750 000 (Art. 100(3)).
note: Fundamental rights impact assessment. Trigger: 'Prior to deploying'; applies to first use (27(2)); excludes Annex III point 2. Must describe (a) processes, (b) period and frequency, (c) affected categories, (d) specific risks of harm (using Art. 13 information), (e) human oversight per instructions, (f) measures if risks materialise. Compares against: no threshold or metric stated. Complements DPIA (27(4)). Also coded Accountability/Design.

quote: the entity using the AI system for other than military, defence or national security purposes should ensure the compliance of the AI system with this Regulation, unless the system is already compliant
holder: the entity using the AI system for other than military, defence or national security purposes
note: Verb 'should ensure'. The recital gives no power to approve or stop, so coded Delivery [inference]. Trigger: use of an excluded-purpose system for another purpose (e.g. law enforcement or public security). Also: providers of dual-purpose systems 'should ensure compliance'. Cross-ref Decision-making/Design (Recital 24).

quote: the deployer considers that any of the elements listed in paragraph 1 has changed or is no longer up to date, the deployer shall take the necessary steps to update the information
if_not_met: Not stated here; Art. 27 is not listed in Art. 99(4) (outside this part).
note: Trigger: on change during use, as judged by the deployer.

quote: Notified bodies shall be independent of the provider of a high-risk AI system in relation to which they perform conformity assessment activities.
if_not_met: Not stated here. Art. 99(4)(f) (outside this part): fines up to EUR 15 000 000 or 3% for breach of Art. 31, 33(1), (3), (4) or 34; designation may be restricted, suspended or withdrawn (Art. 36(4)).
note: Also independent of other operators with an economic interest and of competitors (31(4)); not involved in design, development, marketing or use, no consultancy (31(5)); impartiality procedures (31(6)); confidentiality (31(7)); proportionate procedures (31(8)). 31(1): established under national law with legal personality. Art. 32: presumption of conformity via harmonised standards.

quote: Notified bodies shall verify the conformity of high-risk AI systems in accordance with the conformity assessment procedures set out in Article 43.
if_not_met: Not stated here. Art. 99(4)(f) (outside this part).
note: The third-party check. 34(2): avoid unnecessary burdens, account for size, sector and complexity, minimise burdens for micro and small enterprises, while respecting rigour and protection.

quote: the market surveillance authority referred to in Article 74(8) or (9), as applicable, shall act as a notified body
holder: the market surveillance authority referred to in Article 74(8) or (9)
note: Applies 'where the high-risk AI system is intended to be put into service by law enforcement, immigration or asylum authorities or by Union institutions, bodies, offices or agencies' (Annex III point 1 biometrics). A public checker replaces the notified body for these public-sector deployments.

quote: In demonstrating the compliance of a high-risk AI system with the requirements set out in Section 2, the provider shall follow the conformity assessment procedure set out in Annex VII where:
obligation: mandatory approval gate (conformity assessment before placing on market, Art. 16(f))
if_not_met: Not stated here. Art. 16(f) breach: fines up to EUR 15 000 000 or 3% (Art. 99(4)(a), outside this part); national public authorities as each Member State lays down (Art. 99(8)).
note: Applies to Annex III point 1 (biometrics). If harmonised standards or common specifications were applied, the provider may opt for internal control (Annex VI) or notified-body assessment (Annex VII); Annex VII required where standards/specifications are absent, not applied, partly applied or restricted. Also coded Decision-making/Design and Delivery/Design (MSA as notified body).

quote: the provider shall opt for one of the following conformity assessment procedures
holder: the provider (of high-risk AI systems listed in point 1 of Annex III)
obligation: statutory duty (choice of procedure where standards applied; notified body mandatory otherwise)
if_not_met: not stated here; Art. 99(4)(a) (outside this part) via Art. 16(f)
note: For Annex III point 1 (biometrics): where harmonised standards or common specifications applied, provider chooses (a) internal control (Annex VI) or (b) QMS and technical documentation assessment 'with the involvement of a notified body' (Annex VII). Annex VII is mandatory where standards do not exist, were not applied or only partly applied, or were published with a restriction. Trigger: before placing on the market (Art. 16(f)). Also coded Delivery/Design for the public-authority case.

quote: providers shall follow the conformity assessment procedure based on internal control as referred to in Annex VI, which does not provide for the involvement of a notified body
if_not_met: Not stated here. Art. 16(f) breach: Art. 99(4)(a) (outside this part); national public authorities as each Member State lays down (Art. 99(8)).
note: For Annex III points 2 to 8. Self-assessment, no third-party check. [inference] Covers most public-sector Annex III uses (essential public services and benefits, law enforcement, migration, justice). Trigger: before placing on market/putting into service (Art. 16(f)); compares against Section 2; metric not stated.

quote: shall undergo a new conformity assessment procedure in the event of a substantial modification, regardless of whether the modified system is intended to be further distributed or continues to be used by the current deployer
if_not_met: Not stated here. Art. 16(f) breach: Art. 99(4)(a) (outside this part).
note: Trigger: substantial modification (Art. 3(23)), even if the system stays with the current deployer. Pre-determined changes for continuously learning systems, documented in Annex IV point 2(f), are not substantial modifications.

quote: High-risk AI systems that have already been subject to a conformity assessment procedure shall undergo a new conformity assessment procedure in the event of a substantial modification
holder: not stated (passive); nearest: providers; a deployer making a substantial modification becomes provider (Art. 25(1)(b))
if_not_met: not stated here; Art. 99(4)(a) (outside this part) via Art. 16(f)
note: Re-check trigger: substantial modification (Art. 3(23)), 'regardless of whether the modified system is intended to be further distributed or continues to be used by the current deployer'. For continuously learning systems, changes 'pre-determined by the provider at the moment of the initial conformity assessment' and documented in Annex IV point 2(f) are not substantial modifications.

quote: Certificates shall be valid for the period they indicate, which shall not exceed five years for AI systems covered by Annex I, and four years for AI systems covered by Annex III.
note: Re-check trigger: expiry; extension at provider's request 'based on a re-assessment in accordance with the applicable conformity assessment procedures'. 44(1): certificates in a language understood by relevant authorities.
basis: AI pass A; different cell in pass B

quote: draw up and keep up-to-date the technical documentation of the model, including its training and testing process and the results of its evaluation
if_not_met: Not stated here. Recital 169: GPAI provider obligations enforceable by fines (Art. 101, outside this part; amounts not checked).
note: Recording of model testing and evaluation; minimum content Annex XI; 'for the purpose of providing it, upon request, to the AI Office and the national competent authorities' (Accountability element). Not for qualifying open-source models without systemic risk (53(2)). Information treated under Art. 78 confidentiality (53(7)).
basis: AI pass B; different cell in pass A

quote: put in place a policy to comply with Union law on copyright and related rights
if_not_met: Not stated here. Fines under Art. 101 (outside this part; see Recital 169).
note: Incl. identifying and complying with rights reservations under Art. 4(3) Directive (EU) 2019/790 using state-of-the-art technologies.

quote: verify that the technical documentation specified in Annex XI has been drawn up and all obligations referred to in Article 53 and, where applicable, Article 55 have been fulfilled by the provider
note: Check on the model provider; trigger not stated.

quote: perform model evaluation in accordance with standardised protocols and tools reflecting the state of the art, including conducting and documenting adversarial testing of the model with a view to identifying and mitigating systemic risks
holder: providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk
if_not_met: Not stated here. Fines under Art. 101 (outside this part; see Recital 169).
note: Check: model evaluation incl. adversarial testing; trigger not stated; compares against 'standardised protocols and tools reflecting the state of the art'; metric not stated. In addition to Arts 53-54.

quote: assess and mitigate possible systemic risks at Union level, including their sources, that may stem from the development, the placing on the market, or the use of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk
holder: providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk
if_not_met: Not stated here. Fines under Art. 101 (outside this part; see Recital 169).
note: Includes risks from use (e.g. downstream use by public bodies [inference]).

quote: ensure an adequate level of cybersecurity protection for the general-purpose AI model with systemic risk and the physical infrastructure of the model.
holder: providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk
if_not_met: Not stated here. Fines under Art. 101 (outside this part; see Recital 169).
note: 'Adequate' not quantified.

quote: Any significant risks to health and safety and fundamental rights identified during the development and testing of such AI systems shall result in an adequate mitigation.
if_not_met: suspension of testing or of sandbox participation where no effective mitigation is possible (Art. 57(11))
note: Passive. Nearest named actors: providers or prospective providers in the sandbox and the supervising national competent authority. Trigger: risk identified during development and testing; compared against: not stated; metric: not stated. Also coded Decision-making/Design.

quote: there are effective monitoring mechanisms to identify if any high risks to the rights and freedoms of the data subjects
if_not_met: [inference] the further processing is not permitted
note: Monitoring check. Trigger: ongoing during sandbox experimentation. Compared against: high risks as referred to in Art. 35 GDPR and Art. 39 Regulation (EU) 2018/1725. Metric: not stated. Also requires 'response mechanisms to promptly mitigate those risks and, where necessary, stop the processing'. Nearest named actor: the prospective provider.

quote: any personal data to be processed in the context of the sandbox are in a functionally separate, isolated and protected data processing environment under the control of the prospective provider and only authorised persons have access to those data
if_not_met: [inference] the further processing is not permitted
note: Data environment control. Related conditions: (e) sharing only per Union data protection law, sandbox-created data not shared outside; (g) technical and organisational protection and deletion at end of participation or retention period.

quote: the logs of the processing of personal data in the context of the sandbox are kept for the duration of the participation in the sandbox
if_not_met: [inference] the further processing is not permitted
note: Logging; 'unless provided otherwise by Union or national law'. Nearest named actor: the prospective provider.

quote: a complete and detailed description of the process and rationale behind the training, testing and validation of the AI system is kept together with the testing results as part of the technical documentation referred to in Annex IV
if_not_met: [inference] the further processing is not permitted
note: Recording of training, testing and validation with results. Nearest named actor: the prospective provider.

quote: Providers or prospective providers may conduct testing of high-risk AI systems referred to in Annex III in real world conditions at any time before the placing on the market or the putting into service of the AI system
holder: Providers or prospective providers of high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III
obligation: statutory permission, subject to the conditions in Art. 60(4)
note: Testing. Trigger: before placing on the market or putting into service. Compared against: the real-world testing plan. Metric: not stated. May be done 'on their own or in partnership with one or more deployers or prospective deployers'; without prejudice to Art. 5 prohibitions and to any ethical review required by law (Art. 60(3)).

quote: the subjects of the testing in real world conditions who are persons belonging to vulnerable groups due to their age or disability, are appropriately protected
note: Passive. Nearest named actor: provider or prospective provider. Market surveillance authorities may derogate within sandboxes (Art. 76(2)).

quote: the testing in real world conditions is effectively overseen by the provider or prospective provider, as well as by deployers or prospective deployers
holder: Provider or prospective provider; deployers or prospective deployers
note: Human oversight during testing. Trigger: throughout testing. Also coded Delivery/Resources (qualified persons).

quote: The provider or prospective provider shall establish a procedure for the prompt recall of the AI system upon such termination of the testing in real world conditions.
note: Recall procedure. Trigger: termination of testing.

quote: The informed consent shall be dated and documented and a copy shall be given to the subjects of testing or their legal representative.
note: Recording. Nearest named actor: provider or prospective provider.

quote: The impact assessment should be performed prior to deploying the high-risk AI system, and should be updated when the deployer considers that any of the relevant factors have changed.
obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital); 'should be performed', 'should be updated'
note: Triggers: before deployment; on change (deployer's judgement). Content: deployer's processes, period and frequency of use, categories of persons affected, specific risks of harm to fundamental rights. Compares against fundamental rights; metric not stated.

quote: Providers of high-risk AI systems shall put a quality management system in place that ensures compliance with this Regulation.
if_not_met: Not stated here. Art. 16(c) breach: fines up to EUR 15 000 000 or 3% (Art. 99(4)(a), outside this part).
note: Written policies, procedures, instructions covering at least (a)-(m): compliance strategy and modification management; design control; QA; testing; standards; data management; risk management (Art. 9); post-market monitoring (Art. 72); serious incident reporting (Art. 73); communication; record-keeping; resource management; accountability framework. Financial institutions largely deemed compliant via sectoral rules (17(4)).

quote: adequate safeguards with respect to the protection of  the fundamental rights and freedoms of individuals, to be assessed by the market surveillance authorities competent
holder: Market surveillance authorities competent for the supervision of AI systems used in the area of law enforcement and justice
obligation: non-binding interpretation of a statutory condition
if_not_met: not stated [inference: the exclusion would not apply]
note: A check. Trigger: reliance on the Art. 2(4) exclusion. Compares cooperation frameworks or international agreements against 'adequate safeguards' for fundamental rights and freedoms; metric not stated. The outcome decides whether the exclusion applies, so it also bears on Decision-making.

quote: any research and development activity (including when excluded from the scope of the AI Act)  should be carried out in accordance with recognised ethical and professional standards for scientific research
note: Verb: should. Nearest actor: whoever conducts the research and development. Standards not named. Also 'should be conducted in accordance with applicable Union law' (e.g. data protection law).

quote: whether they implemented appropriate preventive and mitigating measures to avoid  or mitigate the risk of such significant harm s
if_not_met: not stated [inference: harm may be found reasonably likely and the prohibition apply]
note: Part of the reasonable-likelihood test, with 'whether the provider or deployer of the AI system could have reasonably foreseen the significant harm'. Judgement 'on an objective basis and according to universally accepted criteria ( e.g., technical and scientific)'. Para (96) example: the provider 'may assess and try to mitigate potential harmful manipulative effects ... through the design, prior testing, and other proportionate mitigating measures'. Trigger: before and during use; metric not stated.

quote: ensuring that only data related to the social context in which the score is used  are processed for the purpose of the evaluation or classification, the system is performing as intended
holder: The provider and the deployer of the AI system
note: Checks: data relevance to the context of use; that the system is 'performing as intended'; and that resulting treatment is 'justified and proportionate to the social behaviour'. Trigger: to be demonstrated on MSA checks; safeguards 'built in the system and applied during its operation' (ongoing). Metric not stated. Bears on checking AI outputs.

quote: the seriousness, probability and scale of the harm for natural persons, society and law enforcement purposes that would be caused if the system were not used, should be assessed against the consequences of the use of the system
holder: the law enforcement authority deploying the system (passive in para 359; para 363 places the assessment in the FRIA 'that the law enforcement authority is obliged to complete')
obligation: statutory duty ('shall take into account'); guideline wording 'should'
note: Pre-use balancing check. Trigger: 'before using the system'. Compares harm if the system is not used against consequences for rights and freedoms. Metrics, qualitative: seriousness linked to proportionality (para 360); scale = 'the number and categories of persons affected' (para 361); probability = likelihood (para 362). Should include 'evaluating whether less intrusive alternative solutions are available'. 'That assessment will be concluded on a case-by-case basis' (para 363).

quote: the FRIA should complement the DPIA performed by the deployer as data controller
obligation: statutory duties (DPIA, FRIA); the division of labour ('should complement') is non-binding interpretation
note: Relation between two impact assessments. 'The FRIA does not replace the existing Data Protection Impact Assessment' (para 371); the FRIA should avoid 'covering aspects already addressed in the DPIA'. Example: 'a DPIA must be conducted when biometric data are processed through new technologies' such as 'CCTV, AI facial recognition, and body -worn cameras' in publicly accessible spaces. Also coded: FRIA entry (Delivery/Design, para 368).

quote: A description of the RBI use and the deployer’s processes for the use, together with the intended purpose of use
obligation: statutory duty; the listed content is provisional, non-binding guidance ('should include')
note: FRIA content, first items. The description should include the name of the deployer, the law enforcement purpose(s), 'the description of the reference database' and sources of biometric data, the technology (provider documentation entry) and 'the legal basis'. Period and frequency: 'deployers must provide a general indication of the intended period of use and the expected frequency'. Categories of persons: the targeted individual, persons in the reference database, and persons present in the surrounding areas. Further content coded separately (risks, accuracy, human oversight, redress).

quote: a double necessity and proportionality assessment should occur prior to the deployment of any real -time RBI system  in publicly accessible spaces for law enforcement purposes
location: p. 119 [printed 114], s. 10.2.1, para (380); also para (399), p. 123 [printed 118]
holder: the user/deployer (first assessment, in the FRIA) and the judicial or independent administrative authority (second assessment)
obligation: statutory duty; non-binding interpretation of the two-step structure
if_not_met: authorisation refused, so use is not permitted (see prior-authorisation entry)
note: Check before each deployment: first by the user in the FRIA; 'Second, in accordance with Article 5(3) AI Act, a judicial or independent administrative authority must also assess the necessity and proportionality'. Compared against: the objectives in Art. 5(1)(h)(i)-(iii) and limits on time, geography and persons (para 379). Metric: necessity and proportionality; 'National authorities need to verify whether the biometric identification is strictly necessary', based on the FRIA (para 399). The authority's grant is coded Decision-making/Design (para 382).

quote: Automatically generated data logs must be kept for at least 6 months for high -risk AI systems
note: Recording. Logs 'shall include for the high -risk systems mentioned in point 1(a) of Annex III for each use the start and end data and time'. Trigger: each use; retention at least 6 months. A footnote report of other AI Act provisions; coded because it supports the authorisation check (Accountability entry, para 400).

quote: the reference database(s) used for the unauthorized biometric identification must be removed and deleted if it was built specifically for the contested search.
holder: not stated (passive); nearest: the deployer (law enforcement authority)
obligation: statutory duty; non-binding interpretation of its reach
note: Deletion after a rejected urgent use: 'all the data, including the results and outputs of that use, must be immediately discarded and deleted' (para 402), including images, metadata, templates, comparison and output data (para 404). A database may be kept only if built 'in a lawful manner for legitimate aims other than for the unauthorized use' (para 403). Fn 231: supervisory authorities should be able to check this (Accountability entry).

quote: no action or decision may be taken by the deployer on the basis of the identification resulting from the system, ‘unless that identification has been separately verified and confirmed by at least two natural persons
holder: the deployer (verification by at least two natural persons)
obligation: statutory duty, unless Union or national law considers it disproportionate
note: Human review of outputs: two competent persons separately verify and confirm each identification before any action. Trigger: each identification. Exception where 'Union or national law  considers the application of this requirement to be disproportionate'. Permitted real-time RBI 'still falls under the rules for high-risk systems'. Also coded Delivery/Resources (AI literacy; organisation against automation bias).

quote: While providers of AI systems must consider the conditions of use which may be reasonably foreseen prior to placing their AI systems on the market (intended use and reasonably foreseeable misuse 8)
obligation: statutory duty as stated in non-binding guidelines ('must consider')
note: Check: trigger = before placing on the market; compares against = intended use and reasonably foreseeable misuse; metric = not stated. Cross-ref Delivery/Design entry for deployers (same sentence).

quote: deployers remain responsible for taking the lawful conditions for the use of the system into account.
obligation: statutory duty as stated in non-binding guidelines ('remain responsible')
note: Trigger: during use [inference]; what the lawful conditions are is not specified here. Cross-ref Delivery/Design entry for providers (same sentence) and Accountability/Design entry (para 14, deployer liable regardless of provider's terms of use).

quote: Providers must ensure their AI systems meet all relevant requirements before placing them on the market or putting them into service.
holder: Providers (natural or legal persons, public authorities, agencies or other bodies, para 16)
note: 'Ensure' coded as Delivery because the provider must make the system compliant itself. Check: trigger = before placing on the market or putting into service; compares against = 'all relevant requirements' of the AI Act; metric = not stated. Providers outside the Union are covered if they place systems on the Union market or the output is used in the Union (para 16).
basis: AI pass A; different cell in pass B

quote: Continuous compliance with the AI Act is required during all phases of the AI lifecycle. This necessitates ongoing monitoring of and updates to AI systems placed on the market or put into service in the Union
holder: Providers and deployers of AI systems
obligation: required (as stated in non-binding guidelines: 'is required', 'necessitates')
note: Check: trigger = ongoing, throughout the lifecycle; compares against = the AI Act, in particular that the system 'does not result in a practice prohibited under Article 5'; metric = not stated. Holder taken from the next sentence ('Providers and deployers of AI systems have different responsibilities depending on their roles and control'). Allocation: roles 'should be interpreted in a proportionate manner, taking into account who in the value chain is best placed to adopt specific preventive and mitigating measures'.

quote: should be assessed against the consequences of the use of the system on the rights and freedoms of the persons concerned
obligation: statutory duty (Act: 'shall take into account'); Guidelines: 'should'
note: Balancing check. Trigger: before using the system. Compares the seriousness, probability and scale of harm if the system is not used against the seriousness, probability and scale of consequences for rights (para 360-362), and includes 'evaluating whether less intrusive alternative solutions are available'. Metric: qualitative. Para 363: should be part of the FRIA, case by case. Example: street facial recognition on general security grounds is prohibited.

quote: before deployment, the law enforcement authority deploying the real-time RBI system must have conducted a Fundamental Right Impact Assessment (FRIA) and registered the system in the EU database (except in a duly justified case).
holder: the law enforcement authority deploying the real-time RBI system
if_not_met: use may not be authorised: Art. 5(2) as quoted, 'shall be authorised only if the law enforcement authority has completed a  fundamental rights impact assessment'
note: Impact assessment before deployment (para 374). Para 373: the duty rests on the deployer, not on bodies acting on its behalf. Para 371: 'A FRIA is an accountability tool'; to whom it is answered is not stated. Para 372: complements the DPIA without overlap. Registration is coded separately as Accountability/Design (para 377).

quote: the requirements for FRIA set out in Article 27 AI Act should be implemented by the deployers  of real-time RBI systems meeting the conditions to benefit from one or more of the exceptions in Article 5(1) (h) AI Act
holder: deployers of real-time RBI systems meeting the conditions of an Art. 5(1)(h) exception
note: Interim period: between 2 February 2025 and 2 August 2026, and until the Commission adopts the FRIA template. The Guidelines bring the Art. 27 content forward for RBI only. Para 369: FRIAs under Art. 5(2) must comply with Art. 27.

quote: the FRIA must identify the fundamental rights of those persons and assess the impact on their fundamental rights, including the  severity of the impact  and its scale, taking into account the potentially affected persons.
obligation: mandatory ('must'); content guidance is non-binding interpretation
note: FRIA content (para 375): description of use (deployer name, law enforcement purposes, reference database and data sources, technology, legal basis); general period and frequency of use; categories of persons (target, persons in the reference database, persons in the area); specific risks. Para 376 lists rights at stake. Trigger: 'at an abstract level, prior to the first putting into service'; case-specific points go into each authorisation request. Should also assess necessity and proportionality, including less intrusive alternatives.

quote: The FRIA should describe the performance and accuracy level of the system, based on the technical documentation and, if available, the training data on which the technology was tested and developed to prevent biases and discrimination.
note: Check of system performance. Trigger: before first putting into service. Compared against: technical documentation and, if available, training and testing data. Metric: 'performance and accuracy level' named; no threshold given. Provider documentation coded as Delivery/Resources.

quote: The procedures should provide instruc tions on the deployment of the RBI system, clarify the role of a human agent in verifying and interpreting the output and provide training to operate the system.
location: page 117 (printed p. 112), section 10.1.1, para 375 (human oversight measures)
note: Human review of outputs. The FRIA 'should describe the procedures that will be followed during the operation of the system and how the output will be interpreted in the context of decision-making process'. Trigger: during operation, each output [inference]. 'Other considerations for human oversight and monitoring under Articles 14 and 26 AI Act are also relevant and should be described' (p. 118 [printed 113]). Also coded Delivery/Resources (literacy, training, authority).
basis: AI pass B; different cell in pass A

quote: the FRIA should describe the procedures that will be followed during the operation of the system and how the output will be interpreted in the context of decision-making process.
location: page 117 (printed p. 112), section 10.1.1, para 375 (human oversight measures)
note: Follows from Art. 5(3): 'no decision that would adversely affect an individual may be taken solely on the basis of the output'. Page 118: other human oversight and monitoring considerations under Arts. 14 and 26 'should be described'. Resources for oversight coded separately (two Delivery/Resources entries).

quote: a judicial or independent administrative authority must also assess the necessity and proportionality of using such a system within the limits of the national law providing the legal basis for any such use
holder: a judicial or independent administrative authority
note: Second of a 'double necessity and proportionality assessment'; the first is by the user in the FRIA. Trigger: each request, before use. Compared against: the Art. 5(1)(h) objectives, strict necessity for period, geography and persons, the Charter and Union law. Metric: not stated. Para 399: 'National authorities need to verify whether the biometric identification is strictly necessary', based on the FRIA. Also coded: Decision-making/Design (para 382).

quote: the entity using the AI system for the other purposes should ensure compliance of the AI system with the AI Act, unless the system already complies with that act, which has to be verified before such use.
holder: Entity using a military, defence or national-security AI system for other purposes (e.g. civilian, humanitarian, law enforcement or public security)
obligation: should (non-binding interpretation); verification 'has to' be done
note: Check: trigger = before use for a non-excluded purpose (repurposing); compares against = AI Act requirements; metric = not stated. Stated inside a 'For example' passage but sets out what is to be done.

quote: The logging of the processing activities should be made available to the authority to substantiate the timeliness of the request.
note: Logging used as evidence for the authorising authority (also an Accountability link). Fn 230: automatically generated logs must be kept for at least 6 months for high-risk systems and include start and end date and time of each use for Annex III point 1(a) systems.
basis: AI pass A; different cell in pass B

quote: all the data, including the results and outputs of that use, must be immediately discarded and deleted.
note: Trigger: rejection of an urgency request. Para 403: a reference database built specifically for the contested search must also be deleted, unless lawfully built and kept for other legitimate aims. Para 404: images, metadata, templates, comparison and output data must be deleted.

quote: unless that identification has been separately verified and confirmed by at least two natural persons with the necessary competence, training and a uthority
obligation: statutory duty (unless Union or national law considers it disproportionate)
if_not_met: no action or decision may be taken on the identification [Art. 14(5) as quoted]
note: Two-person verification of each identification before action. Trigger: each match. Compared against: not stated. Permitted real-time RBI still falls under the high-risk rules, including design for effective human oversight (Art. 14). Resources coded separately (para 407-408).

quote: the minimum reliability, threshold used, and accuracy rates of the systems used;
obligation: suggested content for national law ('may regulate for example'); non-binding
note: Named performance metrics (reliability, threshold, accuracy rates); no values set. Trigger: authorisation request [inference: listed under rules for the request]. Who measures is not stated.

quote: Providers of those systems should ensure that they comply with the requirements in the AI Act.
holder: Providers of 'dual use' AI systems (placed on the market for excluded and non-excluded purposes)
note: Example: a company offering an RBI system for purposes including law enforcement and national security is the provider of a dual-use system and 'must ensure its compliance with the requirements in the AI Act'. Trigger, comparator and metric: not stated beyond 'requirements in the AI Act'.

quote: Those operators should therefore take necessary measures to ensure that they do not place on the market, put into service or use AI systems that could constitute prohibited practices under Article 5 AI Act.
holder: providers and deployers of AI systems ('Those operators')
obligation: statutory duty ('fully applicable and mandatory'); 'should' for the measures
if_not_met: enforcement by affected parties in national courts, including interim injunctions (para 431); fines only from 2 August 2025 (para 430)
note: The measures are not specified; no check, trigger or metric is given beyond application from 2 February 2025 to all systems 'regardless of whether they were placed on the market or put into service before or after that date' (para 429). On 'ensure': operators can stop their own placing or use (decision) and must take the measures themselves (delivery); coded as Delivery because the verb is 'take necessary measures' [coder judgement].
basis: AI pass B; different cell in pass A

quote: the planned testing  must be  fully compliant with  the requirements for RBI systems in  the AI Act , unless the system is tested in an AI regulatory sandbox
holder: Municipality testing an RBI system in real-world conditions (example)
note: Example of a municipality testing facial recognition with volunteers during a carnival. Check: trigger = before and during real-world testing; compares against = AI Act requirements for RBI systems; metric = not stated. quote: t he risk assessment and management done by the provider and the compliance with the other requirements for high-risk AI systems (e.g., data governance, transparency and human oversight)

note: The sentence ends: 'should help to ensure that the high-risk AI system placed on the market or deployed is lawful and does not constitute a prohibited practice.' Check: trigger = not stated; compares against = high-risk requirements and Art. 5; metric = not stated. Cross-ref Delivery/Design entry for deployers (same sentence).

note: Human oversight and fundamental rights impact assessment as means to avoid a prohibited practice. Which deployers must do a FRIA is not stated here ('in some cases'). quote: each operator should take measures for which they are best placed based on their role and control over the system in the value chain to ensure a responsible and safe provision and use of AI systems

note: Check: trigger = ongoing after supply; compares against = the provider's restriction on prohibited use; metric = not stated. note: Applies where manipulative behaviour is 'merely incidental' (e.g. learned from training data or RLHF). Check: trigger = where significant harms are reasonably likely; compares against = reasonably foreseeable significant harm; metric = not stated. obligation: should (non-binding interpretation of statutory transparency obligations)
note: Design-stage measure; trigger: before the system is provided [inference]; metric: not stated. Detection here means provider-side marking that enables detection of AI-generated content, not a public body checking incoming content. Cross-ref Accountability/Design entry (para 71).
basis: AI pass A; different cell in pass B

note: A generative system that 'incidentally presents false or misleading information and hallucinates' may not be deceptive. Bears on checking AI outputs. Trigger and metric: not stated.

note: Check carried out by the enforcer: trigger = each case under investigation; compares against = an 'average' individual within a targeted group, or specific individuals where the average perspective 'proves difficult or ineffective to assess' (e.g. personalised manipulation, vulnerable groups); metric = not stated (fn 71: the average consumer test 'is not a statistical test'). quote: the following key considerations can be derived and could be taken into account when assessing what constitutes significant harm within the meaning of Article 5(1)(a) AI Act
note: Passive: assessor not named (nearest: market surveillance authorities; providers and deployers). quote: A precautionary approach is therefore particularly warranted in case of uncertainty and potential for significant harms.
note: Passive: assessor not named (nearest: market surveillance authorities; providers and deployers). Check: trigger = uncertainty and potential for significant harm to vulnerable groups; compares against = what is acceptable for adults ('What may be considered an acceptable risk of harm for adults often represents an unacceptable harm for children and these other vulnerable groups'); metric = not stated. Para 120: harms that 'can be externalised and affect other persons' should also be taken into account.

quote: The manufacturer of those products embedding AI systems should therefore take into account these prohibitions in their risk assessments and safety mitigating measures

quote: This requires a case-by-case assessment, which should consider all relevant circumstances of the case, as well as general ethical considerations and principles for fairness and social justice
obligation: requires (as stated in non-binding guidelines); 'should consider'
note: Passive: assessor not named (nearest: market surveillance authorities; providers and deployers). Check: trigger = each case; compares against = 'The severity of the impact and the interference with the fundamental rights ... compared to the gravity of the social behaviour', the general principle of proportionality, and any 'Sectoral Union or national legislation setting specific criteria and procedures'; metric = not stated.

note: Passive: nearest holders are providers (safeguards built in) and deployers (applied during operation) [inference]. Trigger: design stage and ongoing operation; metric not stated. Stated aim: enabling AI evaluation 'for legitimate and beneficial purposes (e.g., to improve the effectiveness of processes, quality of service, safety, etc.)'.

note: Check: trigger = not stated (before use [inference]); compares against = Union and national legislation, 'in particular if there is more specific legislation that strictly regulates the types of data that can be used' and 'more specific rules and procedures to ensure justified and fair treatment'; metric = not stated. quote: The application of Article 5 AI Act will require a case-by-case assessment, which takes due account of the specific situation at issue in an individual case.
note: Passive: who carries out the assessment is not named; nearest named actors are competent authorities (enforcement) and providers and deployers (compliance), para 4. Check: trigger = each individual case; compares against = the cumulative conditions of each Art. 5 prohibition; metric = not stated. The paragraph adds that the examples in the Guidelines 'are merely indicative and are without prejudice to the need for such an assessment in each case'.

quote: In this specific case, their human assessment should ensure that any AI prediction or assessment of the risk of a person committing a crime is based on objective and verifiable facts linked to a criminal activity.
note: Human review of outputs. Trigger: each prediction or assessment, during use [inference]. Compared against: objective and verifiable facts linked to a criminal activity. Metric: not stated. Also coded: Delivery/Resources, Decision-making/Design (same para).

obligation: condition of a statutory exclusion; non-binding interpretation
if_not_met: the exclusion does not apply, so the prohibition may apply (para 206) [inference]
note: Passive; nearest actor is the human assessor in the law enforcement body. The AI system must support a human assessment, not make the risk assessment itself. Para 202: other elements in a risk assessment must be 'real, substantial and meaningful' to take it outside the prohibition, assessed case by case.

quote: The predictions must also be subject to human assessment and verification in compliance with that legislation 141 in order to ensure the accuracy and appropriateness of such assessments.
holder: a banking institution with anti-money-laundering obligations
obligation: statutory duty under sectoral law (restated); non-binding interpretation
if_not_met: compliance keeps the use outside the prohibition; if not met, the prohibition may apply [inference]
note: SCOPE DOUBT: a private bank's legally imposed crime-risk screening, not a public-sector tool; coded because the document places it inside the prohibition's reach as a legal obligation to assess crime risk. Check: human assessment and verification of each prediction; compares against data specified in the AML law that are 'objective and verifiable'; metric not stated. Worked example.

Check: trigger = before placing on the market; compares against = reasonably foreseeable harmful behaviour and misuse; metric = not stated ('verifiable' but no measure given).

quote: To avoid providing or using AI system s that are likely to be prohibited, providers and deployers of AI systems that deploy such manipulative  or deceptive techniques  are encouraged to take appropriate measures

note: Measures listed: (1) transparency and individual autonomy (transparency in how the system operates, clear disclosures about capabilities and limitations, user control and safeguards); (2) compliance with relevant applicable legislation; (3) state of the art practices and industry standards. quote: providers or deployers of AI systems that  are aware that their systems unlawfully discriminate against persons or groups of persons in specific soci al or -economic situation should also be considered to exploit their vulnerabilities
holder: Providers or deployers of AI systems
if_not_met: Provider or deployer is considered to exploit vulnerabilities, bringing the system within Art. 5(1)(b) (fines, para 55) [inference]
note: Implied duty to take corrective measures.
