obligation: non-binding interpretation; non-prescriptive list; verb 'should' (addressed to SAs)
note: Check: internal or external document-based audits of chosen anonymisation measures; may include reports of code reviews and a theoretical analysis of measures to reduce re-identification. First step is to ensure 'the design has been developed as planned  and is subject to effective engineering governance'. Trigger: not stated. Compared against: the planned design. Metric: not stated. External audit could also be read as Accountability.

quote: SAs should take into consideration the scope, frequency, quantity and quality of tests that the controller has conducted on the model.
obligation: non-binding interpretation; non-prescriptive list; verb 'should' (addressed to SAs)
note: Testing of the model by the controller. Successful testing against 'widely known, state-of-the-art attacks can only be evidence for the resistance to those attacks'. Examples: structured testing against attribute and membership inference, exfiltration, regurgitation of training data, model inversion, reconstruction attacks. Trigger: not stated. Compared against: state-of-the-art attacks; metrics: 'metrics on the likelihood of re-identification based on the current state-of-the-art' and test reports '(by whom, when, how and to which extent)' with results (para 58(e)). Para 46: SAs may consider different levels of testing for a publicly available model versus 'an internal AI model only accessible to employees' (relevant to internal public-sector tools [inference]). Bears on checking AI outputs.

quote: Articles 5, 24, 25, and 30 GDPR, and, in cases of likely high risk to the rights and freedoms of data subjects, Article 35 GDPR, require controllers to adequately document their processing  operations.
if_not_met: SA 'would be in a position to consider that the controller has failed to meet its accountability obligations under Article 5(2) GDPR' (para 57)
note: Recording duty restated from the GDPR and applied to AI training 'even if the objective of the processing is anonymisation'. SAs 'should consider such documentation and any regular assessment of the consequential risks' (para 56). DPIA (Art 35) applies where processing is likely to result in high risk; the Opinion does not analyse DPIAs or data protection by design (para 17). Also coded Accountability/Design (para 57).

quote: require controllers to adequately document their processing  operations. This also applies to any processing that would include the training of an AI model
obligation: statutory duty (EDPB interprets it as covering AI model training, including where the aim is anonymisation)
if_not_met: if the SA cannot confirm 'that effective measures were taken to anonymise the AI model, the SA would be in a position to consider that the controller has failed to meet  its accountability obligations under Art icle 5(2) GDPR' (para 57)
note: Recording. Continues 'even if the objective of the processing is  anonymisation'. Para 58 lists what the documentation 'ideally' includes: DPIA information (including decisions that no DPIA was needed); DPO advice; technical and organisational measures with threat model and risk assessments, per-source measures including source URLs; lifecycle measures; documentation of resistance to re-identification (training-data/parameter ratio, re-identification metrics, test reports and results); documentation provided to deployers and data subjects. Also coded Accountability/Design (paras 45, 57).

quote: the development and deployment  of AI models requires that personal data should be adequate, relevant and necessary in relation to the purpose.
note: Passive; nearest actor: controllers. Continues: 'This can include the processing of personal data to avoid the risks of potential biases and errors when this is clearly and specifically identified within the purpose, and the personal data is necessary for that purpose' (bias and error checking). The purpose of development should be informed by the deployment context (para 64). Trigger: development and deployment.

quote: SAs should verify that controlle rs have carefully assessed and documented whether the three following cumulative conditions are met
holder: Controllers (relying on legitimate interest in development or deployment)
obligation: statutory duty where legitimate interest is relied on (as interpreted); verb 'should' addressed to SAs
if_not_met: not stated (see SA corrective powers, para 114)
note: Impact-type assessment in three cumulative steps: legitimate interest (lawful, clearly articulated, real and present, paras 67-69), necessity (paras 70-75), balancing (paras 76-108). Trigger: fn 50 quotes EDPB Guidelines 1/2024: 'assessment should be made at the outset of the processing, with the involvement of the Data Protection Officer (DPO) (if designated), and should be documented by the controller'. Also coded Accountability/Design (same passage). Necessity and balancing steps coded separately.

quote: If the pursuit of the purpose is also possible through an AI model that does not  entail processing  of personal data, then  processing personal data should be considered as not necessary.
if_not_met: not stated (the passage concludes that processing 'should be considered as not necessary')
note: Passive. Nearest named actors: controllers (para 66) and SAs ('SAs should pay particular attention to the amount of personal data processed', para 73). Necessity check compares the intended volume of personal data with less intrusive alternatives, including a model that processes no personal data; 'particularly relevant for the development of AI models'. Two elements (para 72): whether processing allows pursuit of the purpose and whether there is no less intrusive way. Depends on first-party vs third-party data (para 74); technical safeguards short of anonymisation may help meet the test (para 75). Trigger: not stated.
basis: AI pass A; different cell in pass B

quote: SAs may consider whether measures have been implemented to avoid a potential misuse of the AI  model.
note: Passive. Nearest named actors: the controller whose measures are assessed, and SAs. For models deployable for many purposes 'such as generative AI', controls 'limiting as much as possible their use for harmful practices', e.g. creation of deepfakes, chatbots used for disinformation, phishing and fraud, manipulative AI/AI agents. Part of assessing the likelihood of further consequences in the balancing test. Trigger: not stated.

quote: Excluding collection from websites (or sections of websites) which clearly object to web scraping and the reuse of their content  for the purpose of building AI training databases
note: Other examples: excluding content that might include personal data entailing risks for particular persons or groups; excluding certain data categories or sources, e.g. particularly intrusive websites; respecting robots.txt or ai.txt; other limits on collection, e.g. time periods. Holder from para 104 ('controllers conducting web scraping'). Trigger: development phase, at collection. Opt-out list (para 106) noted under Accountability/Design.

quote: Technical measures may for instance be put in place to prevent the storage, regurgitation or generation of personal data, especially in the context of generative AI models (such as output filters)
obligation: optional ('may'); 'should be assessed by SAs on a case-by-case basis'
note: Passive. Nearest named actor: the controller deploying the model. Also measures to mitigate unlawful reuse by general-purpose AI models, 'e.g. digital watermarking of AI-generated outputs' (para 107(a)); measures beyond legal requirements facilitating rights in deployment, e.g. erasure from model output data, deduplication, post-training techniques to remove or suppress personal data (para 107(b)). Trigger: deployment phase. Bears on checking AI outputs.

quote: when the subsequent processing is based on legitimate interest,  the fact that the initial processing was unlawful should be taken into account in the legitimate interest assessment
note: Passive. Nearest named actors: the controller assessing legitimate interest for subsequent (e.g. deployment) processing; SAs verify (para 132). Applies in scenario 1 (same controller) and scenario 2 (another controller), where technical aspects (filters or access limits the subsequent controller cannot circumvent) and legal aspects (nature and severity of the unlawfulness) 'have to be given due consideration within the balancing test' (para 132). Trigger: when subsequent processing relies on legitimate interest.

quote: SAs should take into account whether the controller deploying the model conducted an appropriate assessment
holder: Controller deploying the model (assessment); SAs (take into account)
obligation: non-binding interpretation of a statutory duty; verb 'should' (addressed to SAs)
note: Due-diligence check by a controller that acquires and deploys a model developed by another controller, to ascertain that it was not developed by unlawfully processing personal data, 'as part of its accountability obligations' (Arts 5(2), 24 GDPR). Compares against: the source of the data, whether a SA or court found an infringement, whether data originates from a personal data breach (paras 129-130). Level of detail scales with the risks of the deployment (para 130). Trigger: not stated; [inference] on acquiring or before deploying the model. Relevant where a public body deploys a third-party model [inference]. Unlawfulness of initial processing is weighed in the deployer's balancing test (para 132).
basis: AI pass B; different cell in pass A

quote: The controller should consider, for instance, if the data originates from a personal data breach or if the processing was subject to the finding of an infringement from a SA  or a court
holder: Controller deploying the model (acquired from another controller)
if_not_met: not stated; the SA takes the assessment into account (para 129)
note: Pre-use check by the deployer of a model developed by another controller (scenario 2): ascertain 'that the AI model was not developed by unlawfully processing personal data' (para 129). Compared against: source of the data, personal data breaches, infringement findings by an SA or court. Depth of assessment and SAs' expected detail vary with the risks of the processing in deployment for the data subjects whose data trained the model. Trigger: not stated [inference: before or at deployment]. Directly relevant where a public body acquires a third-party model [inference]. Also coded Accountability/Design (para 129) and Delivery/Resources (documentation from developer, para 58(f)).

quote: SAs should evaluate, on a case -by-case basis,  if the measures implemented by the controller to ensure and prove that an AI model is anonymous are appropriate and effective.
obligation: non-binding interpretation of a statutory duty; verb 'should' (addressed to SAs)
if_not_met: if the SA cannot confirm 'that effective measures were taken to anonymise the AI model, the SA would be in a position to consider that the controller has failed to meet  its accountability obligations under Art icle 5(2) GDPR' (para 57)
note: Check carried out by SAs on controllers' anonymisation measures. Trigger: a claim of anonymity. Compares against: appropriateness and effectiveness; metric not stated. Evaluation areas for model design (paras 49-53): selection of sources; data preparation and minimisation (anonymous or pseudonymised data, filtering); training methods (regularisation and, 'crucially', privacy-preserving techniques e.g. differential privacy); measures on outputs. Level of testing may differ between a publicly available model and an internal model only accessible to employees (para 46). Also coded Decision-making/Design (para 38).
basis: AI pass B; different cell in pass A

quote: reports on how the model has been tested (by whom, when, how and to which extent) and (iv) the results of the tests
obligation: good practice ('Ideally, SAs should verify whether the controller's documentation includes', para 58)
note: Contents of the record SAs should ideally verify: (a) DPIA information, including decisions that a DPIA was not necessary; (b) DPO advice (also coded Delivery/Resources); (c) technical and organisational measures, threat model and risk assessments, per-source measures including source URLs and measures by third-party dataset providers; (d) lifecycle measures; (e) resistance to re-identification, ratio of training data to parameters, re-identification metrics, test reports and results; (f) documentation given to deploying controllers (also coded Coordination/Design).

quote: in assessing the different components in the context of the balancing test, the controller should take into account the interests, fundamental rights and freedoms of the data subjects.
obligation: statutory duty where legitimate interest is relied on; verb 'should'
note: Balancing test elements: data subjects' interests in development and deployment (control over data, financial, personal benefit, socioeconomic e.g. access to healthcare or education, para 77); risks to Charter rights including privacy, data protection, expression, mental health, work (e.g. 'when job applications are pre -selected using an AI model'), non-discrimination, security (paras 79-80); positive impacts (para 81); impact by nature of data, context and further consequences including likelihood (paras 82-90); reasonable expectations (paras 91-95; a privacy-policy mention alone does not make processing expected, para 92). SAs should distinguish risks to training-data subjects and deployment-phase data subjects 'when verifying the balancing test carried out by a controller' (para 89). Trigger: not stated (fn 50: at the outset). No metric. Mitigating measures coded separately.

quote: the controller may consider introducing mitigating measures to limit the impact of the processing on these  data subjects.
note: Trigger: when data subjects' interests 'seem to override' the legitimate interest. Mitigating measures 'should not be confused with the measures that the controller is legally required to adopt anyway' (para 97). Development-phase technical examples: Section 3.2.2 measures short of anonymisation; pseudonymisation; masking or substituting personal data with fake data (paras 100-101). SAs should consider them case by case (para 99). Rights and transparency measures coded Accountability/Design.

quote: That the content is stored only for the duration of the detection and is permanently deleted immediately thereafter (i.e. with a ‘zero retention’ policy)
holder: Signatories who are providers of generative AI systems (detection solutions requiring uploads)
note: Safeguard on content submitted for detection: privacy-sensitive processing, confidentiality, data minimisation, sole-purpose use, zero retention (minimal traffic logs allowed for security), security safeguards, third-country transfer rules (2.1.3(a)-(h)). Relevant where public bodies submit content for checking [inference]. Fingerprinting/logging, where used, limited to output data and not a general commitment to log prompts (1.1.3).

quote: Signatories will ensure that the detection is compliant with EU privacy and data protection law.
holder: Signatories who are providers of generative AI systems
obligation: mandatory under the Code for Signatories ('will'); adherence to the Code is voluntary
if_not_met: not stated (compliance monitored by competent market surveillance authorities; no consequence stated)
note: For detection that requires uploading content: treat content as privacy-sensitive; confidentiality and integrity in transit and at rest; data minimisation; sole purpose of detection; 'zero retention' (content deleted immediately after detection, no verbatim copy kept, minimal traffic logs for security only); security safeguards; third-country transfer rules; cybersecurity best practice. Bears on public bodies uploading content for checking [inference].

quote: Signatories may include as part of their detection solution, as an additional optional measure, forensic detection mechanism to detect content generated or manipulated by their AI system or underlying model for which marking has been stripped.
holder: Signatories who are providers of generative AI systems
note: If used: privacy and security as in Sub-measure 2.1.3, clear disclosure (Measure 2.3), best efforts to match the state of the art. 'At the time of publication of the Code, forensic detection mechanisms were not deemed mature enough' to meet the Art. 50(2) quality requirements; access to results may be restricted to verified expert users.

quote: Signatories will ensure that detection results indicate whether they are based on a metadata marking, a watermark marking, forensic detection or other techniques, to the extent technically feasible.
holder: Signatories who are providers of generative AI systems
obligation: mandatory under the Code for Signatories ('will'); adherence to the Code is voluntary
if_not_met: not stated (compliance monitored by competent market surveillance authorities; no consequence stated)
note: Results must be 'clear  and easily comprehensible to natural persons' and include further information carried in the watermark or metadata; may show the share of content generated and where changes are; tiered access encouraged. Human interfaces must be accessible under the European Accessibility Act and the Web Accessibility Directive ('will', where applicable); ETSI EN 301 549 and WCAG 2.1 AA encouraged. Output of a check (Delivery); also bears on Accountability (information to natural persons under Art. 50(5)).

quote: There is no quantitative evaluation metric linked to this Measure; instead, it requires a user-based assessment of the detection functionality.
holder: Signatories who are providers of generative AI systems
obligation: mandatory under the Code for Signatories ('will'); adherence voluntary; assessment method not prescribed
if_not_met: not stated (compliance monitored by competent market surveillance authorities; no consequence stated)
note: Effectiveness check. Signatories 'will implement' fit-for-purpose solutions; they are effective 'when natural persons can access and understand the meaning of the detection results'. Method: user-based assessment; Signatories 'may conduct relevant panel studies'. No quantitative metric. Encouraged to publish display specifications for downstream stakeholders. Trigger (Commitment 3 preamble): before placing on the market or putting into service, and throughout the lifecycle, through the Commitment 4 processes.

quote: Signatories will measure the accuracy of the detection of AI-generated or manipulated content by using relevant metrics for the type of markings, such as the error rate of the detection.
holder: Signatories who are providers of generative AI systems
obligation: mandatory under the Code for Signatories ('will'); adherence to the Code is voluntary
if_not_met: not stated (compliance monitored by competent market surveillance authorities; no consequence stated)
note: Reliability check. Metric: accuracy, e.g. error rate (Glossary: the false positive rate can undermine trust). Compared against: a variety of samples including the provider's own marked content and other content, possibly from other AI systems. Assessment data 'shall, to the extent possible, not have been used during the training and development'. Measurements 'performed and reported' across content length, size, diversity and semantics. Trigger: before market placement and throughout the lifecycle (Commitment 3 preamble). To whom results are reported is not stated.

quote: Prior to placing their generative AI system on the market or putting it into service, and regularly thereafter, Signatories will test the compliance of their marking and detection solutions
holder: Signatories who are providers of generative AI systems
obligation: mandatory under the Code for Signatories ('will'); adherence to the Code is voluntary
if_not_met: not stated (compliance monitored by competent market surveillance authorities; no consequence stated)
note: Testing. Trigger: before placing on the market or putting into service, then regularly. Conditions 'representative of real-world use'. Compared against: Commitment 3 requirements and the measures of Section 1. Benchmarks: until methods endorsed by the AI Office emerge, Signatories 'will test and report on the performances of their solution according to internal benchmarks and industry best practices'. Optional: independent experts, red teaming, testing in AI regulatory sandboxes (Art. 57 AI Act). Commitment 3 preamble: Signatories commit to assess and demonstrate compliance before market placement 'and throughout its lifecycle'. To whom reports go is not stated.

quote: Signatories will monitor any substantiated compliance shortcomings identified internally or reported by relevant third parties and implement appropriate follow-up corrective actions.
holder: Signatories who are providers of generative AI systems
obligation: mandatory under the Code for Signatories ('will'); adherence to the Code is voluntary
if_not_met: not stated (compliance monitored by competent market surveillance authorities; no consequence stated)
note: Ongoing monitoring and correction. Third-party reports could also be read as an Accountability complaint route, but no channel is specified for Section 1. Trigger: ongoing.

quote: Signatories will put in place or maintain a process to ensure and verify that the design and placement specifications are implemented properly to mitigate risks of non-labelled or incorrectly labelled content.
holder: Signatories who are deployers of AI systems generating deep fakes or published text
obligation: mandatory under the Code ('will') 'where appropriate and particularly in cases of regular use'; adherence voluntary
if_not_met: not stated (compliance monitored by competent market surveillance authorities; no consequence stated)
note: Check. Trigger: where appropriate, particularly with regular use of AI to create deep fakes or published text; ongoing [inference]. Compared against: the design and placement specifications. Metric: not stated. Measure 2.3: 'Signatories will support the effective implementation of the design and placement specifications through internal review and external feedback'.

quote: commit to establish, adapt, or maintain appropriate policies for human review or editorial control prior to publication and that a natural or legal person holds editorial responsibility for the publication.
holder: Signatories who are deployers publishing AI-generated text on matters of public interest, other than media service providers
obligation: commitment under the Code ('commit to'), proportionate to the deployer's size and resources
if_not_met: not stated; [inference] without human review and editorial responsibility, the text must be labelled
note: Human review of AI-generated text before publication. Trigger: prior to publication. Policies must at least identify the person with editorial responsibility and give an overview of organisational measures and human resources (coded Delivery/Resources); no need to document individual reviews. Also coded Decision-making/Design and Accountability/Design.

quote: Signatories will implement a multi -layered marking approach to ensure that the outputs of their generative AI systems are marked with at least two layers of machine-readable marking
holder: Signatories who are providers of generative AI systems
obligation: mandatory under the Code for Signatories ('will'); adherence to the Code is voluntary
if_not_met: not stated (compliance monitored by competent market surveillance authorities; no consequence stated)
note: Marking = recording AI origin in outputs. Trigger: every output generated or manipulated [inference: at generation]. Compared against: Art. 50(2) effectiveness, reliability, robustness and interoperability, via Commitment 3. Exceptions: one layer suffices for generative AI 'embedded in physical products' in a closed, mainly instructive environment that prevents export; free-form text needs only the watermark layer. Future alternative techniques must be proven to MSAs (Accountability/Design). Marking may be done upstream or by third parties (Coordination/Design, Accountability/Design).

quote: Signatories will record information in the metadata on whether the content is AI-generated or manipulated. All recorded information will be digitally signed and time -stamped
holder: Signatories who are providers of generative AI systems
obligation: mandatory under the Code for Signatories ('will'); adherence to the Code is voluntary
if_not_met: not stated (compliance monitored by competent market surveillance authorities; no consequence stated)
note: Recording in metadata where the format supports it (audio, image, video, containerised text). Signing certificates and private keys to be secured, except where the deployment context does not allow, e.g. local deployment. Richer metadata encouraged (Measure 1.3: system name, provider name, timestamp; may add model identifier and version) without privacy- or business-sensitive information.

quote: Signatories will ensure that AI -generated or manipulated content  is marked with an imperceptible watermark, with the exception of very short text.
holder: Signatories who are providers of generative AI systems
obligation: mandatory under the Code for Signatories ('will'); adherence to the Code is voluntary
if_not_met: not stated (compliance monitored by competent market surveillance authorities; no consequence stated)
note: Exception: very short text, under 200 tokens (Glossary). Free-form text over 200 tokens must still be watermarked, though less reliably; access to its detection may be restricted to verified expert users. The watermark is to be 'difficult for it to be separated from the content' and complements the signed metadata. Model-level watermarking by model providers coded Delivery/Resources.

quote: Signatories will, to the extent technically feasible and recognisable as per open standards, retain, and abstain from intentionally altering or removing, existing metadata markings, where such content is used as input
holder: Signatories who are providers of generative AI systems
obligation: mandatory under the Code for Signatories ('will', 'best efforts'); adherence to the Code is voluntary
if_not_met: not stated (compliance monitored by competent market surveillance authorities; no consequence stated)
note: Exceptions: good-faith legitimate processing, e.g. security audits and research. Also: 'Signatories will neither place or make available on the market , nor promote or advertise the use of tools whose purpose is to circumvent the machine -readable markings'. Signatories that run platforms or search engines are encouraged to preserve markings. No responsibility for third-party markings. Terms-of-use prohibition coded Coordination/Design.

quote: Signatories will make available a detection solution, composed of one or more detection mechanisms, to enable deployers, users of their generative AI system, third-party integrators, end-users exposed to the content, and other legitimate parties
holder: Signatories who are providers of generative AI systems
obligation: mandatory under the Code for Signatories ('will'); adherence to the Code is voluntary
if_not_met: not stated (compliance monitored by competent market surveillance authorities; no consequence stated)
note: Legitimate parties include 'competent authorities, independent researchers, civil society and media organisations'. Edge case: detection lets public bodies check whether incoming content is AI-generated by others. Available as public specification, software or API (2.1.1); free of charge (coded Delivery/Resources for free access to authorities); results presented clearly, stating the basis (metadata, watermark, forensic) and accessible to persons with disabilities (Measure 2.3); downloadable signed result (2.1.2).
basis: AI pass B; different cell in pass A

quote: Signatories will ensure that adversarial robustness of their marking and detection solutions is assessed in terms of resilience to malicious behaviour such as copying, removal, regeneration, and modification attacks on the markings.
holder: Signatories who are providers of generative AI systems
obligation: mandatory under the Code for Signatories ('will'); adherence to the Code is voluntary
if_not_met: not stated (compliance monitored by competent market surveillance authorities; no consequence stated)
note: Robustness check in two parts. (1) Typical processing: in-place changes (e.g. compression, screenshots, lexical substitution, homoglyphs); desynchronisation (e.g. cropping, paraphrasing, translation cycles); the analogue hole (e.g. print-and-scan); localised changes such as blurred faces. (2) Adversarial robustness, measured by ability to verify marking integrity; threats chosen as plausible real-world threats for the content type, mark type and deployment context. Metric: same as reliability (Measure 3.2). Encouraged: rate limits, frequent threat-assessment updates. Does not apply to systems subject only to one layer of metadata marking.

quote: Signatories will document, implement, and keep up to date, in line with the state of the art, a compliance process that describes at a high -level how they have implemented the different  Measures
holder: Signatories who are providers of generative AI systems
obligation: mandatory under the Code for Signatories ('will'), proportionate for SMEs and SMCs; adherence voluntary
if_not_met: not stated (compliance monitored by competent market surveillance authorities; no consequence stated)
note: Recording. May use existing processes and documentation, and documentation from third parties or model providers 'without prejudice to the ultimate responsibility of the Signatory'; reliance on open-source standards and tools is documented. Provided to MSAs on reasoned request (Accountability/Design, Measure 4.4).

quote: Signatories will put in place or maintain appropriate internal compliance processes and documentation that specifies how they implement the disclosure obligations using the icon or equivalent label.
holder: Signatories who are deployers of AI systems generating deep fakes or published text
obligation: mandatory under the Code ('will'), proportionate to size, resources and capacities; adherence voluntary
if_not_met: not stated (compliance monitored by competent market surveillance authorities; no consequence stated)
note: Recording. Documentation may include 'representative, concrete and real examples of how disclosures are implemented in practice'. Media service providers (Art. 2(2) Regulation (EU) 2024/1083) may comply through existing procedures and professional standards if those comply.

quote: All other Signatories, including those  without such review or editorial procedures , commit to establish, adapt, or maintain appropriate policies for human review or editorial control prior to publication
holder: Signatories (deployers) other than media service providers already subject to editorial standards
obligation: commitment under the Code for Signatories other than media service providers (mandatory for Signatories); adherence voluntary
note: Human review of outputs before publication. Trigger: prior to publication. Compared against: not stated. Policies 'may rely on existing processes, will be proportionate to the deployer’s size and resources', and include (a) the person with editorial responsibility and (b) an overview of organisational measures and human resources; 'This does not entail having to document individual instances of human review'. Media service providers (Art. 2(2) Regulation (EU) 2024/1083) 'may rely on the exception' through existing editorial procedures. [Inference: this is the route by which AI-generated text on matters of public interest is taken out of the labelling duty; text without it counts as 'published text' and must be labelled.] Directly relevant to public bodies using AI to draft public information [inference]. Also coded Decision-making/Design, Accountability/Design and Delivery/Resources.

quote: Signatories may implement as an optional supplementary measure fingerprinting or logging solutions for AI -generated or manipulated
holder: Signatories who are providers of generative AI systems
obligation: optional ('may'); safeguards are mandatory ('will') if the option is used
note: Quote breaks at a page boundary; the text continues 'content which allow for checking whether content has been generated or manipulated by their AI system'. 'relying on fingerprinting or logging alone is not considered sufficient'. If implemented, Signatories 'will ensure that it is limited to the output data', privacy-preserving and respecting media freedom and journalistic source protection. It 'shall in no way be interpreted as creating a general commitment to log, monitor, or retain prompts'. Deployers' control over logging coded Decision-making/Design.

quote: national strategies should include proportionate but robust monitoring mechanisms  – as also highlighted by the framework – operating both at the national level and within individual administrations.
note: Monitoring. Trigger: 'should begin with assessing existing needs', then ongoing. Monitors 'the pace of AI adoption but also public value creation, effectiveness, risk management, compliance with applicable rules ( e.g. the AI Act) and the readiness of the organisation'. Compares against 'Clear and measurable objectives'. Metric: not stated.

quote: Mechanisms to validate pilot outcomes and enable replication are essential to ensure that successful pilots evolve into sustainable and interoperable solutions.
note: Validation of pilots. Nearest actor: public administrations. Trigger: end of a pilot, before scaling. Comparator and metric: not stated.

quote: These needs should be carefully assessed, with a focus on public value creation (Chen et al., 2023; van Noordt et al., 2023), trustworthiness and people-centric design
note: Needs assessment. Nearest named actor: public administrations. Trigger: before adoption ('Effective AI adoption begins with identifying a clear real-world need and defining the problem to be addressed'). Compares against: public value, trustworthiness, people-centric design. Metric: not stated.

quote: Before committing to any AI initiative, administrations might take stock of their current state across the technological, organisational and contextual dimensions detailed in Section 3.3.
note: Readiness assessment. Trigger: before committing to any AI initiative. Compares against the enabling factors in Section 3.3 (Box 2 offers them as a self-assessment baseline). Covers data governance, infrastructure, competencies, governance arrangements, wider environment. 'it should be proportionate to the scope of the intended AI initiative'. Metric: not stated.

quote: Throughout the adoption process – and after deployment – public administrations should monitor whether AI solutions are delivering the intended public value, tracking progress through key performance indicators, and deciding if adjustments are needed.
note: Monitoring. Trigger: ongoing, during adoption and after deployment. Compares against intended public value. Metric: key performance indicators (unspecified). Also coded as Decision-making/Design (deciding adjustments).

quote: AI solutions should therefore be designed and deployed in ways that promote fairness, accessibility and equal treatment, including for marginalised and underserved communities.
note: Nearest named actor: public administrations ('responsible for providing high-quality services to all citizens, ensuring inclusivity and non-discrimination'). Applies at design and deployment. No check, comparator or metric stated.

quote: Public administrations should assess environmental, social and economic sustainability across the life cycle of the AI solutions they are considering.
note: Assessment. Trigger: before adoption and across the life cycle. Compares 'expected benefits against potential environmental and societal costs'; may consider 'energy consumption, supply chains and long-term operational impacts'. Metric: not stated.

quote: administrations should take these principles into account when designing, procuring and adopting AI solutions
note: Sentence starts 'Public' on page 20 before footnote 9 and the page break. 'These principles' = guiding principles from the High-Level Expert Group on AI. The standard is set elsewhere (HLEG); applying it is delivery. Trigger: design, procurement, adoption.
basis: AI pass B; different cell in pass A

quote: Adopting AI responsibly requires a thorough assessment of enabling factors to ensure the accurate and effective adoption of AI and its ethical use and transparency.
note: Assessment against enabling factors (Figure 3: data, infrastructure, cybersecurity, interoperability, transparency registries; culture, governance, competences, procurement; user readiness, trusted suppliers, support systems). Trigger: before adoption [inference]. Metric: not stated.

quote: Adopting AI requires evaluating whether all essential technological components are in place and of sufficient quality to ensure that the system runs effectively and in a secure and sustainable way.
note: Technological readiness check. Trigger: before adoption. Compares against 'sufficient quality'; also 'a strategic assessment of the infrastructure’s criticality and accessibility', including 'cloud services, adherence to industry standards and technology provider choice'. Metric: not stated.

quote: Ensuring robust cybersecurity measures is critical to protect AI systems, underlying infrastructure and data from cyber threats.
note: Cybersecurity measures. Nearest named actor: public administrations. Trigger, comparator and metric: not stated.

quote: Public administrations should monitor and understand users’ readiness to interact with AI-based services and understand their concerns and expectations
note: Monitoring of users' readiness, concerns, expectations. Trigger and metric: not stated. Related: 'Engaging citizens and assessing their readiness to interact with AI solutions can help ensure responsible adoption.'

quote: As services become more automated, it is crucial to maintain transparency, human oversight and accountability, in order to uphold public trust and meet auditability standards, in accordance with the requirements of the AI Act.
note: Human oversight (human review of outputs). Nearest actor: public administrations providing people-centric services. Trigger: as services become automated. Comparator and metric: not stated. Also coded as Accountability/Design.

quote: public administrations might want to conduct a readiness assessment as a baseline and starting point for their AI adoption journey
note: Readiness assessment. Verb 'might want to'. Trigger: 'Before committing to any AI initiative'. Compared against: technological, organisational and contextual enabling factors of Section 3.3. Metric: not stated; 'should be proportionate to the scope of the intended AI initiative' (page 19). Resource: Box 2 enabling factors as self-assessment baseline (coded Delivery/Resources).

quote: They should be considered from the outset of any AI project and integrated into each stage of development and adoption.
note: 'They' = the three anchoring elements (public sector core mandate; EU regulatory framework on AI; EU vision and priorities). Trigger: from the outset and at each stage. Holder passive; nearest actor public administrations.

quote: t he AI Office is tasked with monitoring whether providers of general-purpose AI models effectively comply with their obligations under the AI Act

quote: (ii) conduct evaluations of general-purpose AI models (Article 92  AI Act )

quote: The copyright policy required under Article 53(1), point (c), AI Act must be applied throughout the  entire lifecycle of each of the provider’s relevant models.
if_not_met: not stated in passage; Commission powers in para (103)
note: Includes 'identifying and complying with a reservation of rights expressed under Article 4(3) of Directive (EU) 2019/790' (para (72)). Not exempt for open source (para (72)). One policy may cover all models. Legacy models: para (108).

quote: The systemic risk assessment and mitigation required under Article 55(1) AI Act must be carried out continuously for each model  throughout its entire lifecycle.
holder: Providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk

note: Trigger: continuous, plus 'more comprehensive and thorough measures at regular intervals and before key decisions  in the lifecycle'. Standard: 'effective, adequate, and proportionate to the systemic risks'. Compares against systemic risks (Art. 3(65), para (24)). Metric: not stated. Governance mitigations also lifecycle-wide.

quote: providers should estimate the cumulative amount of training compute that they will use before starting this run

note: Trigger: before the large pre-training run, then 'closely monitor their  actual and expected compute usage over the course of training  and throughout the model’s entire lifecycle'. Compares against the Art. 51(2) threshold (10^25 FLOP). Metric: FLOP, within 30% (para (120)). Also coded as Accountability/Design (notification).

quote: These include conducting model evaluations, reporting serious incidents , and ensuring an adequate level o f cybersecurity protection.
holder: Providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk

note: Model evaluations (testing) and cybersecurity. Trigger and metric for evaluations: not stated. Cybersecurity per para (21): 'for the model and its physical infrastructure, if appropriate, along the entire model lifecycle' (recital 115). Serious incidents coded separately.

quote: the documentation required by Article 53(1), points (a) and (b) , AI Act is limited to information on the modification
holder: Downstream modifiers who become providers of a general-purpose AI model
if_not_met: not stated in passage; Commission powers in para (103)
note: Copyright policy and training summary 'are limited to the data used as part of the modification'. Must also comply with Art. 54 (para (66)).

quote: for instance by carrying out a gap analysis that compares the measures they have implemented with the measures set out by a code of practice that is assessed as adequate

note: Check: compares the provider's measures against those of an adequate code of practice. Trigger and metric: not stated. Also coded as Accountability/Design.

note: Human review of AI screening of candidates. Also coded Decision-making/Design (final decision with selection panels).

quote: further developing the directorate’s prompt library, with appropriate quality controls and documentation.

note: Assessment. Trigger: systems in use and planned. Compared against: risk-based approach and operational guidelines. Metric: not stated.

note: Human review of outputs for intellectual property. Verb 'should always'. Trigger: the outputs (each output, [inference]).
