obligation: n/a (provided); establishment described as a duty on Member States ('should ensure')
note: A supervised testing environment before market or service; may be joint with other Member States, and physical, digital or hybrid. Serves testing and compliance (Delivery). Cross-ref Recitals (139)-(140).

quote: Establishing authorities should also ensure that the AI regulatory sandboxes have the adequate resources for their functioning, including financial and human resources.
obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital, 'should also ensure'); required of establishing authorities
note: Money and staff for sandboxes; serves the sandbox entry (Recital 138).

quote: This Regulation should provide the legal basis for the providers and prospective providers in the AI regulatory sandbox to use personal data collected for other purposes for developing certain AI systems in the public interest
holder: the providers and prospective providers in the AI regulatory sandbox
obligation: n/a (provided); legal basis under specified conditions
note: Data access as a resource, provided by the Regulation itself, for public-interest AI. Does not provide a basis under Art. 22(2)(b) GDPR or Art. 24(2)(b) EUDPR; other data protection duties remain.

quote: Member States should utilise existing channels and where appropriate, establish new dedicated channels for communication with SMEs, including start-ups, deployers, other innovators and, as appropriate, local public authorities, to support SMEs throughout their development path by providing guidance
note: Guidance and query-answering channels; named recipients include deployers and local public authorities. Channels 'should work together' for homogeneous guidance.
basis: AI pass A; different cell in pass B

quote: the Commission should provide standardised templates for the areas covered by this Regulation, upon request of the Board.
obligation: n/a (provided); recital 'should', on request of the Board
note: Templates; framed as addressing SMEs' needs. Official offer.

quote: providing a single information platform with easy-to-use information with regards to this Regulation for all providers and deployers
note: Information platform for all providers and deployers (including public deployers [inference]), plus awareness campaigns. Official offer.

quote: the AI-on-demand platform, the European Digital Innovation Hubs and the testing and experimentation facilities established by the Commission and the Member States at Union or national level should contribute to the implementation of this Regulation.
holder: the AI-on-demand platform, the European Digital Innovation Hubs and the testing and experimentation facilities (established by the Commission and the Member States)
note: They 'are able to provide in particular technical and scientific support to providers and notified bodies'. Official offer; deployers are not named.

quote: The Commission should develop guidelines to specify the elements of the quality management system to be fulfilled in this simplified manner by microenterprises.
note: Microenterprises may fulfil QMS duty in a simplified manner; guidance serves the QMS requirement (recital (81)).

quote: the Commission facilitates, to the extent possible, access to testing and experimentation facilities to bodies, groups or laboratories established or accredited pursuant to any relevant Union harmonisation legislation
note: Serves conformity-assessment bodies (e.g. medical device expert panels and laboratories).

quote: the AI Office should be able to involve independent experts to carry out the evaluations on its behalf
note: Outside expertise serving the AI Office's evaluations of GPAI models (design entry: AI Office evaluations, also coded Accountability/Design). Provided to/available to a named actor (AI Office); not an offer to deployers.
basis: AI pass B; different cell in pass A

quote: The Commission may develop initiatives, including of a sectoral nature, to facilitate the lowering of technical barriers hindering cross-border exchange of data for AI development
note: Possible support on data access infrastructure and semantic and technical interoperability of data for AI development.

quote: Providers and deployers of AI systems shall take measures to ensure, to their best extent, a sufficient level of AI literacy of their staff and other persons dealing with the operation and use of AI systems on their behalf
holder: Providers and deployers of AI systems
obligation: statutory duty (best efforts: 'to their best extent'); required of holder
if_not_met: Not stated in Art. 4; Art. 4 is not among the provisions given a fine ceiling in Art. 99(3)-(4) (outside this part); Member States lay down penalty rules for infringements generally (Art. 99(1)).
note: Skills and training for staff operating or using AI, 'taking into account their technical knowledge, experience, education and training and the context'. Applies to all AI systems, not only high-risk. AI literacy defined in Art. 3(56). Serves all use and oversight duties.

quote: provision of information required pursuant to Article 13 and, where appropriate, training to deployers.
obligation: statutory duty (resource the provider must give deployers)
if_not_met: Not stated here. Breach of Art. 16(a): fines up to EUR 15 000 000 or 3% (Art. 99(4)(a), outside this part).
note: Training and information for deployers; serves deployer use and human oversight duties (Art. 26). 'due consideration' to the deployer's expected technical knowledge, experience, education, training and context of use.

quote: the providers of such systems may exceptionally process special categories of personal data, subject to appropriate safeguards for the fundamental rights and freedoms of natural persons
obligation: statutory power (permission to process data, under conditions)
note: Data resource for bias detection and correction (10(2)(f)-(g)). Conditions: not achievable with other data incl. synthetic/anonymised; re-use limits, pseudonymisation; access controls; no transfer; deletion once corrected or at end of retention; records state why strictly necessary.

quote: the Commission shall establish a simplified technical documentation form targeted at the needs of small and microenterprises
note: SMEs incl. start-ups may provide Annex IV elements in simplified form using it; 'Notified bodies shall accept the form'.

quote: High-risk AI systems shall be designed and developed in such a way as to ensure that their operation is sufficiently transparent to enable deployers to interpret a system’s output and use it appropriately.
if_not_met: Not stated here. Breach of Art. 16(a): fines up to EUR 15 000 000 or 3% (Art. 99(4)(a), outside this part).
note: Passive; nearest actor: provider. Transparency as a resource for deployers' interpretation and use (Art. 26(1), 14(4)(c)).

quote: High-risk AI systems shall be accompanied by instructions for use in an appropriate digital format or otherwise that include concise, complete, correct and clear information that is relevant, accessible and comprehensible to deployers.
if_not_met: Not stated here. Breach of Art. 16(a): fines up to EUR 15 000 000 or 3% (Art. 99(4)(a), outside this part).
note: Instructions for use are 'information provided by the provider' (Art. 3(15)). Serve deployer duties: use per instructions (26(1)), monitoring (26(5)), DPIA (26(9)), FRIA (27(1)(d)-(e)). Contents (13(3)): purpose, accuracy, risks, explainability features, group performance, input data specs, predetermined changes, oversight measures, resources and maintenance, log mechanisms.

quote: the level of accuracy, including its metrics, robustness and cybersecurity referred to in Article 15 against which the high-risk AI system has been tested and validated and which can be expected
if_not_met: Not stated here. Breach of Art. 16(a): fines up to EUR 15 000 000 or 3% (Art. 99(4)(a), outside this part).
note: Gives deployers the tested metric and expected level, and known circumstances affecting it. Art. 15(3): 'The levels of accuracy and the relevant accuracy metrics of high-risk AI systems shall be declared in the accompanying instructions of use.' 13(3)(b)(v): performance for specific persons or groups, when appropriate.

quote: AI literacy should equip providers, deployers and affected persons with the necessary notions to make informed decisions regarding AI systems.
note: Resource: skills and knowledge. Recipients named: providers, deployers and affected persons; who must provide it is not stated in this recital (nearest named actors: providers and deployers; operative duty appears to be Art. 4 [inference; not in this part]). Content includes 'the suitable ways in which to interpret the AI system’s output' (serves human review, Delivery) and informed decisions (also serves Decision-making).

quote: The European Artificial Intelligence Board (the ‘Board’) should support the Commission, to promote AI literacy tools, public awareness and understanding of the benefits, risks, safeguards, rights and obligations
holder: The European Artificial Intelligence Board (the ‘Board’); the Commission
note: Official offer of AI literacy tools and public awareness; serves the AI literacy entry (Recital 20, Delivery/Resources). Supporting role, not authority.

quote: the human oversight measures referred to in Article 14, including the technical measures put in place to facilitate the interpretation of the outputs of the high-risk AI systems by the deployers
if_not_met: not stated here; Art. 99(4)(a) (outside this part) via Art. 16(a)
note: Tools and information for deployers' human oversight (serves Art. 14 and Art. 26(2)).

quote: to remain aware of the possible tendency of automatically relying or over-relying on the output produced by a high-risk AI system (automation bias)
holder: not stated (passive: system 'shall be provided to the deployer'); beneficiaries: natural persons to whom human oversight is assigned
if_not_met: Not stated here. Breach of Art. 16(a): fines up to EUR 15 000 000 or 3% (Art. 99(4)(a), outside this part).
note: The system 'shall be provided to the deployer in such a way that natural persons to whom human oversight is assigned are enabled' to: (a) understand capacities and limitations and monitor operation, detecting 'anomalies, dysfunctions and unexpected performance'; (b) stay aware of automation bias, especially where outputs inform decisions by natural persons; (c) 'correctly interpret the high-risk AI system’s output'. Capability provided for overseers' human review.
basis: AI pass B; different cell in pass A

quote: the Commission shall, in cooperation with relevant stakeholders and organisations such as metrology and benchmarking authorities, encourage, as appropriate, the development of benchmarks and measurement methodologies
note: Measurement resources for accuracy and robustness (Art. 15(1)). The Commission encourages development; it does not itself set the benchmark here.

quote: The levels of accuracy and the relevant accuracy metrics of high-risk AI systems shall be declared in the accompanying instructions of use.
if_not_met: not stated here; Art. 99(4)(a) (outside this part) via Art. 16(a)
note: Information given to deployers to check performance against; see also Art. 13(3)(b)(ii).

quote: resource management, including security-of-supply related measures
if_not_met: Not stated here. Art. 16(c) breach: Art. 99(4)(a) (outside this part).
note: QMS element; serves the QMS and Section 2 compliance.

quote: make available the necessary information and provide the reasonably expected technical access and other assistance that are required for the fulfilment of the obligations set out in this Regulation
obligation: statutory duty (resource the initial provider must give the new provider)
note: Information and technical access for the new provider (e.g. a deployer that became provider under 25(1)), 'in particular regarding the compliance with the conformity assessment'. Also coded Coordination/Design.

quote: natural persons who have the necessary competence, training and authority, as well as the necessary support
if_not_met: Not stated here. Art. 99(4)(e) (outside this part).
note: Staff, skills, authority and support for human oversight, required of the deployer. Serves Art. 14 oversight and 26(5) monitoring. Also coded Decision-making/Design.

quote: The deployer may, in similar cases, rely on previously conducted fundamental rights impact assessments or existing impact assessments carried out by provider.
note: Existing assessments, incl. the provider's, as a resource for the FRIA.

quote: The AI Office shall develop a template for a questionnaire, including through an automated tool, to facilitate deployers in complying with their obligations under this Article in a simplified manner.
note: Serves the FRIA (27(1)) and the notification to the MSA (27(3)).

quote: The notified body shall have permanent availability of sufficient administrative, technical, legal and scientific personnel who possess experience and knowledge relating to the relevant types of AI systems, data and data computing
if_not_met: Not stated here. Art. 99(4)(f) (outside this part).
note: Also 'sufficient internal competences' to evaluate outsourced tasks; 31(2) organisational, quality management, resources and process requirements plus cybersecurity; 31(10) professional integrity and competence. Serves conformity assessment (Arts 34, 43).

quote: draw up, keep up-to-date and make available information and documentation to providers of AI systems who intend to integrate the general-purpose AI model into their AI systems
obligation: statutory duty (resource provided to downstream providers)
if_not_met: Not stated here. Fines under Art. 101 (outside this part; see Recital 169).
note: Must 'enable providers of AI systems to have a good understanding of the capabilities and limitations' and to comply; minimum Annex XII; subject to IP protection. [inference] Serves public bodies that build tools on GPAI models. Also connects model and system providers (Coordination).

quote: The AI Office shall encourage and facilitate the drawing up of codes of practice at Union level in order to contribute to the proper application of this Regulation
note: Codes of practice serve GPAI providers' compliance with Arts. 53 and 55 (53(4), 55(2)). AI Office and Board 'shall aim to ensure' codes cover those obligations incl. keeping information up to date, detail of the training summary, systemic risk identification and management (56(2)), with objectives, commitments and KPIs, taking account of 'all interested parties, including affected persons' (56(4)). 56(8): AI Office encourages review and adaptation and 'shall assist in the assessment of available standards'.
basis: AI pass B; different cell in pass A

quote: Member States shall ensure that their competent authorities establish at least one AI regulatory sandbox at national level, which shall be operational by 2 August 2026.
obligation: statutory duty (resource provided to providers and prospective providers)
note: Sandboxes support development, training, testing and validation before placing on market (57(5)). May be joint or via an existing sandbox with equivalent coverage; regional/local sandboxes allowed (57(2)). [inference] Usable by public bodies acting as providers.

quote: The Commission may provide technical support, advice and tools for the establishment and operation of AI regulatory sandboxes.
note: Support to national authorities running sandboxes.

quote: The European Data Protection Supervisor may also establish an AI regulatory sandbox for Union institutions, bodies, offices and agencies
note: Public-sector sandbox for EU bodies; EDPS may exercise NCA roles under Chapter VI.

quote: Member States shall ensure that the competent authorities referred to in paragraphs 1 and 2 allocate sufficient resources to comply with this Article effectively and in a timely manner.
note: Resources for running sandboxes.

quote: Competent authorities shall provide, as appropriate, guidance, supervision and support within the AI regulatory sandbox with a view to identifying risks, in particular to fundamental rights, health and safety, testing, mitigation measures
note: 57(7): also 'guidance on regulatory expectations and how to fulfil the requirements and obligations set out in this Regulation'.

quote: The competent authority shall also provide an exit report detailing the activities carried out in the sandbox and the related results and learning outcomes.
note: Also written proof of activities on request. Providers may use these to demonstrate compliance in conformity assessment or market surveillance; MSAs and notified bodies 'shall' take them positively into account.
basis: AI pass A; different cell in pass B

quote: and may ask them for support and guidance.
obligation: n/a (provided on request); statutory power to request
note: Support available to national competent authorities operating sandboxes, in which systems are developed and tested under supervision. Offered by named EU actors on request; no duty on the AI Office or Board to give it is stated.

quote: access to the AI regulatory sandboxes is free of charge for SMEs, including start-ups, without prejudice to exceptional costs that national competent authorities may recover in a fair and proportionate manner
note: Free access serves supervised development and testing in sandboxes (Art. 57). Holder inferred from the cost-recovery clause.

quote: that they facilitate providers and prospective providers, by means of the learning outcomes of the AI regulatory sandboxes, in complying with conformity assessment obligations under this Regulation
note: Serves conformity assessment and voluntary codes of conduct (Art. 95). Nearest named actors: national competent authorities operating sandboxes; the Commission sets the arrangements by implementing act.

quote: AI regulatory sandboxes facilitate the development of tools and infrastructure for testing, benchmarking, assessing and explaining dimensions of AI systems relevant for regulatory learning, such as accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity
note: Testing and benchmarking tools; also 'measures to mitigate risks to fundamental rights and society at large'. Serves testing and evaluation. Nearest named actors: national competent authorities; Commission via implementing acts.

quote: Prospective providers in the AI regulatory sandboxes, in particular SMEs and start-ups, shall be directed, where relevant, to pre-deployment services such as guidance on the implementation of this Regulation
note: Points to services: guidance, help with standardisation documents and certification, testing and experimentation facilities, European Digital Innovation Hubs, centres of excellence. Providers of these services not named; a referral, not an offer by a named actor. Nearest named actor: national competent authorities.

quote: personal data lawfully collected for other purposes may be processed solely for the purpose of developing, training and testing certain AI systems in the sandbox when all of the following conditions are met
holder: Prospective providers in the AI regulatory sandbox ('a public authority or another natural or legal person')
if_not_met: processing allowed only 'when all of the following conditions are met'
note: Resource: access to personal data. Only for AI 'developed for safeguarding substantial public interest by a public authority or another natural or legal person' in listed areas, incl. (v) 'efficiency and quality of public administration and public services'. Conditions coded separately: (c), (f), (i), (j). Art. 59(2): law-enforcement processing needs a specific Union or national legal basis.

quote: through persons who are suitably qualified in the relevant field and have the necessary capacity, training and authority to perform their tasks
holder: Provider or prospective provider; deployers or prospective deployers
obligation: statutory condition for testing (required of the holder)
note: Staff, training and authority required of the holders; serves oversight of testing (Delivery/Design, same point).

quote: provide SMEs, including start-ups, having a registered office or a branch in the Union, with priority access to the AI regulatory sandboxes
obligation: statutory duty (Member States); n/a (provided) for recipients
note: Access resource for supervised development and testing; subject to eligibility and selection criteria; does not preclude other SMEs.

quote: organise specific awareness raising and training activities on the application of this Regulation tailored to the needs of SMEs including start-ups, deployers and, as appropriate, local public authorities
obligation: statutory duty (Member States); n/a (provided) for recipients
note: Training provided by a named actor to deployers and local public authorities. Serves compliance with the Regulation generally [inference: including deployer obligations].

quote: utilise existing dedicated channels and where appropriate, establish new ones for communication with SMEs including start-ups, deployers, other innovators and, as appropriate, local public authorities to provide advice and respond to queries about the implementation of this Regulation
obligation: statutory duty (Member States); n/a (provided) for recipients
note: Advice offered by a named actor, including on sandbox participation. The channel is also a contact point [could be read as Coordination].
basis: AI pass A; different cell in pass B

quote: The specific interests and needs of the SME providers, including start-ups, shall be taken into account when setting the fees for conformity assessment under Article 43, reducing those fees proportionately to their size
note: Reduced fees serve conformity assessment. Passive; whoever sets the fees is not named (nearest: notified bodies or Member States [inference]).

quote: provide standardised templates for areas covered by this Regulation, as specified by the Board in its request
note: Templates; content set by the Board's request.

quote: develop and maintain a single information platform providing easy to use information in relation to this Regulation for all operators across the Union
note: Information resource for all operators, including public-sector deployers [inference].

quote: organise appropriate communication campaigns to raise awareness about the obligations arising from this Regulation
note: Awareness resource.

quote: the Commission shall develop guidelines on the elements of the quality management system which may be complied with in a simplified manner considering the needs of microenterprises
note: Guidance 'without affecting the level of protection or the need for compliance with the requirements in respect of high-risk AI systems'. Serves the quality management system (delivery).

quote: support the Commission in promoting AI literacy, public awareness and understanding of the benefits, risks, safeguards and rights and obligations in relation to the use of AI systems
note: AI literacy resource [inference: supports the AI literacy duty of providers and deployers set out earlier in the Act].

quote: facilitate the development of common criteria and a shared understanding among market operators and competent authorities of the relevant concepts provided for in this Regulation, including by contributing to the development of benchmarks
note: Shared criteria and benchmarks. Serves testing and evaluation.
basis: AI pass B; different cell in pass A

quote: contributing to the development of tools and methodologies for evaluating capabilities of general-purpose AI models and systems, including through benchmarks
note: Evaluation tools and benchmarks. Serves evaluation of general-purpose AI models. Also (v): 'contributing to the development of tools and templates'.
basis: AI pass B; different cell in pass A

quote: is aimed to serve as a preliminary guidance for deployers in this interim period before the AI Office provides a template.
holder: European Commission (these Guidelines); AI Office (template, forthcoming)
note: Resource: the FRIA guidance in para 375-376 is an official offer; the AI Office template is promised, not yet provided (para 370 also says the Commission will provide 'further guidance on the obligation under Article 27'). Serves the FRIA entries (Delivery/Design, para 368, 370, 375).

quote: the description of the technology underlying the system to explain its functioning (by referencing the available documentation provided by the provider and its name)
note: Information from the provider that the deployer uses in the FRIA. Fn 215: once high-risk rules apply, this can be done by reference to the system's EU database registration number. Serves the FRIA entries (Delivery/Design, para 375).

quote: The person in charge of human oversight should have sufficient ‘AI literacy, training and auth ority’216 to understand how the system functions and when it underperforms or malfunctions.
location: page 117 (printed p. 112), section 10.1.1, para 375 (human oversight measures)
holder: the person in charge of human oversight
note: Skills, training and authority for the overseer; who provides them is not stated (nearest: deployer). Serves the human-oversight entries (para 375, 407).

quote: The procedures should provide instruc tions on the deployment of the RBI system, clarify the role of a human agent in verifying and interpreting the output and provide training to operate the system.
location: page 117 (printed p. 112), section 10.1.1, para 375 (human oversight measures)
note: Resources: instructions, a defined human role, training. Required of the deployer. Serves the human-oversight procedures entry (Delivery/Design, para 375).
basis: AI pass A; different cell in pass B

quote: Article 4 AI Act prescribes AI literacy measures  for providers and users of AI systems to ensure ‘a sufficient level of AI literac y of their staff and other persons dealing with the operation and use of AI systems’
holder: providers and users of AI systems
note: Skills resource; serves the human verification entry (Art. 14(5)). Restates the AI Act ('users' is the document's word for deployers).

quote: It is also necessary to establish a workplace and organisation that counteracts the effects of automation bias, and av oids fostering the uncritical acceptance of the results
note: Organisational conditions for effective oversight; EDPB names time pressure, burdensome procedures and career effects as causes. The Commission adopts the EDPB view only as 'may apply'. Serves the human oversight entries.

quote: unless the system is tested in an AI regulatory sandbox or in accordance with the special regime for testing in real world conditions outside the sandbox, as provided for in Articles 60 and 61 AI Act.
note: Mention only, not an offer: AI regulatory sandboxes and the real-world testing regime set up by the AI Act. Who runs sandboxes is not stated here (nearest: national competent authorities under AI Act Art. 57 [inference, not in the passage]). Serves the Delivery/Design entry on real-world testing (para 32).

quote: provide appropriate information in the instructions of use for deployers and regarding the necessary human oversight.
holder: Providers of AI systems (required to supply); recipients: deployers
obligation: expected (non-binding); resource required of the provider
note: Information resource required of the provider to serve the deployer's lawful use and human oversight (Delivery/Design entries paras 14, 37, 40). Para 41: where prohibitions are linked to a very specific purpose (Art. 5(1)(d)-(h)), providers 'will have to rely on primarily providing appropriate instructions and information to the deployers and the required human oversight and restricting prohibited use of the system'.

quote: the European Data Protection Board has adopted a series o f guidelines (e.g. on the noti on of ‘profiling’,41 which is particularly relevant for the prohibition in Article 5(1)(d) AI Act
note: Pointer to another body's guidance for interpreting 'profiling' (also relevant to social scoring, para 154). Mention only. Serves assessment of whether a system falls under a prohibition.
basis: AI pass B; different cell in pass A

quote: For the interpretation of the concept of ‘material distortion  of behaviour ’, Union consumer protection law , in particular, Directive 2005/29/EC (Unfair Commercial Practices Directive or ‘UCPD’), may constitute a valid source of inspiration.
note: Mention: interpretive source the document points to for the market surveillance authorities' assessment (Delivery/Design entry, para 81), including the CJEU 'average consumer' benchmark. Fn 71 notes that in the UCPD Guidance the Commission advised authorities to 'make use of behavioural insights and other data'. Not an offer of a tool.

quote: adherence to professional due diligence practices and industry standards for the responsible development and use of safe and ethical AI systems and measures to mitigate the harms can help to pre-empt and mitigate unintended significant harms.
note: Mention only: no standard or standards body is named and nothing is offered. Serves the 'encouraged' measures entry (para 95).

quote: AI systems posing minimal to no risk are not regulated, but providers and deployers may voluntarily adhere to voluntary codes of conduct.
holder: Providers and deployers of AI systems posing minimal to no risk
note: Mention only: voluntary codes of conduct under AI Act Art. 95; who drafts or offers them is not stated here. Part of the document's summary of the AI Act's four risk categories; the document does not offer a code itself.

quote: They should serve as practical guidance to assist competent authorities under the AI Act in their enforcement activities, as well as providers and deployers of AI systems in ensuring compliance with their obligations under the AI Act
holder: European Commission (provider of the guidance); recipients: providers and deployers of AI systems
note: Resource provided by a named actor (Commission) to serve providers' and deployers' compliance with Art. 5 (the Delivery and Decision-making design entries in this file). Providers and deployers include public authorities (paras 16-17). Para 7: examples in the Guidelines are 'merely indicative'. Also coded as Accountability/Resources (same passage, for competent authorities) and Coordination/Resources.

quote: These requirements include that the human oversight must be assigned to persons with the necessary competence, training and authority who should be able to properly understand the capabilities and limitations of the AI system
note: Passive; nearest named actor is the deployer (Art. 26 cited), i.e. law enforcement authorities using non-prohibited crime-risk tools. Resource required of the holder: staff with competence, training and authority. Serves the human-assessment entry (Delivery/Design, para 204). The 'authority' element is also coded as Decision-making/Resources.

quote: Those persons should have clear procedures, training and the necessary competence and authority to meaningfully assess the outputs of the AI system .
obligation: recommended ('should'); non-binding interpretation of a statutory duty
note: Resources: procedures, training, competence, authority. Who provides them is not stated (nearest: deployer). Serves the human-assessment entry (Delivery/Design, para 204).

quote: Such safeguards could include, for example, prior written and motivated expert opinion relating to t he specific use case.
obligation: suggested ('could include'); required of the holder if adopted
note: Outside expert support, to be obtained by the deployer (not provided by any named actor). Serves the necessity safeguard (Delivery/Design, para 259).

quote: Public institutions need to have civil servants with the right capacities and skills to develop and/or use AI
obligation: required of holder ('need to have'), non-binding
note: Skills required of the holder to develop and/or use AI. The sentence sits under a heading that describes a theme in national strategies, but is itself normative. Serves delivery generally, not a specific check. See also the section 2.1.6 entries on internal capacity.

quote: the work of the ISO (International Organization for Standardization) on Guidelines on the testing of AI-based systems
note: Footnote to the common-testing-criteria action. Mention ('See, for example'), not an official offer.

quote: The Digital Europe Programme ,53 as well as the EU Recovery and Resilience Facility (RRF)54 programme include funding opportunities dedicated to AI for the public sector.
holder: European Union (Digital Europe Programme; Recovery and Resilience Facility)
note: Money for 'designing, testing and experimenting with new innovative AI solutions'. Footnote 54: 20% of the EUR 672.5 billion RRF goes to the digital target. Serves adoption generally, not a specific check.

quote: the one developed by the ECP Platform for the Information Society in the Netherlands90
holder: ECP Platform for the Information Society (Netherlands)
note: Frameworks should 'take into account emerging impact assessment frameworks'. Annex 2: 'AI Impact Assessment & Code of Conduct'. Mention only.

quote: Citizen Generated Data approaches, being an established practice of public engagement for the management of common good, can be directly deployed as an important contribu tion to ex ante and ex post impact assessment exercises
note: Citizen data as input to ex ante and ex post impact assessments. Refers to Commission Staff Working Document SWD(2020) 149, Best Practices in Citizen Science for Environmental Monitoring (mention).

quote: make sure that civil servants can work with the procured AI solutions.
holder: the public sector (in countries with private sector-led strategies)
obligation: recommended (hedged: 'it may still be very much required to')
note: Required of the holder: the skills civil servants need to operate procured AI solutions. Serves operation of the tool [inference]. The adjacent bullets are coded as Decision-making/Resources and Coordination/Resources.

quote: the need to collect and scrutinise both good and bad practices in order to acquire experience and identify the necessary validation tools, methodologies and relevant processes
note: Required of the holder (not stated): validation tools, methods and processes, drawn from good and bad practice. Serves the validation of AI applications, which is not otherwise specified.
basis: AI pass A; different cell in pass B

quote: There is a strong need to promote the internal capacity of public administrations in terms of organisational, structural, human and financial resources, to develop, experiment, implement and monitor AI within organisational processes.
note: Resources named: organisational, structural, human and financial. They serve development, experimentation, implementation and monitoring of AI by public administrations. Provider not stated.

quote: These bodies could also provide experimentation facilities and training opportunities, and represent an ideal environment for deploying regulatory sandboxing approaches.
note: EDIHs could serve as AI champions, 'focusing on the provision of support specifically to the public sector'. Resources: experimentation facilities, training and an environment for regulatory sandboxing. Serves testing and experimentation (Delivery). Footnote 47 points to the EDIH network on the Commission's digital-strategy site. This is a suggestion in the handbook, not an offer made by the EDIHs.

quote: The development of dedicated capacity-building programmes  would grant an adequate level of independence and higher capability to create relevant solutions for public administrations’ specific needs.
note: Resource: skills and training. Serves the development and adoption of AI by public administrations. Rationale: without internal skills, public administrations 'may become too dependent on external suppliers and on proprietary technologies'. The text notes 'Capacity-building programmes are being considered Europe-wide.' [scope doubt] Concerns capacity to adopt AI, not a check.

quote: developing “train the trainers” schemes within national training plans for civil servants engaged in both the commissioning of and/or direc t development of AI solutions
obligation: suggested option ('could be done, for example')
note: Training for civil servants who commission (procure) or develop AI. Serves procurement (Coordination) and development (Delivery). Holder not stated; nearest: the national authorities responsible for training plans.

quote: According to the e xperience of the EU’s Interoperability Academy 49 that could act as springboard and as an initial reference point
note: Pointed to as a 'springboard' and 'initial reference point' for capacity-building programmes 'aimed at different civil servant groups'. A mention, not an offer.

quote: A model of providing capacity-building that draws on a Europe-wide network could be the new Master in AI for public services (AI4Gov),50 launched in October 2021 by a consortium of universities across Member States.
holder: consortium of universities across Member States (Master in AI for public services, AI4Gov)
note: Cited as a model for capacity building and as a possible first step towards an EU-wide ecosystem. Non-state provider; a mention only. Mentioned again under Rec 3.1 (p. 37) as a springboard for a university alliance.

Beneficiaries (para 55): exposed persons and 'competent market surveillance authorities and other competent authorities, independent researchers, civil society organisations , media, trusted flaggers, fundamental rights defenders', platforms, rightsholders. quote: these Commission Guidelines are issued with the aim to serve as practical guidance to assist competent authorities , as well as providers and deployers of AI systems

obligation: n/a (provided by a non-state actor, where offered)
note: Labelling tools offered by platforms; deployers 'can rely on such tools' within that platform, 'without prejudice to the responsibility of the deployers'. Not an official offer; conditional mention.

holder: Upstream model provider or a third party providing a marking solution

note: Marking tools from the value chain, serving the Art. 50(2) marking duty. Only a mention, not an official offer. Reliance is 'without prejudice to the responsibility of the provider of the AI system to demonstrate compliance' (coded as Accountability/Design).
